injuries.name: Andrew Wingard
injuries.headline: Wingard made 10 tackles (one solo) in the Cardinals' 36-30 loss to the 49ers on Sunday.
injuries.notes: Wingard led the Cardinals in tackles Sunday, beating out Jack Gibbens' eight. The free safety played all 54 of the team's defensive snaps in the close loss, and he's up to 22 tackles (nine solo) with an interception and a forced fumble through the first three games of the season.

injuries.name: Dadrion Taylor-Demerson
injuries.headline: Taylor-Demerson (back) didn't participate in Wednesday's practice, Tyler Drake of ArizonaSports.com reports.
injuries.notes: Taylor-Demerson is still dealing with the back injury that forced him to miss the Week 3 loss to the Commanders. He will likely have to participate in either Thursday or Friday's practice session in order to have a chance to play in Sunday's matchup against the Giants.

injuries.name: Mack Wilson Sr.
injuries.headline: Wilson (thumb) was a limited participant in Arizona's practice Wednesday, Tyler Drake of ArizonaSports.com reports.
injuries.notes: Wilson popped up on the injury report Wednesday due to a thumb issue, putting his status for Sunday's matchup versus the Giants up in the air. If he ends up being unable to play, Cody Simon would be in line to start at middle linebacker.

injuries.headline: questionable
injuries.notes: questionable

injuries.name: Walter Nolen III
injuries.headline: questionable
injuries.notes: questionable

injuries.name: Hjalte Froholdt
injuries.headline: questionable
injuries.notes: questionable

injuries.name: Kendrick Bourne
injuries.headline: Bourne hauled in two passes on three targets for 22 yards during the Cardinals' 36-30 loss to the 49ers on Sunday.
injuries.notes: Bourne's first target of the game came early in the first quarter, but he wasn't looked at by Jacoby Brissett again until late in the fourth, when the duo connected on passes of 14 and eight yards on back-to-back plays to set up a one-yard touchdown run by the QB. Bourne played 48 of 87 offensive snaps (55.2 percent), which was third-most among Cardinals wide receivers behind Michael Wilson (81) and Marvin Harrison (67). Bourne is up to a 12-108-0 receiving line on 14 targets through three regular-season games, ahead of Harrison in target volume but well behind Wilson and Trey McBride. Up next is a Week 4 road tilt against the Giants this Sunday.

injuries.name: Tyler Allgeier
injuries.headline: Allgeier rushed twice for minus-1 yard and caught all four of his targets for 10 yards in the Cardinals' 36-30 loss to the 49ers on Sunday.
injuries.notes: Rookie first-round pick Jeremiyah Love worked as the clear lead back for the first time in his nascent career Sunday, relegating Allgeier to a minor role. Allgeier was thus limited to screen passes and checkdowns, catching everything thrown his way for minimal gains. It remains to be seen if Sunday's notable shift in workload will have carryover into a Week 4 road matchup against the Giants on Sunday.

injuries.name: Chad Ryland
injuries.headline: Ryland hit all three field-goal attempts and all three extra-point tries in Sunday's 36-30 loss to the 49ers.
injuries.notes: The kicker's longest field goal came from 49 yards out. Ryland has only missed one kick this year, a 54-yard field-goal try. The Cardinals have also shown some life on offense, so if they continue to move the ball, Ryland will remain a fantasy-relevant option.

injuries.name: Jacoby Brissett
injuries.headline: Brissett completed 38 of 52 passes for 280 yards with two touchdowns and no interceptions and rushed four times for four yards in the Cardinals' 36-30 loss to the 49ers on Sunday.
injuries.notes: Brissett put together one of his signature stat lines, parlaying massive passing volume into a solid yardage figure while remaining free of turnovers. The veteran signal-caller's pass-distribution profile also was on brand, as a whopping 28 of his pass attempts went in the direction of Michael Wilson (17 targets) and Trey McBride (11 targets). Brissett hit Wilson (five yards) and Jeremiyah Love (one yard) for his pair of touchdown passes, marking his first multi-TD tally of the season. Brissett is averaging a typically conservative 5.6 yards per attempt over his first three games, but he's thrown for over 275 yards twice to date heading into a Week 4 road matchup against the Giants next Sunday.

injuries.name: Marvin Harrison Jr.
injuries.headline: Harrison brought in three of five targets for 40 yards in the Cardinals' 36-30 loss to the 49ers on Sunday.
injuries.notes: Harrison was a distant third in receiving yards and tied for the same slotting in targets for the Cardinals on the afternoon. Despite the modest stat line across the board, Harrison's Sunday was certainly an improvement on his Week 2, when he was blanked and saw only one target. While his season-high reception, receiving yardage and target totals offer some solace, they fall short of satisfying frustrated fantasy managers who banked on a comeback campaign from the 2024 first-round pick. Harrison still appears to clearly be behind Michael Wilson and Trey McBride in the Cardinals' pass-catching hierarchy heading into a Week 4 road matchup against the Giants next Sunday.

injuries.name: Michael Wilson
injuries.headline: Wilson secured 11 of 17 targets for 89 yards and a touchdown in the Cardinals' 36-30 loss to the 49ers on Sunday.
injuries.notes: Wilson's afternoon was reminiscent of several of those in his 2025 campaign, as the veteran receiver garnered a bulk of Jacoby Brissett's attention in his short- and mid-range role while leading the team in receptions, receiving yards and targets. Marvin Harrison was a bit more involved Sunday with three catches for 40 yards on five targets, but it appears clear Wilson and Trey McBride have far and away the most chemistry with Brissett. Wilson will take an 18-163-1 line on 31 targets into a Week 4 road matchup against the Giants next Sunday.

injuries.name: Trey McBride
injuries.headline: McBride brought in nine of 11 targets for 75 yards in the Cardinals' 36-30 loss to the 49ers on Sunday.
injuries.notes: The talented tight end filled his usual workhorse role, finishing second in all of receptions, receiving yards and targets for the Cardinals behind Michael Wilson. The chemistry between McBride and Jacoby Brissett is extremely well-established after nearly a season working together, and the former already has a 26-211-2 line on 34 targets through only three games, recording at least eight receptions and logging no fewer than 10 targets in each contest. McBride will continue to offer perhaps the best floor of any player at his position in a Week 4 road matchup against the Giants next Sunday.

injuries.name: Jeremiyah Love
injuries.headline: Love rushed 21 times for 90 yards and brought in all five targets for 19 yards and a touchdown in the Cardinals' 36-30 loss to the 49ers on Sunday.
injuries.notes: Sunday may have marked the official crowning of Love as the Cardinals' unquestioned lead back, as he took 19 more carries than veteran backup Tyler Allgeier. All of Love's rush attempts, rushing yardage, receptions, receiving yardage and targets were new career-high figures for the rookie first-round pick, who also recorded his first receiving touchdown on a one-yard grab early in the fourth quarter. His draft pedigree and talent always made an ascension to the No. 1 role a matter of when and not if, and it will be interesting to see how the Notre Dame product fares in what could be a favorable Week 4 road matchup against the Giants next Sunday.

injuries.name: Max Melton
injuries.headline: Melton (toe) is active for Sunday's game against the 49ers, Darren Urban of the Cardinals' official site reports.
injuries.notes: Melton logged back-to-back limited practices to end Week 3 prep and draw the questionable tag, but he's been cleared to play Sunday after going through pregame warmups. The third-year pro has four tackles (two solo) and two pass defenses through two regular-season games.

injuries.name: Carson Beck
injuries.headline: Beck (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the emergency third quarterback against the 49ers on Sunday, Darren Urban of the Cardinals' official site reports.
injuries.notes: Beck will once again be the Cardinals' emergency QB3, meaning he won't be allowed to play Sunday unless both Jacoby Brissett and Gardner Minshew leave the game due to injury, illness or ejection.

injuries.name: Garrett Williams
injuries.headline: Williams (Achilles) does not carry an injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the 49ers, Darren Urban of the Cardinals' official site reports.
injuries.notes: Williams hasn't played yet this season while working his way back from a torn Achilles that he suffered in December of 2025. He was limited in practice Wednesday and Thursday. However, the 25-year-old was a full participant Friday. While Williams might be eased back into action for a week or two, he could be in line for as many snaps as he can handle, considering Will Johnson (neck) isn't expected to play again this season.

injuries.name: Starling Thomas V
injuries.headline: The Cardinals signed Thomas to the active roster from their practice squad Wednesday, Darren Urban of the team's official site reports.
injuries.notes: Thomas appeared in 17 games for Arizona during the 2024 campaign and logged 47 tackles (31 solo) and a forced fumble, but he missed the entirety of last season due to a torn ACL. With Will Johnson expected to miss the remainder of the season due to a neck injury, Thomas should provide additional depth at corner to help fill the void.

injuries.name: Will Johnson
injuries.headline: The Cardinals placed Johnson (neck) on injured reserve  Wednesday, Darren Urban of the team's official site reports.
injuries.notes: Johnson suffered a neck injury in the 31-7 loss to the Seahawks in Week 2. He was placed on injured reserve, so he is guaranteed to miss at least four games. However, the 23-year-old isn't expected to play again this season. If that's the case, he will finish the year with eight total tackles (three solo), one fumble recovery and one pass defended. Without Johnson, Garrett Williams (Achilles), who has yet to play this season, could take on a larger role upon his return. Max Melton (toe), Kei'Trel Clark and Starling Thomas, the latter who was promoted from the practice squad, may also be more involved.

injuries.name: Budda Baker
injuries.headline: Baker recorded 11 tackles (seven solo), including 1.0 sacks, and a pass breakup in Sunday's loss to the Seahawks.
injuries.notes: While Baker racked up a load of tackles, he was burned in coverage on Jaxon Smith-Njigba's 82-yard touchdown on a double-move in the first quarter. JSN made the entire Arizona secondary look foolish en route to 9-155-3 receiving line across 11 targets. Through two games this season, Baker has 16 tackles (11 solo), including 1.5 sacks, on 100 percent of the defensive snaps.

injuries.name: Isaac Seumalo
injuries.headline: Seumalo (shoulder) is active for Sunday's game against Seattle.
injuries.notes: Seumalo earned the questionable tag after ending the week with consecutive limited practices, and he's been cleared to play after going through pregame warmups. Hayden Conner will provide depth at left guard behind Seumalo.

injuries.name: Isaiah Adams
injuries.headline: Adams (knee) is active for Sunday's game against the Seahawks.
injuries.notes: Adams was limited in practice all week by a knee injury, but he's been cleared to play in Sunday's NFC West tilt. The third-year pro will start at right guard, with Jon Gaines providing depth at the position.

injuries.name: Gervon Dexter Sr.
injuries.headline: The Falcons signed Dexter to a four-year, $78 million contract extension Wednesday, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
injuries.notes: Atlanta acquired Dexter via a trade with the Bears back in August, and now the team will have him under contract through the 2030 season. Through three games in 2026, he has recorded seven tackles (two solo) including 0.5 sacks, and a pass defensed.

injuries.name: Samson Ebukam
injuries.headline: questionable
injuries.notes: questionable

injuries.name: Jessie Bates III
injuries.headline: Bates recorded four tackles (one solo) and one pass defense during the Falcons' 35-14 victory over the Packers on Thursday.
injuries.notes: Bates played 65 of 66 defensive snaps during Thursday's win, though interestingly, he has yet to play every single defensive snap through three regular-season games after doing so 16 times last year. The veteran safety leads the Falcons with 17 total tackles, with his eight solo stops being fourth-most on the team.

injuries.name: Xavier Watts
injuries.headline: Watts recorded five tackles (three solo) and one interception during Thursday's 35-14 win over the Packers.
injuries.notes: The Falcons put together an all-around performance for their first win of the season, with Watts putting the finishing touches on the victory by picking off Jordan Love within the last two minutes of the fourth quarter. Watts, a third-round selection of the Falcons in the 2025 NFL Draft, finished his rookie season with five interceptions, tied for second-most in the league behind Kevin Byard (seven). Watts has 16 tackles (10 solo), one interception and one forced fumble through the first three games of the 2026 regular season.

injuries.name: Austin Hooper
injuries.headline: Hooper caught both of his targets for 11 yards and a touchdown during Atlanta's 35-14 win over Green Bay on Thursday.
injuries.notes: Hooper was on the field for 16 of the Falcons' 71 offensive snaps, which was behind fellow tight ends Charlie Woerner (43), Kyle Pitts (42) and Nick Muse (17). However, unlike those three tight ends, Hooper contributed to the scoreboard by hauling in a five-yard touchdown pass from Michael Penix with just over a minute left to play in the second quarter. Hooper has a 4-31-1 receiving line (on six targets) through the first three games of the regular season.

injuries.name: Zachariah Branch
injuries.headline: Branch caught one pass on two targets for seven yards while logging an 18-yard punt return and a 22-yard kickoff return during the Falcons' 35-14 win over the Packers on Thursday.
injuries.notes: The rookie third-rounder has contributed on both special teams as a returner and on offense as a rotational pass catcher. He's up to three catches (on four targets) for 21 yards and 110 return yards through three regular-season games. His involvement on offense hasn't been as high as other rookie wide receivers, but the Falcons appear committed to using Branch in multiple ways to utilize his speed and explosiveness.

injuries.name: Olamide Zaccheaus
injuries.headline: Zaccheaus brought in both of his targets for nine yards and returned one punt for four yards during the Falcons' 35-14 win over the Packers on Thursday.
injuries.notes: Both of Zaccheaus' catches occurred in the second quarter on the same drive, which ended with a 44-yard field goal by Nick Folk. Zaccheaus is up to four catches (on six targets) for 17 yards through three regular-season games while operating as a depth option in the passing game, though Thursday's win may have been the start for a more explosive offense for the Falcons with Michael Penix under center, rather than Tua Tagovailoa, Cooper Rush (coach's decision) or Jack Strand (coach's decision). The Falcons will travel to New Orleans to face the Saints on Monday, Oct. 5.

injuries.name: Jahan Dotson
injuries.headline: Dotson caught one pass on three targets for 11 yards during the Falcons' 35-14 win over the Packers on Thursday.
injuries.notes: Dotson's three targets from Michael Penix were actually second-most on the Falcons behind Drake London (10), with Dotson finishing tied for the third-most receiving yards on the team. He's played over 60 percent of offensive snaps in each of the first three games of the regular season but has a 4-41-0 receiving line (on 11 targets) to show for it. That said, Dotson's scoring floor could steadily increase as the season progresses and Penix gets more reps under his belt. The Falcons will stay on the road for a Week 4 NFC South tilt against the Saints on Monday, Oct. 5.

injuries.name: Kyle Pitts Sr.
injuries.headline: Pitts secured one of two targets for five yards in the Falcons' 35-14 win over the Packers on Thursday.
injuries.notes: Pitts' slow start persisted Thursday despite Michael Penix making his season debut and taking the reins of the offense from the ineffective duo of Cooper Rush and Jack Strand. Pitts has managed just two receptions for 20 yards on six targets through three games, but given how sharp Penix looked right out of the gate Thursday, the duo is bound to start clicking in coming games as they've done previously.

injuries.name: Nick Folk
injuries.headline: Folk hit both field-goal attempts and all three extra-point tries in Thursday's 35-14 win over the Packers.
injuries.notes: The kicker did his job during the blowout win, with his longest field goal connecting from 44 yards out. Folk missed three field goals across Atlanta's first two games, both losses, but he bounced back Thursday night. If the Falcons can keep scoring, he is a viable fantasy option.

injuries.name: Brian Robinson Jr.
injuries.headline: Robinson rushed 10 times for 50 yards and a touchdown and returned two kickoffs for 54 yards in the Falcons' 35-14 win over the Packers on Thursday.
injuries.notes: Robinson's backfield mate Bijan Robinson and No. 1 receiver Drake London stole the show Thursday while accruing 194 yards apiece, but Brian had his own moment in the spotlight when he capped off a 10-play, 92-yard drive in the third quarter with a seven-yard touchdown run. Brian Robinson now has back-to-back games with double-digit carries and has at least 50 rushing yards in each, keeping him somewhat relevant in very deep formats heading into a Week 4 road matchup against the Saints on Monday, Oct. 5.

injuries.name: Michael Penix Jr.
injuries.headline: Penix completed 18 of 25 passes for 256 yards with one touchdown and one interception while rushing twice for minus-2 yards in the Falcons' 35-14 win over the Packers on Thursday. He also threw a two-point conversion pass.
injuries.notes: Playing in his first game since Week 11 of last season, Penix started off sluggishly Thursday before finding a rhythm and putting together a near-flawless performance. Penix threw his one interception four plays into the night on a pass intended for Jahan Dotson, but he went on to record only five more incompletions the rest of the way while connecting with Austin Hooper for a five-yard touchdown pass just before halftime. Penix's chemistry with Drake London also was in fine form over the last three quarters, and he hit his No. 1 target for gains of 68 and 40 yards in the fourth quarter to help close out the upset victory. Penix should only get more comfortable the further removed he is from the third ACL surgery of his playing career, and he'll look to carry over the considerable momentum from his season debut into a Week 4 road divisional showdown against the Saints on Monday, Oct. 5.

injuries.name: Drake London
injuries.headline: London secured nine of 10 targets for 194 yards in the Falcons' 35-14 win over the Packers on Thursday.
injuries.notes: London and Michael Penix got their first 2026 game together off to a very quiet start, but once the duo began clicking, they helped fuel the surprising road rout. Two of London's fourth-quarter catches accounted for 108 of his yards, the first a 68-yarder early in the period on which he appeared he could have scored but was caught from behind at the Packers' 16-yard line. London then struck again with just over five minutes remaining, recording a 40-yard grab where he ran away from a fallen defender to Green Bay's 13-yard line to set up the final touchdown of the night. The receiving yardage tally was a new career high for the 2022 first-round pick, while his nine receptions were his most since Week 9 of last season. London will take a 15-274-0 line into a Week 4 divisional road clash against the Saints on Monday, Oct. 5.

injuries.name: Bijan Robinson
injuries.headline: Robinson rushed 29 times for 194 yards and two touchdowns and brought in both targets for 19 yards in the Falcons' 35-14 win over the Packers on Thursday.
injuries.notes: Robinson's night on the ground was every bit as dominating as his final line suggests, as the star running back repeatedly ripped off chunk gains against an overwhelmed Packers defense. He got the night off on the right foot by netting 21 yards on the Falcons' first two plays, and he struck for his game-long 55-yard run on Atlanta's third possession to set himself up for a three-yard touchdown rush two plays later. The 2023 first-round pick went on to add a three-yard touchdown run to close out the scoring with just over three and a half minutes remaining, and he came just a yard short of equaling the career-high 195 rushing yards he hung on the Rams in Week 17 of last season. Robinson already has 543 rushing yards and three total touchdowns through three games heading into a Week 4 road matchup against the Saints on Monday, Oct. 5.

injuries.name: Billy Bowman Jr.
injuries.headline: Bowman (Achilles) is available for Thursday's game versus the Packers.
injuries.notes: Bowman sustained a season-ending Achilles injury ahead of the Week 12 meeting with the Saints during the 2025 campaign. It's unknown if the 23-year-old will be eased back into action. However, Bowman's return, even if it's in a limited capacity, couldn't come at a better time, considering A.J. Terrell (groin) was placed on injured reserve Tuesday. Bowman, No. 118 overall pick in the 2025 Draft, finished his inaugural NFL year with 26 total tackles (15 solo), including 1.5 sacks, one interception and one pass defended in six regular-season games.

injuries.name: Jawaan Taylor
injuries.headline: Taylor (ribs) was a full participant in Tuesday's practice, Tori McElhaney of the Falcons' official site reports.
injuries.notes: Taylor injured his ribs during the Falcons' 34-3 loss to the Panthers on Sunday. However, his full participation in Tuesday's practice means he'll start at right tackle against the Packers on Thursday.

injuries.name: Zach Harrison
injuries.headline: The Falcons signed Harrison to the active roster from their practice squad Tuesday, Tori McElhaney of the team's official site reports.
injuries.notes: Harrison will rejoin the active roster after having been waived in late August before catching on with the team's practice squad. With Da'Shawn Hand (quadriceps) on injured reserve, Harrison will likely serve as Atlanta's primary rotational defensive end behind LaCale London and Brandon Dorlus.

injuries.name: Nick Muse
injuries.headline: Muse (shoulder) was a full participant in Tuesday's practice, Tori McElhaney of the Falcons' official site reports.
injuries.notes: Muse popped up on Monday's estimated practice report due to a shoulder injury, but he was cleared to participate fully in Tuesday's practice and is on track to play against the Packers on Thursday. The fifth-year tight end has contributed on both offense as a blocker and on special teams, though he's yet to record a target through two regular-season games.

injuries.name: Brandon Dorlus
injuries.headline: Dorlus (thumb) was a full participant in Tuesday's practice, Tori McElhaney of the Falcons' official site reports.
injuries.notes: Dorlus injured his thumb during the Falcons' 34-3 loss to the Panthers on Sunday, but his full participation in Tuesday's practice indicates he'll be available for Thursday's road game against the Packers. The third-year pro has four tackles (three solo) through the first two games of the regular season, though he's yet to record a sack after posting 8.5 sacks across 15 regular-season games in 2025.

injuries.name: C.J. Henderson
injuries.headline: Henderson is expected to step into a starting role at cornerback in Week 3, Tori McElhaney of the Falcons' official website reports.
injuries.notes: Henderson has compiled five solo tackles and two passes defensed while playing 66 snaps on defense and 16 snaps with the special-teams unit over Atlanta's first two games of the season. The cornerback will now take over a starting role in the secondary after A.J. Terrell (groin) was placed on injured reserve Tuesday.

injuries.name: Chris Moore
injuries.headline: questionable
injuries.notes: questionable
injuries.vacated_opportunity_note: Expands to high-volume target progression and 2-WR/3-WR set route participation.

injuries.name: Lamar Jackson
injuries.headline: Jackson (back) is participating at the start of Thursday's practice, Cordell Woodland of 105.7 The Fan Baltimore Sports Radio reports.
injuries.notes: Jackson was deemed a limited participant Wednesday, when he missed the early part of practice before joining teammates later in the session. The star quarterback's presence at the start of Thursday's practice suggests Jackson is in position to log a full session Thursday, though confirmation on that front won't come until after the Ravens wrap up their practice. There has been on indication that Jackson's status for Sunday's home game against the Titans is in any doubt.
injuries.vacated_opportunity_note: Takes over first-team reps under center with full pass-funnel responsibility.

injuries.name: Jovaughn Gwyn
injuries.headline: Gwyn was diagnosed with a fractured fibula that will likely require surgery, Jamison Hensley of ESPN.com reports.
injuries.notes: The fourth-year center is expected to be sidelined for 2-to-3 months, though likely more if he ends up undergoing surgery. Backup center Ethan Pocic (knee) is also expected to miss significant time, and with Danny Pinter (knee) on injured reserve, that leaves rookie first-rounder Olaivavega Ioane as the starting center for the Ravens in Week 4 against the Titans.

injuries.name: Durham Smythe
injuries.headline: Smythe (heel) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice.
injuries.notes: Smythe likely suffered the heel injury during the Ravens' 34-31 win over the Cowboys in Rio. The tight end being a limited participant after recently sustaining the injury is a positive sign for his ability to suit up for Sunday's game against the Titans. Smythe will likely need to upgrade to a full participant by Friday's practice to dodge any injury designation ahead of Sunday's game.
injuries.vacated_opportunity_note: Assumes inline snaps and high-leverage red-zone target share.

injuries.name: Zay Flowers
injuries.headline: Flowers (hamstring) was limited in Wednesday's practice, Sam Cohn of The Baltimore Sun reports.
injuries.notes: Baltimore is continuing to exercise caution with its star receiver, who is working his way back to 100 percent from a hamstring injury. Flowers was effective in his return Sunday but logged only 21 (33 percent) offensive snaps. He didn't aggravate the injury Sunday, though his practice reps remain limited for now.

injuries.notes: questionable

injuries.name: Marlon Humphrey

injuries.notes: questionable

injuries.name: Trey Hendrickson
injuries.headline: questionable
injuries.notes: questionable

injuries.name: Roquan Smith
injuries.headline: Smith logged nine tackles (three solo), including 1.0 sacks, during the Ravens' 34-31 win over the Cowboys in Rio on Sunday.
injuries.notes: Smith played 100 percent of the Ravens' defensive snaps for the third straight game. The linebacker has yet to miss a defensive play and led the Ravens in tackles for the second time this season. Smith sacked quarterback Dak Prescott on third-and-goal in the first quarter for a loss of nine yards, leading to the Cowboys settling for a field goal on the team's opening drive.

injuries.name: Ronnie Stanley
injuries.headline: questionable
injuries.notes: questionable

injuries.name: Mark Andrews
injuries.headline: Andrews caught three of five targets for 24 yards during Sunday's 34-31 win over the Cowboys.
injuries.notes: Andrews was limited by a hand injury that he suffered in the second quarter, and he was on the field for only 33 of the team's 64 offensive snaps. The tight end has recorded at least three catches in each of the team's first three games, reeling in 13 of 18 targets for 122 yards so far this season. Andrews has yet to reach the end zone this year, and his next chance will come against the Titans in Week 4.

injuries.name: Ethan Pocic
injuries.headline: Pocic (knee) is set to miss significant time, Clifton Brown of the Ravens' official site reports.
injuries.notes: Pocic suffered a knee injury during the Ravens' Week 3 win over the Cowboys in Rio. Pocic's exit marks the third significant injury to a Ravens center, following Danny Pinter's torn patellar tendon in August and Jovaughn Gwyn's (ankle) injury in the Week 3 contest as well. With all three offensive linemen out for either the season or a large amount of time, Olaivavega Ioane is now set to man the position for Baltimore moving forward.

injuries.name: Tyler Loop
injuries.headline: Loop made both field-goal tries, including a 56-yard game-winning kick as time expired, and all four extra-point attempts in Sunday's 34-31 win over the Cowboys.
injuries.notes: Loop's kick flew just inside the left upright to lift the Ravens to victory. The kicker has missed just once in 2026 so far. As long as the Ravens keep scoring, the 2025 sixth-round pick will remain a strong fantasy play.

injuries.name: Rashod Bateman
injuries.headline: Bateman caught two of three targets for 37 yards in Sunday's 34-31 win over the Cowboys.
injuries.notes: Bateman finished second on the team in receiving yards behind Zay Flowers, who compiled 84 receiving yards in the latter's return from a one-game absence due to a hamstring injury. Bateman stepped up with seven catches for 88 yards and a touchdown while Flowers was sidelined in Week 2, but Flowers is the clear No. 1 option in Baltimore's wide receiver room, as Bateman was held without a catch when Flowers was active for the season opener. Up next for Bateman and the Ravens will be a Week 4 home game against the Titans.

injuries.name: Derrick Henry
injuries.headline: Henry rushed 26 times for 89 yards and two touchdowns while catching his lone target for no gain in Sunday's 34-31 win over the Cowboys.
injuries.notes: Henry scored a four-yard rushing touchdown in the first quarter and a three-yard rushing touchdown in the second quarter, but he was denied the hat trick in the fourth quarter, when a would-be third rushing score was ruled down at the 1-yard line on replay, and Henry's subsequent effort to get in on fourth down was stuffed. The 32-year-old Henry is showing no signs of slowing down, as he has six touchdowns through three games and is averaging just over 100 rushing yards per game heading into a Week 4 home game against the winless Titans.

injuries.name: Elijah Sarratt
injuries.headline: Sarratt (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against Dallas.
injuries.notes: Sarratt was available for the Week 2 loss to the Saints. However, with Zay Flowers (hamstring) cleared to suit up after missing the meeting with New Orleans, Sarratt will be inactive in Week 3.

injuries.name: Joe Fagnano
injuries.headline: Fagnano (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against Dallas but will be available as the team's emergency quarterback if needed.
injuries.notes: Fagnano was also the Ravens' emergency signal-caller for the first two games of the 2026 campaign. That trend will likely continue as long as Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley are available.

injuries.name: Teddye Buchanan
injuries.headline: Buchanan (knee) is expected to play in Sunday's game versus Dallas, Matt Zenitz of CBSSports.com reports.
injuries.notes: Buchanan suffered a torn ACL in December 2025 and has been working his way back since. He wasn't available for the Ravens' first two games of the 2026 campaign. However, after practicing in full Wednesday and Thursday, all signs are pointing toward Buchanan's season debut versus the Cowboys. The 2025 No. 129 overall pick finished his inaugural year by garnering 93 total tackles (49 solo), including 0.5 sacks, and one forced fumble.

injuries.name: Nnamdi Madubuike
injuries.headline: Madubuike (neck) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice.
injuries.notes: Madubuike has not practiced in full since suffering a significant neck injury in September of 2025. If he's able to participate in full throughout Week 3 prep, the defensive tackle could be cleared to make his season debut against the Cowboys in Rio on Sunday.

injuries.name: Kyle Hamilton
injuries.headline: Hamilton tallied 13 tackles (seven solo) during the Ravens' 24-17 loss to the Saints on Sunday.
injuries.notes: Hamilton played all but one of the Ravens' 68 defensive snaps during Sunday's loss, and he was much more involved in the second half, with 10 of his career-high 13 tackles coming over the final two quarters. It was the eighth time in Hamilton's career that he logged 10-plus combined tackles, the most recent time having been Week 12 of the 2025 season. He's up to 18 combined tackles through two regular-season games and is well on pace to reach 100-plus tackles for a third consecutive year. Hamilton figures to be busy Week 3 against Dak Prescott, CeeDee Lamb and the Cowboys' passing attack.

injuries.name: Devontez Walker
injuries.headline: Walker caught one of his two targets for 47 yards in Sunday's 24-17 loss to the Saints.
injuries.notes: Walker saw 17 of the Ravens' 58 offensive snaps in Sunday's contest. The wide receiver also saw eight special-teams snaps. Walker saw nearly half as many offensive snaps as LaJohntay Wester (31), even though Zay Flowers (hamstring) was unavailable. The 2024 fourth-rounder sees most of his usage as a deep threat, but he appears hard-pressed to expand his role much beyond that of an occasional deep threat.

injuries.name: C.J. Gardner-Johnson
injuries.headline: Gardner-Johnson logged five tackles (three solo) and two passes defensed, including one interception, in the Bills' 24-16 win over the Chargers on Sunday.
injuries.notes: Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert threw Gardner-Johnson a "meatball sub," according to commentator Tom Brady, early in the fourth quarter of Sunday's game at the Bills' one-yard line. The pick resulted in the Bills taking a lead for the first time in an eventual 24-16 win. Gardner-Johnson played 68 of the team's 69 defensive plays in the contest.

injuries.name: Greg Rousseau
injuries.headline: Rousseau logged eight tackles (five solo), including 2.0 sacks, in the Bills' 24-16 win over the Chargers on Sunday.
injuries.notes: Rousseau leads the NFL with 6.0 sacks, having logged 2.0 sacks in each of the first three games of the 2026 regular season. The linebacker has had a stunning breakout since switching to defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard's 3-4 defense. The 26-year-old is entering his sixth NFL season and has begun to make a compelling early case that should put him on Defensive Player of the Year ballots if he can keep producing throughout the season.

injuries.name: Ar'maj Reed-Adams
injuries.headline: Reed-Adams (elbow) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice.
injuries.notes: The rookie seventh-rounder was not available for the Bills' Week 3 home game against the Chargers due to an elbow injury. Reed-Adams' full practice Wednesday indicates he'll suit up against the Patriots on Sunday to provide the Bills with depth on the offensive line.

injuries.name: Keon Coleman
injuries.headline: Coleman (ankle) did not practice Wednesday.
injuries.notes: Coleman dealt with the ankle injury in practice last week and was listed as questionable for Week 3 before suiting up and playing just 48.5 percent of the offensive snaps against the Chargers. He turned two targets into one catch for 37 yards. If Coleman is unable to play Sunday against the Patriots, Joshua Palmer would be in line for increased snaps.

injuries.headline: questionable
injuries.notes: questionable

injuries.name: Damar Hamlin
injuries.headline: questionable
injuries.notes: questionable

injuries.name: Joe Andreessen
injuries.headline: questionable
injuries.notes: questionable

injuries.name: DJ Moore
injuries.headline: Moore (shoulder) was limited in Wednesday's practice.
injuries.notes: Moore was limited last week in practice after he was injured in Buffalo's Week 2 game against the Lions. The veteran wideout still played through it last Sunday against the Chargers and played 42 of 66 offensive snaps while running a team-high 23 routes on Josh Allen's 31 dropbacks. Moore turned 10 targets into six catches for 67 yards. He should be fine for Week 4 against New England.
injuries.vacated_opportunity_note: Expands to high-volume target progression and 2-WR/3-WR set route participation.

injuries.name: Josh Allen
injuries.headline: Allen (knee) was spotted participating in practice Wednesday, Sal Capaccio of WGR Sports Radio 550 Buffalo reports.
injuries.notes: Allen played every snap in this past Sunday's 24-16 win over the Chargers, but he appeared to take a hard hit to his left knee at one point during the fourth quarter and looked to be in pain. Head coach Joe Brady spoke to the media Monday and downplayed any concern about Allen's availability heading into this Sunday's matchup with the Patriots, and the quarterback's presence on the field for the start of Week 4 prep supports the notion that he'll be ready to go for game day. Jay Skurski of The Buffalo News noted that Allen had no noticeable protection on his knee during individual drills Wednesday and seemed to be moving around without issue.

injuries.name: Dawson Knox
injuries.headline: Knox hauled in his lone target for five yards in a 24-16 win over the Chargers on Sunday.
injuries.notes: Knox and fellow tight end Dalton Kincaid combined for only four targets from Josh Allen, with wide receiver DJ Moore leading all pass catchers with 10 targets. Knox is up to a 4-17-1 line on four targets through three games, and his production will be limited to occasional red zone opportunities as long as Kincaid is healthy. The Bills will stay home for an AFC East clash against the Patriots in Week 4.

injuries.name: T.J. Sanders
injuries.headline: doubtful
injuries.notes: doubtful

injuries.name: Khalil Shakir
injuries.headline: Shakir caught one of his three targets for six yards in the Bills' 24-16 win over the Chargers on Sunday.
injuries.notes: Shakir played 71 percent of the Bills' offensive snaps in the contest but caught just one pass. The wide receiver was bullied in coverage while Josh Allen struggled on a day when the team's offense combined for five total turnovers.

injuries.name: Ray Davis
injuries.headline: Davis played five snaps on offense and five snaps on special teams without showing up in the box score otherwise in the Bills' 24-16 win over the Chargers on Sunday.
injuries.notes: Davis' catch for no gain early in the fourth quarter was negated by a holding penalty by Alec Anderson. It appears Davis will not be a factor in the Bills' offensive game plan this season, with Ty Johnson serving as the backup option in the backfield for James Cook. Davis should continue to see the field as a contributor on special teams, though he did not return a kickoff after doing so in both of the first two games of the regular season.

injuries.name: Tyler Bass
injuries.headline: Bass made his lone field-goal attempt and all three of his extra-point tries during Sunday's 24-16 win over the Chargers.
injuries.notes: The Bills finally got on the scoreboard at the 6:02 mark of the second quarter on a 28-yard, chip-shot field goal by Bass, with the veteran kicker making each of his next three extra-point attempts. He's made all four of his field-goal tries (all within 50 yards) and has gone 11-for-12 on PATs through three regular-season games, and his scoring floor should be elevated week-to-week as long as Josh Allen is running the Bills offense. Buffalo wraps up its three-game homestand in a Week 4 AFC East showdown against New England.

injuries.name: Dalton Kincaid
injuries.headline: Kincaid secured two of three targets for 38 yards and lost a fumble in the Bills' 24-16 win over the Chargers on Sunday.
injuries.notes: Kincaid finished third in receptions and receiving yards on the afternoon for the Bills and tied for the same slotting in targets, but the tight end's downturn in production compared to the first two weeks stood out. He had opened the season with a combined 12-125-1 line on 14 targets, but the Chargers appeared to key on slowing him down Sunday and also forced the ball from him at the end of a 24-yard catch late in the third quarter for Kincaid's first lost fumble since his 2023 rookie campaign. Despite the relatively quiet performance, Kincaid should remain a key figure in the air attack during a Week 4 home matchup against the Patriots next Sunday.

injuries.name: James Cook III
injuries.headline: Cook rushed 24 times for 154 yards and a touchdown and failed to bring in his only target in the Bills' 24-16 win over the Chargers on Sunday. He also lost a fumble.
injuries.notes: Although neither offense looked anywhere close to cohesive as a whole, Cook was a rare exception. The star running back delivered another dominant performance on the ground despite his day getting off on the wrong foot, as he lost a fumble on the first play from scrimmage and saw the Chargers parlay it into a touchdown. Cook's longest run of the day was a relatively modest 23 yards, meaning he consistently ripped off chunk gains against the Chargers defense. He also went in for his second touchdown of the season at a critical juncture in the fourth quarter, extending a 17-13 Bills lead at the time with a three-yard run. Cook has quickly amassed 346 rushing yards at 6.0 yards per carry over his first three games, affording him an abundance of momentum heading into a Week 4 divisional home showdown against the Patriots next Sunday.

injuries.name: Christian Benford
injuries.headline: Benford (toe) has been ruled out for the rest of Sunday's game against the Chargers.
injuries.notes: Benford left the game in the third quarter due to a toe injury, which is severe enough for him to be sidelined for the rest of Sunday's contest. Te'Cory Couch and Davison Igbinosun will continue to operate in elevated roles in Benford's absence.

injuries.name: Ed Oliver
injuries.headline: Oliver (hip) is available for Sunday's game versus the Chargers.
injuries.notes: Oliver didn't play in the Week 2 win over Detroit due to a hip injury. However, despite carrying a questionable tag for the Week 3 meeting with the Chargers, the veteran will be back on the field, likely resulting in less work for DeWayne Carter.

injuries.name: Jordan Hancock
injuries.headline: The Bills placed Hancock (hamstring) on injured reserve Friday.
injuries.notes: Hancock likely suffered his hamstring injury in the Bills' Week 2 win over the Lions. The issue appears to be significant, leading the team to move Hancock to IR. The defensive back will need to miss at least four games before becoming eligible to return to the Bills' active roster. The team signed Greg Dortch from the practice squad to the active roster in a corresponding move.

injuries.name: Greg Dortch
injuries.headline: The Bills signed Dortch from the practice squad to the active roster Friday, Maddy Glabb reports.
injuries.notes: Dortch has expended two practice squad elevations for the Bills so far. The returner has played four offensive snaps and 18 special-teams snaps in the two contests, totaling 133 kick return yards and 46 punt return yards. With defensive back Jordan Hancock (hamstring) moving to IR, the team utilized the freshly opened spot to secure its primary returner a spot on the 53-man roster.

injuries.name: Monroe Freeling
injuries.headline: Freeling (concussion) did not participate in Wednesday's practice.
injuries.notes: Freeling entered the league's concussion protocol following the Panthers' 21-18 loss to the Browns in Week 3. A return to practice would indicate that the rookie first-rounder is progressing in his recovery, but even if he logs a full session, he would need to be cleared by an independent neurologist in order to play. Stone Forsythe and Albert Reese would be the top candidates to start at right tackle if Freeling is not cleared to play against the Lions on Sunday.

injuries.name: Damien Lewis
injuries.headline: Coach Dave Canales said Wednesday that Lewis (elbow) may return to game action following Carolina's bye in Week 5, Joe Person of The Athletic reports.
injuries.notes: Lewis sustained a UCL injury during Sunday's game at Cleveland, and it looks like he'll have to miss at least one game as a result. For now, Corey Bullock figures to start at left guard Sunday versus the Lions.

injuries.name: Devin Lloyd
injuries.headline: Lloyd (calf) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice.
injuries.notes: After missing last Sunday's loss to the Browns, Lloyd appears ready to return to the lineup Sunday night against the Lions. Lloyd was a star in the Panthers' Week 2 win over the Falcons, piling up nine tackles (seven solo), including 1.0 sack, and two interceptions, one of which was returned for a touchdown.

injuries.name: Nick Scott
injuries.headline: Scott (ribs) practiced fully Wednesday.
injuries.notes: After missing Week 3 against the Browns, Scott appears ready to return from his one-game absence. He should slide back into his starting role at safety alongside Tre'von Moehrig for Sunday night's game versus Detroit.

injuries.name: Mike Jackson
injuries.headline: Head coach Dave Canales said Wednesday that Jackson (groin) underwent core-muscle surgery and will be sidelined about eight weeks, Joe Person of The Athletic reports.
injuries.notes: The Panthers are in a code-red situation at cornerback after both starters, Jackson and Jaycee Horn (quadriceps), suffered significant injuries against Cleveland in Week 3. Ahead of a date with Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jameson Williams on national television Sunday night, Carolina will be relying on Will Lee, Akayleb Evans and Chau Smith-Wade to cover the snaps.

injuries.name: Xavier Legette
injuries.headline: Legette (knee) did not practice Wednesday, Alex Zietlow of The Charlotte Observer reports.
injuries.notes: Coach Dave Canales labeled Legette as week-to-week headed into Sunday night's game against the Lions. With Jalen Coker (quad) also dinged up, the Panthers could again be looking at giving Brycen Tremayne and John Metchie considerable playing time alongside Tetairoa McMillan in Detroit. Legette has a 2-64-0 receiving line on six targets across two games this season.
injuries.vacated_opportunity_note: Expands to high-volume target progression and 2-WR/3-WR set route participation.

injuries.name: Princely Umanmielen
injuries.headline: questionable
injuries.notes: questionable

injuries.name: Bryce Young
injuries.headline: Young (knee) was listed as a full participant on Wednesday's practice estimate, Darin Gantt of the Panthers' official site reports.
injuries.notes: Young played every snap in this past Sunday's 21-18 loss to the Browns, but he made a visit to the blue medical tent on the Carolina sideline at one point during the contest to get his knee checked out. The knee issue evidently isn't a concern heading into Week 4, when Young and the Panthers will be preparing to face off against a Lions defense that has surrendered an NFL-high 299.3 passing yards per game through three contests. Young will profile as a strong fantasy option this week, even while the status of one of his top pass-catching weapons in wideout Jalen Coker (quadriceps) remains somewhat murky.

injuries.name: Jalen Coker
injuries.headline: The Panthers listed Coker as a non-participant on Wednesday's practice estimate, Darin Gantt of the team's official site reports.
injuries.notes: Carolina held a walk-through session for its first Week 4 practice, and though Coker was in attendance for the workout, he looked to be rehabbing off to the side, per Joe Person of The Athletic. Coker had previously appeared on injury reports in Weeks 2 and 3 due to an ankle injury, but he's now tending to a minor quad strain, which knocked him out of this past Sunday's 21-18 loss to the Browns. Per Alex Zietlow of The Charlotte Observer, head coach Dave Canales said he's viewing Coker as day-to-day, so the wideout should have a decent chance at suiting up this Sunday versus the Lions so long as he can practice in some capacity Thursday and/or Friday.
injuries.vacated_opportunity_note: Expands to high-volume target progression and 2-WR/3-WR set route participation.

injuries.name: David Moore
injuries.headline: The Panthers signed Moore off the practice squad to the active roster Wednesday.
injuries.notes: With Xavier Legette (knee) missing last Sunday's loss to the Browns, Moore was elevated from the practice squad for his 2026 debut in Week 3. Now that Jalen Coker (quadriceps) is also dinged up, Moore gets a spot on the 53-man roster after playing five offensive snaps and another 13 on special teams against Cleveland.

injuries.name: Anthony Tyus III
injuries.headline: The Panthers signed Tyus from the practice squad to the active roster Wednesday.
injuries.notes: The 23-year-old running back made his regular-season NFL debut in Sunday's loss to the Browns, logging 14 snaps on special teams. He returned a pair of kickoffs for 47 yards and will now slot in behind Chuba Hubbard and AJ Dillon on the backfield depth chart.

injuries.name: Jaycee Horn
injuries.headline: The Panthers placed Horn (quadriceps) on injured reserve Wednesday.
injuries.notes: Horn suffered a torn quadriceps in Sunday's loss to the Browns and is expected to miss anywhere from 6-to-12 weeks. It's a brutal blow to the Carolina secondary, which will also be without Mike Jackson (groin) for at least the next four weeks after he was also placed on injured reserve Wednesday. Will Lee, Akayleb Evans and Chau Smith-Wade will handle cornerback duties moving forward.

injuries.name: Brycen Tremayne
injuries.headline: Tremayne finished with four receptions for 83 yards on six targets in Sunday's 21-18 loss to the Browns.
injuries.notes: After playing less than 20 percent of the offensive snaps and failing to draw a target in either of the Panthers' first two games, Tremayne took on an expanded profile in the passing attack in Week 3 while Xavier Legette (knee) was inactive and Jalen Coker (quadriceps) made an early exit. Tremayne ended up playing 62 of the team's 77 offensive snaps (81 percent), leading Carolina in receiving with a career-best yardage total. However, if the Panthers get one or both of Coker and Legette back for Week 4 against the Lions, Tremayne is likely to see his playing time drop precipitously.

injuries.name: Ryan Fitzgerald
injuries.headline: Fitzgerald went 4-for4 on field-goal tries in Sunday's 21-18 loss to the Browns.
injuries.notes: The kicker hit from 35, 41, 53 and 37 yards out, helping the Panthers stay in the game even as they struggled to find the end zone. Fitzgerald has made all seven of his field-goal attempts on the young season, though he has missed one extra point.

injuries.name: Darren Waller
injuries.headline: Waller brought in five of eight targets for 51 yards in the Panthers' 21-18 loss to the Browns on Sunday.
injuries.notes: Waller continued to click frequently with Bryce Young, leading the Panthers in receptions and targets while finishing second in receiving yards with totals that all qualified as season highs. The veteran tight end has proven to be a seamless fit in head coach Dave Canales' offense, recording 10 receptions for 112 yards and two touchdowns on 13 targets over the first three games. Waller should continue to fill a prominent role in a Week 4 home matchup against the high-powered Lions next Sunday night.

injuries.name: Chuba Hubbard
injuries.headline: Hubbard rushed 19 times for 82 yards and brought in all four targets for 28 yards in the Panthers' 21-18 loss to the Browns on Sunday.
injuries.notes: As expected, Hubbard dominated the touches out of the Panthers backfield, outpacing AJ Dillon by 15 carries. Hubbard also played his customary pass-game role with efficacy, recording a new season high in receptions along the way. He's upped his rushing yardage total over that of the previous contest in each game so far, and considering Jonathon Brooks (abdomen, IR) will remain unavailable for the foreseeable future, the former lines up for another workhorse role in a Week 4 home showdown against the Lions next Sunday night.

injuries.name: Tetairoa McMillan
injuries.headline: McMillan brought in two of five targets for 17 yards in the Panthers' 21-18 loss to the Browns on Sunday.
injuries.notes: The Panthers' No. 1 receiver fell victim to a Browns defense that played aggressively for the second straight game. Cleveland brought pressure on Bryce Young throughout while recording a trio of sacks and picking him off once, and McMillan's production suffered as a result. McMillan's catch and receiving yardage totals tied for and qualified as the second-lowest figures of his career, respectively, making it an all-around forgettable afternoon for the second-year wideout. The second-year wideout and the rest of the Panthers offense will look to regroup and atone for the stumble in a Week 4 primetime home showdown against the Lions next Sunday night, and McMillan will be in line for an even heavier workload than usual if Jalen Coker (quadriceps) is unable to suit up.

injuries.name: Jaelan Phillips
injuries.headline: Phillips (back) was a full participant in Thursday's practice.
injuries.notes: Phillips didn't practice Wednesday but was back out there for Thursday's session. While his presence at practice was an encouraging sign, his status is still worth monitoring ahead of the Week 3 meeting with the Browns. The 27-year-old has played in both of the Panthers' games during the 2026 campaign thus far, amassing five total tackles, including 2.0 sacks.

injuries.name: Trevis Gipson
injuries.headline: Gipson (head) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice.
injuries.notes: Gipson was not listed on the Panthers' injury report to start Week 3 prep. The linebacker exited the team's Week 2 win over the Falcons early to be evaluated for a possible concussion. Gipson was evidently cleared of any potential issue by an independent neurologist during the game and is all set to fully participate in practice leading up to Sunday's game against the Browns.

injuries.name: Bobby Brown III
injuries.headline: Brown (back) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice.
injuries.notes: Brown was unable to suit up for the Panthers' Week 2 win over the Falcons due to a back injury. The defensive tackle appears to be ready to return to action, logging full participation in the first practice of Week 3 prep. Brown will likely start alongside Lee Hunter and Derrick Brown in the Panthers' 3-4 defense during Sunday's game against the Browns.

injuries.name: Isaiah Simmons
injuries.headline: The Panthers signed Simmons to the active roster from their practice squad Wednesday, Darin Gantt of the team's official site reports.
injuries.notes: Simmons had been elevated for each of the team's first two games, playing 49 snaps on special teams and five on defense, but he failed to record any stats. The 28-year-old will likely continue to serve a similar role going forward.

injuries.name: Anthony Johnson Jr.
injuries.headline: ir
injuries.notes: ir

injuries.name: Dillon Thieneman
injuries.headline: Thieneman registered six tackles (four solo) and an interception during the Bears' 27-7 win over the Eagles on Sunday.
injuries.notes: Thieneman picked off Andy Dalton on a pass intended for Dontayvion Wicks in the end zone, and the Bears' offense capitalized on the turnover with an 11-play, 69-yard drive that ended with a 29-yard field goal by Cairo Santos to extend Chicago's lead to 10-0. Thieneman has played every single defensive snap through the first three regular-season games of his NFL career, and his 15 solo tackles are tied for seventh in the league.

injuries.name: Braxton Jones
injuries.headline: Jones is week-to-week with a knee injury, Courtney Cronin of ESPN.com reports.
injuries.notes: Jones exited the Bears' Monday night win over the Eagles early with a knee injury. After further evaluation, it has been determined that Jones will likely need to miss at least a week, if not longer, with the injury. Ozzy Trapilo or Theo Benedet will likely start at left tackle in Sunday's game against the Jets.

injuries.name: Kyler Gordon
injuries.headline: Gordon (calf) was estimated as a full participant on the Bears' official injury report Wednesday.
injuries.notes: Since he began the regular season on Chicago's reserve/PUP list, Gordon won't be eligible to suit up for game action again until Week 5 at Green Bay. With that said, his current availability at practice is a strong indication he's on track to do just that. His status will be worth monitoring until he is officially activated.

injuries.name: Caleb Williams
injuries.headline: Coach Ben Johnson said Williams is "getting better every singly day" but won't participate in Wednesday's walkthrough, Sean Hammond of the Chicago Tribune reports.
injuries.notes: Williams exited a Week 2 loss to the Vikings in the fourth quarter due to a hamstring injury. He was considered week-to-week by Johnson afterward and then didn't practice at all before being ruled out for Monday's game against the Eagles. On Sunday, Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport of ESPN reported that Williams was diagnosed with a Grade 2 right hamstring strain, which is considered to be a 3-to-4-week injury. Johnson told Chris Emma of 670TheScore.com on Wednesday that "the direction has already been made" as it pertains to a Week 4 starting QB this Sunday versus the Jets, but who that may be between Case Keenum and Tyson Bagent isn't known.
injuries.vacated_opportunity_note: Takes over first-team reps under center with full pass-funnel responsibility.

injuries.name: Cairo Santos
injuries.headline: Santos made both of his field-goal attempts and all three PATs in the Bears' 27-7 win over the Eagles on Monday night.
injuries.notes: Santos made field goals from 29 yards and 48 yards in the contest. The kicker had a consistent night and now moves to 4-for-5 on field-goal attempts and a flawless 11-for-11 on PATs over three regular-season games in 2026.

injuries.name: Kyle Monangai
injuries.headline: Monangai rushed 10 times for 31 yards and wasn't targeted in the Bears' 27-7 win over the Eagles on Monday night.
injuries.notes: The second-year back logged exactly half of D'Andre Swift's workload on the ground, with Monangai handling his third straight 10-carry total to open the season. The Rutgers product saw his efficiency take a notable dip for the second consecutive game following a stellar Week 1 where he averaged 10.0 yards per carry, yet Monangai's role as a fairly high-volume No. 2 back in Chicago's offense is safe. The lack of receiving work Monday night was a disappointment after Monangai posted a 4-35-0 line through the air in the first two games, but he'll have a chance to atone in what should be a favorable Week 4 home matchup against the Jets on Sunday.

injuries.name: Colston Loveland
injuries.headline: Loveland secured all four targets for 31 yards in the Bears' 27-7 win over the Eagles on Monday night.
injuries.notes: Head coach Ben Johnson appeared to make a concerted effort to get the ball into Loveland's hands Monday after the tight end's slow first two games, and that approach met with some success. While all three components of Loveland's receiving line qualified as season-high figures, the second-year pro's longest reception went for just 12 yards, and he was well behind the wideout trio of Kalif Raymond, Luther Burden and Rome Odunze in receiving yards. Loveland's chemistry with fill-in signal-caller Case Keenum was encouraging, however, and the duo should have a chance to continue working together in Sunday's Week 4 home matchup against the Jets.

injuries.name: Rome Odunze
injuries.headline: Odunze secured three of six targets for 44 yards in the Bears' 27-7 win over the Eagles on Monday night.
injuries.notes: Odunze was relegated to a complementary role in the 20-point victory, finishing fourth in receptions and third in both receiving yards and targets for the Bears on a night in which Case Keenum filled in for Caleb Williams (hamstring) under center. While Odunze entered the season as the presumptive No. 1 receiver, veteran offseason addition Kalif Raymond, who had familiarity with head coach Ben Johnson's scheme from their mutual time with the Lions, has enjoyed an expanded role over the first three games while gathering in an impressive 19 of 21 targets. Conversely, Odunze is averaging a career-best 17.4 yards per reception but has a modest eight catches and no touchdowns through three games, numbers he'll look to boost during a Week 4 home matchup against the Jets on Sunday.

injuries.name: Luther Burden III
injuries.headline: Burden secured seven of 11 targets for 61 yards and a touchdown while rushing once for seven yards in the Bears' 27-7 win over the Eagles on Monday night.
injuries.notes: The second-year wideout led the Bears in receptions and targets in the impressive win with totals that also qualified as season highs, while checking in second only to Kalif Raymond in receiving yards. Burden also scored his first touchdown of the season on a nifty shovel pass that he took eight yards to the house while breaking multiple tackles near the goal line to cap off Chicago's opening possession. Burden's ability to click with fill-in signal-caller Case Keenum bodes well for the receiver's fantasy prospects, considering Caleb Williams (hamstring) is still projected to miss several more games. Burden will look to carry over the momentum into a Week 4 home matchup against the Jets on Sunday.

injuries.name: Kalif Raymond
injuries.headline: Raymond caught six of seven targets for 90 yards and a touchdown and recorded two punt returns for 15 yards in the Bears' 27-7 win over the Eagles on Monday.
injuries.notes: Despite having three quarterbacks throwing him the ball in as many weeks, Raymond continues to be a top option for the Bears' receiving offense. The wide receiver was second in targets Monday night to only Luther Burden (11), who did not manage to exceed Raymond in yards. The returner's additional value on special teams just further adds to his offensive allure as the season continues.

injuries.name: Case Keenum
injuries.headline: Keenum completed 24 of 34 passes for 247 yards with two touchdowns and no interceptions while rushing four times for six yards and another score in the Bears' 27-7 win over the Eagles on Monday night. He also fumbled once but recovered.
injuries.notes: Keenum's final numbers underscore how effective he was running Ben Johnson's aggressive offense against a quality defense. The 38-year-old signal-caller, who got the starting nod over Tyson Bagent in Caleb Williams' (hamstring) stead, connected with seven different targets overall, facilitating multi-reception tallies for four of his pass catchers. Keenum completed an eight-yard shovel pass to Luther Burden for his first touchdown toss of the night, and he followed it up with an impressive 41-yard scoring strike to Kalif Raymond in the latter portion of the third quarter. He then closed out the scoring with a one-yard run just past the midway point of the final period, rounding out a rewarding fantasy night. Given Monday night's results, Keenum appears well in line to be under center for a Week 4 home matchup against the Jets on Sunday.

injuries.name: Cam Lewis
injuries.headline: Lewis exited Monday night's game against the Eagles with a leg injury, Sean Hammond of the Chicago Tribune reports.
injuries.notes: Lewis was unable to gain clearance to return to the game despite not receiving an official in-game injury designation. The slot cornerback went down untouched after blitzing on a play in the fourth quarter. More information on the severity of Lewis' injury should become available when the Bears resume practicing Wednesday.

injuries.name: D'Andre Swift
injuries.headline: Swift rushed 20 times for 84 yards and brought in two of three targets for four yards in the Bears' 27-7 win over the Eagles on Monday night.
injuries.notes: Facing the team he suited up for back in 2023, Swift had a nifty nine-yard run on the Bears' opening possession, but he otherwise found running room at a premium for the next two-plus quarters. However, Swift got it going late to help ice Chicago's impressive win, rattling off 23 yards on the first three plays of the Bears' final drive and then closing things out with a 15-yard tackle-breaking scamper on fourth-and-1 on the first play after the two-minute warning. Swift has eclipsed 80 rushing yards in two of the first three games of the campaign and will take an average of 4.7 yards per carry into a Week 4 home matchup against the Jets on Sunday.

injuries.name: Tyson Bagent
injuries.headline: Bagent (concussion) is expected to remain the Bears' backup quarterback for Monday's game against the Eagles, while Case Keenum starts in place of the injured Caleb Williams (hamstring), Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
injuries.notes: The Bears' No. 2 quarterback for the first two games of the season, Bagent was initially lined up to start against the Eagles after Williams sustained a Grade 2 hamstring strain in the Week 2 loss to the Vikings. However, after emerging from the Vikings game with a concussion, Bagent missed the first two practices of Week 3, resulting in Keenum taking all the reps with the first-team offense. Bagent returned to practice Saturday as a limited participant and had his questionable designation removed Sunday upon clearing the five-step concussion protocol, but because of his minimal practice time this week, the Bears will keep him in the backup role. Keenum will thus pick up his first start since the 2023 season, but barring a strong performance against a stout Eagles defense, the Bears would presumably go with Bagent as their starter Week 4 versus the Jets in the likely event that Williams remains out.

injuries.name: Tyrique Stevenson Sr.
injuries.headline: Stevenson (hamstring) does not have any injury designation ahead of Monday's game against the Eagles.
injuries.notes: Stevenson upgraded his participation level each day of the Bears' Week 3 prep. The cornerback went from a non-participant Thursday to a full participant in Saturday's session. Stevenson is all set to suit up for Sunday's contest as the starting outside cornerback opposite Jaylon Johnson.

injuries.name: Shemar Turner
injuries.headline: The Bears opened the 21-day practice window for Turner (knee) on Wednesday, Kevin Fishbain of The Athletic reports.
injuries.notes: Turner suffered a torn ACL during Week 8 of last season but is now closer to making his return to the field. The 23-year-old was placed on the reserve/PUP list in August and will have to miss at least two more games as a result before he's eligible to return. Once healthy, Turner could contribute as a depth defensive lineman.

injuries.name: Noah Sewell
injuries.headline: The Bears opened the 21-day practice window for Sewell (Achilles) on Wednesday, Kevin Fishbain of The Athletic reports.
injuries.notes: Sewell began the 2026 campaign on the reserve/PUP list while working his way back from a torn Achilles. Although that means he is required to miss at least two more games, it appears he is moving in a positive direction toward a return. The 24-year-old most recently appeared in 13 regular-season games for Chicago during the 2025 campaign, amassing 59 total tackles and one forced fumble.

injuries.name: Sam Roush
injuries.headline: Roush caught one of three targets for nine yards during the Bears' 9-3 loss to the Vikings on Sunday.
injuries.notes: The rookie third-rounder did not record a target in the Bears' Week 1 win over the Panthers, but Roush hauled in a nine-yard pass from Caleb Williams (hamstring) late in the third quarter for the former's first NFL catch. Roush is firmly behind Colston Loveland and Cole Kmet on the depth chart, although those three tight ends, along with the other Bears pass catchers, will all see their scoring floors lowered if Case Keenum is the starting quarterback against the Eagles in Week 3 if Williams and Tyson Bagent (concussion) are both unable to play.

injuries.name: Devin Bush
injuries.headline: Bush recorded four tackles (three solo) and a pass defensed during Sunday's 9-3 loss versus the Vikings.
injuries.notes: Bush played all 52 of Chicago's defensive snaps in Week 2, but he only managed four tackles, even against a run-heavy Minnesota attack. Managers relying on him for IDP production will be hoping for more in a Week 3 tilt versus the Eagles.

injuries.name: T.J. Edwards
injuries.headline: Edwards recorded four tackles (two solo) during Sunday's 9-3 loss versus the Vikings.
injuries.notes: Edwards played on 100 percent of the Bears' defensive snaps for the second time in as many games to open the season. However, Edwards' tackle total remained modest, and he'll look to boost his production in a Week 3 matchup against the Eagles.

injuries.name: Demetrius Knight Jr.
injuries.headline: Knight made nine tackles (two solo) in the Bengals' 30-27 loss to the Steelers on Sunday.
injuries.notes: Knight played 56 defensive snaps in the contest, good for 90 percent of the Bengals' defensive plays. The weak-side linebacker led the team in tackles but was unable to do much more in a close loss.

injuries.name: Dexter Lawrence II
injuries.headline: Lawrence logged four tackles (three solo), including 2.0 sacks, in the Bengals' 30-27 loss to the Steelers on Sunday.
injuries.notes: The prominent offseason addition to the Bengals' defensive line dominated in Sunday's game, showing why he commanded the 10th overall pick in the 2026 Draft as trade capital. Lawrence sacked Aaron Rodgers two times in the contest and accumulated another two tackles, anchoring the middle of the Bengals' 4-3 defensive front.

injuries.name: Kyle Dugger
injuries.headline: Dugger (quadriceps) did not participate at practice Wednesday, Paul Dehner Jr. of The Athletic reports.
injuries.notes: It's not immediately obvious, but Dugger might have sustained the quad injury at some point during Sunday's game at Pittsburgh. He'll likely need to get back on the practice field Thursday or Friday to have a chance to play in Week 4 versus the Jaguars.

injuries.name: Dalton Risner
injuries.headline: questionable
injuries.notes: questionable

injuries.name: Bryan Cook
injuries.headline: questionable
injuries.notes: questionable

injuries.name: Jordan Battle
injuries.headline: questionable
injuries.notes: questionable

injuries.name: Samaje Perine
injuries.headline: Perine turned three carries into nine yards and caught one pass on three targets for five yards during the Bengals' 30-27 loss to the Steelers on Sunday. He also returned one kickoff for 26 yards.
injuries.notes: Perine saw most of his offensive output in the first half and was limited to only one carry for zero gain in the second. His 18 offensive snaps were well behind Chase Brown's 40, and Perine figures to be limited to a rotational role in the Bengals' backfield this season unless Brown were to miss time. The Bengals will head home to host the Jaguars in Week 4.

injuries.name: Jalen Davis
injuries.headline: The Bengals placed Davis (hamstring) on injured reserve Tuesday.
injuries.notes: Davis injured his hamstring during the Bengals' 30-27 loss to the Steelers in Week 3. The injury is severe enough for the Utah State product to spend time on IR, which means he'll be sidelined for at least the next four games and is eligible to return for Week 9 against the Falcons on Sunday, Nov. 8. Ja'Sir Taylor (undisclosed) is also on injured reserve, so Dax Hill and Tacario Davis are both in line for more snaps in the Bengals' secondary.

injuries.name: Tanner Hudson
injuries.headline: The Bengals signed Hudson off the practice squad to the active roster Tuesday.
injuries.notes: Hudson was elevated from the practice squad for two of the Bengals' first three games of the regular season, accumulating three catches on as many targets for 17 yards. He'll now be a part of the team's 53-man roster moving forward and will contribute mostly on special teams and in a depth role on offense behind fellow tight ends Mike Gesicki, Drew Sample and Erick All.

injuries.name: Mitchell Tinsley
injuries.headline: The Bengals signed Tinsley off the Texans' practice squad to the active roster Tuesday.
injuries.notes: The Bengals needed to replenish their depth at wide receiver due to the injury absences of Andrei Iosivas (thumb, IR) and rookie fourth-rounder Colbie Young (knee), the latter of whom has already been ruled out for Week 4 against the Jaguars. Tinsley appeared in 17 regular-season games for the Bengals in 2025, finishing with an 8-117-2 receiving line on 24 targets, though he joined the Texans' practice squad Sept. 1 after failing to make Cincinnati's 53-man roster at the end of training camp. Now that he's back with the Bengals, Tinsley will contribute both on special teams and in a rotational role on offense.

injuries.name: B.J. Hill
injuries.headline: questionable
injuries.notes: questionable

injuries.name: Colbie Young
injuries.headline: Young (knee) is not expected to play in Week 4 against the Jaguars, Jay Morrison of SI.com reports.
injuries.notes: Young suffered a left knee injury in the first quarter of Sunday's 30-27 loss to the Steelers, and he was forced to miss the remainder of the contest. Head coach Zac Taylor provided an update Monday, explaining the wide receiver isn't dealing with a long-term injury, but he will be sidelined for at least one game. The Bengals are expected reevaluate the injury after Week 4 and then determine the next steps for Young.
injuries.vacated_opportunity_note: Expands to high-volume target progression and 2-WR/3-WR set route participation.

injuries.name: Mike Gesicki
injuries.headline: Gesicki caught all three of his targets for 37 yards and a touchdown during Sunday's 30-27 loss to Pittsburgh.
injuries.notes: Gesicki took a step in the right direction after he was blanked in the team's Week 2 victory over Houston. The tight end was able to finished tied with wide receiver Dohnte Meyers for third on the team in catches, and he left his mark on the game in the fourth quarter, connecting with quarterback Joe Burrow for a 25-yard touchdown. Gesicki has now caught eight of 10 targets for 112 yards and two touchdowns over three regular-season contests so far in 2026.

injuries.name: Evan McPherson
injuries.headline: McPherson made both of his field-goal attempts and each of his three extra-point tries during Sunday's 30-27 loss to Pittsburgh.
injuries.notes: McPherson's first made field goal came from 50 yards out, which was his fifth made field goal from 50-plus yards this season. He has yet to miss a kick through three regular-season games, and he'll continue to operate with a higher scoring floor than most kickers for as long as the Bengals' offense under Joe Burrow continues to move the ball. Up next is a Week 4 home tilt against the Jaguars on Sunday, Oct. 4.

injuries.name: Tee Higgins
injuries.headline: Higgins brought in six of seven targets for 90 yards and a touchdown in the Bengals' 30-27 loss to the Steelers on Sunday.
injuries.notes: Higgins and Ja'Marr Chase turned in signature performances in the high-scoring loss, and the former finished as the runner-up in receptions, receiving yards and targets on the day to his talented teammate. Higgins' first score of the season came on a difficult and contested 28-yard grab late in the first half, knotting the score at 17-17 going into halftime. Through three games, Higgins is on pace for a potential third career 1,000-yard season, as he's quickly amassed a 14-244-1 line on 23 targets.

injuries.name: Chase Brown
injuries.headline: Brown rushed 13 times for 61 yards and brought in both targets for eight yards in the Bengals' 30-27 loss to the Steelers on Sunday.
injuries.notes: Brown continued his career-long tradition of efficient rushing performances against the Steelers, but the running back's overall opportunities at least were somewhat capped due to game script. The versatile back also struggled to make an impact in the passing game for the second straight game after opening the season with a 5-22-0 receiving line, as he's produced the same number of receptions for just 10 yards over the last two contests. Brown should continue in a workhorse role against the Jaguars at home next Sunday.

injuries.name: Ja'Marr Chase
injuries.headline: Chase brought in nine of 12 targets for 98 yards and a touchdown in the Bengals' 30-27 loss to the Steelers on Sunday.
injuries.notes: Chase paced the Bengals in receptions, receiving yards and targets, taking his customary position at the top of the team's pass-catching corps. The All-Pro wideout recorded his touchdown on a three-yard grab with just under six minutes remaining in the first quarter to answer a Steelers opening-drive score, marking his third trip to the end zone already this season. Chase will aim to stay just as productive when the Jaguars pay a visit for a Week 4 showdown next Sunday.

injuries.name: Joe Burrow
injuries.headline: Burrow completed 28 of 37 passes for 282 yards with three touchdowns and no interceptions while adding two rushes for 13 yards in the Bengals' 30-27 loss to the Steelers on Sunday. He also lost a fumble.
injuries.notes: Burrow was impressive throughout the majority of the afternoon, taking just one sack from Pittsburgh's aggressive defense and connecting with Ja'Marr Chase, Tee Higgins and Mike Gesicki for his trio of scoring tosses. Burrow spread the ball around to nine different targets overall on an afternoon he entered already down Andrei Iosivas (thumb, IR) and during which he then lost promising rookie Colbie Young (knee). However, a would-be game-tying or game-winning drive was short-circuited by the franchise signal-caller, as he lost the handle on the ball on a sack with under a minute remaining, snuffing out any chance of Cincinnati being able to at least force overtime. The highly untimely turnover aside, Burrow has looked comfortable with an offensive approach that has him under center more often than previous seasons, and he'll next take aim at the Jaguars in a Week 4 home matchup next Sunday.

injuries.name: Andrei Iosivas
injuries.headline: The Bengals placed Iosivas (thumb) on injured reserve Saturday.
injuries.notes: Iosivas is having surgery to repair a torn ligament in his thumb, necessitating his move to injured reserve. As such, he will not be allowed to play for at least the next four games, so the earliest Iosivas can return is Week 8 against the Titans on Sunday, Nov. 1. Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins will continue to serve as the Bengals' top pass catchers, but in Iosivas' absence, there are more offensive snaps available for rookie fourth-rounder Colbie Young, Dohnte Meyers and Ke'Shawn Williams.

injuries.name: Jonathan Allen
injuries.headline: Allen (knee) missed practice for the second day in a row Thursday, but it was with a rest designation, Jay Morrison of SI.com reports.
injuries.notes: The defensive tackle popped up on the injury report Wednesday with a knee issue, but it does not appear to be serious.
