Allen should be able to continue playing a starting role for the Bengals on the defensive line this Sunday against the Steelers. The veteran has six tackles (five solo), including 2.0 sacks, through two games.

injuries.name: Teven Jenkins
injuries.headline: Jenkins (back) is officially listed as out for Thursday's game versus Pittsburgh.
injuries.notes: Jenkins was able to return to practice during the week on a limited basis, but he'll have to wait at least one more game to make his 2026 regular-season debut. Rookie third-rounder Austin Barber should get another start at right guard in Week 4.

injuries.name: Elgton Jenkins
injuries.headline: Jenkins (concussion) is officially listed as out for Thursday's game versus the Steelers.
injuries.notes: Jenkins was unable to practice during the week after entering concussion protocol, and he'll now spend at least one game on the sidelines as he recovers. In his stead, Luke Wypler projects to start at center in Week 4.

injuries.name: Tylan Wallace
injuries.headline: Wallace (knee) has been ruled out for Thursday's game against the Steelers.
injuries.notes: A knee injury prevented Wallace from practicing all week, so the sixth-year pro will observe Thursday's game from the sidelines, which means Isaiah Bond and Malachi Corley are both in line to see a slight uptick in offensive snaps. Wallace's next opportunity to play is Week 5 against the Jets on Sunday, Oct. 11.
injuries.vacated_opportunity_note: Expands to high-volume target progression and 2-WR/3-WR set route participation.

injuries.name: Grant Delpit
injuries.headline: Delpit (shoulder) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice session.
injuries.notes: Delpit was able to play through a shoulder issue during the Browns' 21-18 win over the Panthers on Sunday, and the seventh-year pro will do the same for Thursday's AFC North clash against the Steelers. He's played every single defensive snap through three regular-season games, accumulating 12 tackles (eight solo), including 1.0 sacks and one pass defense in that span.

injuries.name: Tyson Campbell
injuries.headline: Campbell (knee) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice.
injuries.notes: Campbell opened the week with back-to-back DNPs before fully practicing Wednesday, putting him on track to play in Thursday's AFC North showdown against the Steelers. With Campbell back in the fold, Mekhi Blackmon will revert to a depth role in the secondary for Week 4. Campbell has 12 tackles (seven solo) through two regular-season games.

injuries.name: Carson Schwesinger
injuries.headline: Schwesinger logged six tackles (one solo) in the Browns' 21-18 win over the Panthers on Sunday.
injuries.notes: Schwesinger played all 74 defensive snaps in Sunday's contest. He has played all 196 defensive snaps for the Browns through three regular-season games. The middle linebacker and signal caller for the defense did not have any incredible box-score feats in the Week 3 win but practiced stellar communication that helped enable Mason Graham's 2.0 sacks and Ronnie Hickman's game-winning interception.

injuries.name: Ronnie Hickman
injuries.headline: Hickman made eight tackles (three solo) and had one pass defensed for an interception in the Browns' 21-18 win over the Panthers on Sunday.
injuries.notes: Hickman intercepted Bryce Young on a third down with 16 seconds left in the game while the Browns were up by three points. The turnover sealed the game, securing the Browns consecutive wins for the first time since December 2023. The free safety played all 74 defensive snaps in the contest.

injuries.name: Mason Graham
injuries.headline: Graham logged seven tackles (four solo), including 2.0 sacks, in the Browns' 21-18 win over the Panthers on Sunday.
injuries.notes: Graham played 53 defensive snaps in the contest and notched two of the three sacks on quarterback Bryce Young. The second-year defensive tackle out of Michigan totaled 0.5 sacks throughout 17 games in 2025, so Sunday's production was easily a career high for the young player. Graham is up to 4.0 sacks through three regular-season games in 2026, leading all defensive tackles.

injuries.name: Jerry Jeudy
injuries.headline: Jeudy finished Sunday's 21-18 victory against Carolina with no targets or touches.
injuries.notes: It was the second straight week that Jeudy didn't log a reception, and this time he didn't even get a target (he logged just one in Week 2 versus Tampa Bay). The veteran wideout continues to be on the field fairly often -- he's recorded an offensive snap share of over 50 percent in each of the Browns' three contests, including Sunday when he played 51 percent. However, he doesn't seem to be clicking well with QB Deshaun Watson, and at this point fantasy managers have little reason to include him in their lineups.

injuries.name: KC Concepcion
injuries.headline: Concepcion finished Sunday's 21-18 victory versus Carolina with two catches (on nine targets) for nine yards. He also returned one punt for one yard.
injuries.notes: Concepcion actually tied tight end Harold Fannin for the team lead with nine targets, but the rookie wideout managed to haul in just two of those looks. His receptions went for five and four yards, continuing what has become a trend, as he's averaging a meager 6.7 yards per reception so far this season. The target share indicates that the Browns want Concepcion to be an integral part of the passing game, but so far he doesn't seem to be clicking with QB Deshaun Watson.

injuries.name: Denzel Boston
injuries.headline: Boston caught two of four targets for 41 yards during the Browns' 21-18 win over the Panthers on Sunday. He also caught a two-point conversion.
injuries.notes: The rookie second-rounder was held without a catch until the fourth quarter, when he caught 28- and 13-yard passes from Deshaun Watson before the duo connected on a two-point conversion late in the fourth quarter to extend the Browns' lead to three points. Boston was unable to record a touchdown catch for a third-straight game, though he still finished Sunday's contest as the Browns' second-leading receiver behind tight end Harold Fannin (51). Boston, Fannin and rookie first-rounder KC Concepcion will continue to serve as Watson's top targets in the passing game, with Jerry Jeudy and Isaiah Bond working in rotation. Boston will take a 9-195-2 receiving line (on 15 targets) into Thursday's AFC North showdown against the Steelers.

injuries.name: Andre Szmyt
injuries.headline: Szmyt made both of his field-goal attempts and his sole PAT in the Browns' 21-18 win over the Panthers on Sunday.
injuries.notes: Szmyt made field goals from 45 yards and 48 yards during the contest, with the 45-yarder coming in the fourth quarter to stake the Browns to a 13-12 lead. The kicker moved to a perfect 6-of-6 on field goals and 4-of-4 on PATs through three regular-season games in 2026.

injuries.name: Deshaun Watson
injuries.headline: Watson completed 16 of 30 passes for 144 yards with two touchdowns and no interceptions while rushing 11 times for 45 yards in the Browns' 21-18 win over the Panthers on Sunday. He also threw a two-point conversion pass.
injuries.notes: While Watson was anything but efficient through the air for the majority of the afternoon, the veteran signal-caller avoided turnovers and fired a pair of key touchdown passes to Harold Fannin, including a game-winning scoring toss with 1:48 remaining on which Watson scrambled to buy himself time before releasing the ball on the run. Watson's mobility played a key part throughout earlier portions of the game, as he was second on Cleveland in rushing yards with his highest total since Week 9 of the 2020 season while he was still with the Texans (he'd also rushed for 45 yards in Week 1 of the 2023 season). Watson is still clearly a work in progress in head coach Todd Monken's offense, but he appears to have an increasingly firm hold on the starting job heading into Thursday night's Week 4 divisional home clash against the Steelers.

injuries.name: Harold Fannin Jr.
injuries.headline: Fannin brought in seven of nine targets for 51 yards and two touchdowns in the Browns' 21-18 win over the Panthers on Sunday.
injuries.notes: The second-year tight end led the Browns in receptions, receiving yards and targets on the afternoon, and he capped off Cleveland's upset victory with a 14-yard touchdown grab at the 1:48 mark of the fourth quarter. The score proved to be the difference in the game, and it was preceded by a two-yard scoring reception just before halftime. After a quiet Week 1, Fannin has come alive with a combined 12-125-2 line on 15 targets over the last pair of contests, affording him plenty of momentum heading into a Week 4 divisional home showdown against the Steelers on Thursday night.

injuries.name: Quinshon Judkins
injuries.headline: Judkins rushed 18 times for 70 yards and brought in both targets for nine yards in the Browns' 21-18 win over the Panthers on Sunday.
injuries.notes: Judkins took all but one of the Browns' running backs' carries, and he was able to capitalize on an injury-hampered Panthers defense to produce his best showing of the new season. He still finished under 4.0 yards per carry, but after averaging under 3.0 in each of the first two games, Sunday's effort was certainly an improvement. Judkins and the surprising 2-1 Browns now have a quick turnaround for a Week 4 home divisional clash against the Steelers on Thursday night.

injuries.name: Mekhi Blackmon
injuries.headline: Blackmon will start at outside cornerback against the Panthers on Sunday due to the absence of Tyson Campbell (ankle/hip/knee), Daniel Oyefusi of ESPN.com reports.
injuries.notes: Campbell will be held out of Sunday's game while nursing multiple lower-body injuries, so Blackmon and Denzel Ward will be the starting outside cornerbacks for the Browns in Week 3. Blackmon started in 11 of 17 regular-season games with the Colts in 2025 and finished the year with 64 tackles (50 solo), including 1.0 sacks, and seven pass defenses (including two interceptions).

injuries.name: Blake Whiteheart
injuries.headline: Whiteheart caught one of his two targets for a 17-yard touchdown in Sunday's 23-19 win over the Buccaneers.
injuries.notes: Whiteheart played 27 of the Browns' 58 offensive snaps in Sunday's contest, and his one catch, which came with 3:51 remaining, erased a 19-16 deficit and proved to be the difference in the game. The tight end also contributed on 15 special-teams snaps. Whiteheart is the second option at tight end behind Harold Fannin but plays a significant run-blocking role.

injuries.name: Jaleel McLaughlin
injuries.headline: McLaughlin logged one carry for three yards and could not catch his sole target in Sunday's 23-19 win over the Buccaneers.
injuries.notes: McLaughlin saw just eight offensive snaps in Sunday's win. The running back was signed to the active roster from the practice squad last Tuesday after Dylan Sampson (knee) was placed on injured reserve. McLaughlin appears set to fill a depth role behind Quinshon Judkins and Raheim Sanders until Sampson is able to return.

injuries.name: Raheim Sanders
injuries.headline: Sanders caught his sole target for seven yards, had two rushes for four yards and returned two kickoffs for 50 yards in Sunday's 23-19 win over the Buccaneers.
injuries.notes: Sanders played 11 offensive snaps and six special-teams snaps in Sunday's contest. Despite the small snap share, Sanders found plenty to do in Cleveland's first win of the season, making key plays for both the offensive and special-teams units.

injuries.name: Jonathan Bullard
injuries.headline: The Cowboys placed Bullard (calf) on injured reserve Wednesday, Tommy Yarrish of the Cowboys' official site reports.
injuries.notes: Bullard suffered a calf injury during the Cowboys' Week 3 loss to the Ravens. The injury is severe enough for him to require a stint on IR, which means he'll have to miss at least the next four games and is eligible to return for Week 8 against the Cardinals on Sunday, Nov. 1. Rookie fourth-rounder LT Overton could see a bump in rotational defensive snaps for as long as Bullard is on the shelf.

injuries.name: Malik Hooker
injuries.headline: Hooker (forearm) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice, Tommy Yarrish of the Cowboys' official site reports.
injuries.notes: Hooker was unable to practice during the Cowboys' Week 3 prep, getting ruled out early ahead of the game against the Ravens. The free safety starting Week 4 prep as a limited participant is a great sign that the 30-year-old may be able to suit up for Sunday's game against the Texans. Hooker will likely need to upgrade to a full participant by Friday to avoid any injury designation ahead of Sunday's contest.

injuries.name: DeMarvion Overshown
injuries.headline: Overshown (hamstring) did not participate in Wednesday's practice, Tommy Yarrish of the Cowboys' official site reports.
injuries.notes: Overshown has not practiced since sustaining a hamstring injury during the Cowboys' Week 1 loss to the Giants. Given the amount of time he's been sidelined, Overshown likely needs to log at least one limited session during Week 4 prep to have a chance to suit up for Sunday's game against the Texans.

injuries.name: Jalen Thompson
injuries.headline: The Cowboys placed Thompson (hamstring) on injured reserve Wednesday, Tommy Yarrish of the Cowboys' official site reports.
injuries.notes: Thompson sustained the injury in Sunday's loss to the Ravens and will now miss at least the next four contests. Markquese Bell filled in alongside rookie Caleb Downs at safety following Thompson's departure.

injuries.name: Tyler Smith
injuries.headline: Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer said Tuesday that Smith (thumb) is progressing well and could return from injured reserve for the team's Week 5 game against the Buccaneers, Todd Archer of ESPN.com reports.
injuries.notes: Smith is working his way back from thumb surgery and has apparently hit no snags in the recovery process thus far. T.J. Bass has been serving as the Cowboys' starting left guard to begin the season, but he'll shift into a reserve role once Smith -- a three-time Pro Bowl selection -- is ready to return to action.

injuries.name: Ryan Flournoy
injuries.headline: Flournoy caught just two of eight targets for 22 yards in Sunday's 34-31 loss to the Ravens.
injuries.notes: Flournoy logged 66 percent of the offensive snaps against Baltimore, and his eight targets were good for second on the team and a respectable 20 percent share. He obviously was unable to do much with them against a stingy Ravens secondary. Flournoy has a valuable role as the third receiver in a Dallas offense that likes to use plenty of 11 personnel, but he'd likely need an injury to CeeDee Lamb or George Pickens to become anything more than a bench stash in fantasy.

injuries.name: Cobie Durant
injuries.headline: Durant (hamstring) likely won't be suiting up for Sunday's game against the Texans, Joe Hoyt of The Dallas Morning News reports.
injuries.notes: When addressing reporters Tuesday, head coach Brian Schottenheimer was not very optimistic about the starting cornerback's chances of playing in Week 4. Durant sustained a hamstring injury during the Cowboys' Week 2 win over the Commanders and has not practiced since suffering the injury. With current starter Shavon Revel (knee) also dealing with an injury, Ameer Speed may start at cornerback opposite DaRon Bland in Sunday's game.

injuries.name: Shavon Revel Jr.
injuries.headline: Revel (knee) is expected to "work into" practice this week, Nick Harris of the Fort Worth Star-Telegram reports.
injuries.notes: Revel was hurt while attempting to make a tackle in Sunday's loss to Baltimore. Head coach Brian Schottenheimer indicated Tuesday that the cornerback is likely to practice to some extent this week, so Revel has a chance to suit up Sunday versus Houston. That could be particularly important with Cobie Durant dealing with a hamstring injury that caused him to sit out Week 3 and that could sideline him for additional contests.

injuries.name: Jake Ferguson
injuries.headline: Ferguson caught three of five targets for 23 yards and a touchdown while also losing a fumble during Sunday's 34-31 loss to the Ravens.
injuries.notes: Ferguson was able to reach the end zone for the second straight week, connecting with quarterback Dak Prescott for a 19-yard score in the third quarter. The tight end did have a mishap early in the fourth quarter, losing a fumble after reeling in a short pass from Prescott. Ferguson now has hauled in nine of 11 targets for 72 yards and three touchdowns over three contests this season, and he'll face a tough test against the Texans' dominant defense in Week 4.

injuries.name: Brandon Aubrey
injuries.headline: Aubrey went three of four on field-goal tries and 2-for-2 on extra-point attempts in Sunday's 34-31 loss to the Ravens.
injuries.notes: The kicker had a 59-yard attempt blocked in the third quarter. Aubrey has now missed one field goal and one extra point this season, though he is getting plenty of opportunities in Dallas' high-scoring offense, with nine extra-point attempts and seven field-goal tries through three games.

injuries.name: Dak Prescott
injuries.headline: Prescott completed 25 of 40 passes for 276 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 34-31 loss to the Ravens. He added 19 rushing yards on four carries and also threw a two-point conversion to CeeDee Lamb.
injuries.notes: Despite the big numbers for the Cowboys on the scoreboard, Prescott had a relatively quiet day in Rio, with Jake Ferguson hauling in his only TD pass in the third quarter. Prescott didn't commit any turnovers for a second straight game, and through three weeks he's completed 69.5 percent of his passes (73-for-105) for 730 yards and a 7:1 TD:INT. The veteran QB will look to stay efficient in a Week 4 road trip to Houston.

injuries.name: George Pickens
injuries.headline: Pickens caught seven of 11 targets for 82 yards in Sunday's 34-31 loss to Baltimore.
injuries.notes: The fifth-year wideout led the Cowboys in targets while setting new season highs in targets, catches and receiving yards, as he begins to shake off a slow start to the campaign. Pickens is still searching for his first TD of 2026, or even his first gain of 20-plus yards, but he'll look to continue building momentum in a Week 4 road trip to Houston.

injuries.name: CeeDee Lamb
injuries.headline: Lamb caught seven of eight targets for 112 yards in Sunday's 34-31 loss to the Ravens. He also caught a two-point conversion.
injuries.notes: George Pickens led the Cowboys in targets with 11, but it was Lamb who paced the team in receiving yards while the two star wideouts each tied for the team lead in receptions. This was the first game in 2026 during which Lamb failed to score a TD, but he has produced back-to-back performances of over 100 yards. He'll take a 20-309-3 line on 25 targets into a Week 4 road trip to Houston.

injuries.name: Javonte Williams
injuries.headline: Williams carried the ball 19 times for 98 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 34-31 loss to the Ravens. He also caught two of three targets for five yards.
injuries.notes: The veteran back gave the Cowboys a 10-0 lead in the first quarter with a two-yard TD plunge, his third trip to the end zone in three games this season, and Williams topped 100 scrimmage yards for the first time since Week 12 of 2025. Even with Sunday's strong effort, Williams has managed just 3,9 yards per carry to begin the year, a major downturn from his 4.8 mark in 2025. He'll look to keep building momentum in a Week 4 road trip to Houston.

injuries.name: Markquese Bell
injuries.headline: Bell (dehydration) has returned to Sunday's contest against Baltimore, Tommy Yarrish of the Cowboys' official site reports.
injuries.notes: Bell was briefly sidelined while battling dehydration, but he has now made his way back out onto the field. The safety is operating in a starting role in the absence of Malik Hooker (forearm) and P.J. Locke (foot), and he will look to leave his mark during the final stretch of Sunday's matchup.

injuries.name: Tyler Goodson
injuries.headline: Goodson is active for Sunday's game against the Ravens.
injuries.notes: Todd Archer of ESPN.com initially reported that Goodson would be a healthy scratch. Instead, it will be Emari Demercado (coach's decision) that will be inactive, with Goodson and Javonte Williams the active running backs for the Cowboys in Brazil.

injuries.name: Emari Demercado
injuries.headline: Demercado (coach's decision) is listed as inactive Sunday against the Ravens in Rio de Janeiro.
injuries.notes: Demercado served as the No. 2 RB behind Javonte Williams in the first two games of the campaign, totaling five carries for 15 yards. In Week 3, though, he'll take a backseat to Tyler Goodson. Demercado's next chance to suit up is next Sunday in Houston.

injuries.name: Justin Barron
injuries.headline: The Cowboys signed Barron from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday.
injuries.notes: Barron was elevated to the active roster for the Cowboys' Week 2 win over the Commanders. The linebacker played one defensive snap and 20 special teams snaps in the contest. Barron will likely continue in his role as a special-teamer while on the 53-man roster. Free safety P.J. Locke (foot) was moved to IR in a corresponding move.

injuries.name: P.J. Locke
injuries.headline: The Cowboys placed Locke (foot) on injured reserve Saturday.
injuries.notes: Locke has not practiced since sustaining a foot injury in the Cowboys' Week 2 win over the Commanders. The free safety must now miss at least four games on IR before becoming eligible to return to the team's active roster. While Locke is absent, Markquese Bell will likely start at free safety alongside strong safety Jalen Thompson.

injuries.name: Dee Winters
injuries.headline: Winters (shoulder) has returned to Sunday's game against the Commanders, Tommy Yarrish of the Cowboys' official site reports.
injuries.notes: Winters sustained a shoulder injury in the first quarter and exited the contest for further evaluation. Winters has now been cleared to return, which should lead to a reduction in snaps for Shemar James and Jaishawn Barham.

injuries.name: Caleb Downs
injuries.headline: Downs totaled eight tackles (four solo), including 1.0 sacks, during Dallas' loss to the Giants on Sunday.
injuries.notes: Downs had a strong performance in his regular-season debut despite the loss, as he finished tied for third on the team in tackles and logged one of their two sacks of Jaxson Dart. The 21-year-old will look to keep up this high level of production throughout his rookie campaign.

injuries.name: Alex Singleton
injuries.headline: Singleton finished Sunday's 30-26 win over the Rams with eight tackles (five solo).
injuries.notes: Singleton played every single defensive snap for a second consecutive week, and he finished Sunday's game tied with Patrick Surtain as the Broncos' second-leading tackler behind Brandon Jones (eight). Singleton is up to 33 combined tackles through three regular-season games, which leads the Broncos and is tied with Fred Warner for second most in the NFL behind rookie second-rounder Anthony Hill (34). Singleton and the Broncos' defense will have its hands full in a Week 4 road tilt against the 49ers.

injuries.name: Brandon Jones
injuries.headline: Jones posted 12 tackles (10 solo) and one pass defense during the Broncos' 30-26 win over the Rams on Sunday.
injuries.notes: Sunday was the first time since Week 3 of the 2025 season that Jones posted double-digit tackles, and his 10 solo tackles were one shy from matching his career high that he set in Week 6 of the 2024 campaign against the Chargers. Jones has played almost every single defensive snap and is up to 22 combined tackles through three regular-season games, which is second only to Alex Singleton (33) on the Broncos.

injuries.name: Talanoa Hufanga
injuries.headline: Hufanga recorded five tackles (two solo), including 1.0 sacks and three pass defenses (one interception and a pick-six) during the Broncos' 30-26 win over the Rams in Week 3.
injuries.notes: Hufanga's heroics in the fourth quarter was a driving force behind the Broncos' come-from-behind victory this past Sunday. It started early in the period with a 10-yard sack on Matthew Stafford on a third-and-5, leading to a 48-yard field goal by Harrison Mevis. Hufanga followed that up by picking off a Stafford pass intended for Kyren Williams, which Hufanga returned 66 yards for a touchdown to give the Broncos the lead. The sixth-year safety wrapped up his career night with a game-sealing interception off Stafford in the end zone on the final play of the contest. Hufanga and the Broncos will look to carry their momentum into a Week 4 road tilt against the 49ers this Sunday.

injuries.name: Marvin Mims Jr.
injuries.headline: Mims (foot) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice.
injuries.notes: Mims has missed the last two games with a foot injury, but his full practice Wednesday puts him track to play Sunday against the 49ers. Mims ran just nine routes in Week 1 against the Chiefs and is likely to remain in a bit role behind Jaylen Waddle, Courtland Sutton and Pat Bryant at wide receiver.

injuries.name: Jaylen Waddle
injuries.headline: Waddle (leg) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice, Parker Gabriel of The Denver Post reports.
injuries.notes: Though he was seen donning a walking boot following Sunday's win over the Rams, Waddle may have just been wearing the boot as a precaution. He was back on the field three days later and took every rep in practice, with head coach Sean Payton relaying afterward that Waddle is "doing fine." Waddle thus looks like he'll be ready to handle his usual allotment of snaps in Sunday's game at San Francisco.

injuries.name: Dondrea Tillman
injuries.headline: questionable
injuries.notes: questionable

injuries.name: Evan Engram
injuries.headline: Engram failed to haul in his two targets during the Broncos' 30-26 win over the Rams on Sunday.
injuries.notes: Although he wasn't listed as a starter, Engram's 40 offensive snaps led all Broncos tight ends, including Adam Trautman (27). That's little comfort to those expecting Engram to at least see some involvement in the offense, with the veteran tight end sporting a 5-60-1 receiving line on eight targets through three games. He's recorded at least 60 targets in each of his first nine NFL seasons, but he's well behind that pace in 2026. Perhaps Engram's fortune will be better in Week 4 against the 49ers, whose defense gave up nine catches on 11 targets for 75 yards to Trey McBride in a Week 3 win over the Cardinals.

injuries.name: Pat Bryant
injuries.headline: Bryant recorded two receptions for 44 yards and a touchdown on two targets in Sunday's 30-26 win over the Rams. He also scored on a two-point conversion.
injuries.notes: Bryant reached the end zone for the first time this season with 7:44 left in the third quarter, connecting with quarterback Bo Nix on a five-yard catch. The second-year wideout has seen his snap share gradually climb through the first three weeks, topping out at 70 percent in Week 3. The Broncos have been without Marvin Mims (foot) for the past two games, however, so Bryant could see a slight downturn in playing time once the Denver receiving corps is at full strength.

injuries.name: Wil Lutz
injuries.headline: Lutz missed his one field-goal attempt and went 2-for-2 on PATs in Sunday's 30-26 win over the Rams.
injuries.notes: With the Broncos trailing 16-0 in the first half, coach Sean Payton went for two after each of the team's first two touchdowns instead of using Lutz for the point-after attempts. Prior to that, Lutz missed a 43-yard field goal try when he hit the left upright. On the season, Lutz has attempted just four field goals and five extra points, making him an uninspiring fantasy kicker.

injuries.name: Courtland Sutton
injuries.headline: Sutton caught three of seven targets for 46 yards in Sunday's 30-26 win over the Rams.
injuries.notes: Sutton led the team in receiving yards Sunday night while tying for the team lead in targets with RJ Harvey and Jaylen Waddle. This was a step in the right direction after Sutton mustered just 36 receiving yards over the previous two games combined. Between the offseason acquisition of Waddle and the change in play callers from Sean Payton to Davis Webb, Sutton has taken a step back early in the 2026 season after exceeding 1,000 receiving yards in each of the previous two regular seasons and catching 15 touchdown passes over that span. Sutton is still searching for his first TD of the campaign heading into a Week 4 road game against the 49ers.

injuries.name: J.K. Dobbins
injuries.headline: Dobbins rushed 17 times for 49 yards while catching one of two targets for four yards in Sunday's 30-26 win over the Rams.
injuries.notes: Dobbins is up to 35 rushing attempts through three weeks, while no other Denver running back has exceeded 10. Jonah Coleman (ankle) was placed on injured reserve Saturday, while RJ Harvey has more targets (11) than carries (five). Dobbins has yet to score on the ground after recording four rushing touchdowns last season, and he has been a non-factor in the passing game, as Sunday's targets were Dobbins' first two of the season. On the bright side, Dobbins has recovered from previous hip and hamstring concerns and is poised to keep leading Denver's ground game in Week 4 at San Francisco.

injuries.name: RJ Harvey
injuries.headline: Harvey (hamstring) rushed twice for six yards while catching six of seven targets for 41 yards in Sunday's 30-26 win over the Rams.
injuries.notes: Harvey didn't see much involvement on the ground but tied for the team lead in targets in his return from a one-game absence due to a hamstring injury. He was evaluated for a concussion in the second half and cleared to return, though Harvey had just one touch after that point. J.K. Dobbins is likely to keep working as Denver's primary rushing option in Week 4 against the 49ers, especially with rookie fourth-round pick Jonah Coleman (ankle) on IR, while Harvey remains the preferred running back in passing situations.

injuries.name: Bo Nix
injuries.headline: Nix completed 17 of 34 passes for 186 yards, two touchdowns and one interception in Sunday's 30-26 win over the Rams. He also rushed four times for seven yards and a touchdown in addition to throwing two successful two-point conversions.
injuries.notes: Nix threw for just 53 yards in the first half as the Broncos took a 16-0 deficit into the locker room. Denver turned things around in the third quarter, tying things up at 16-16 heading into the fourth quarter thanks to touchdown passes of five yards to Pat Bryant and eight yards to Nate Adkins, which were followed up by two-point conversions for Jaylen Waddle and Bryant, respectively, all thrown by Nix. The dual-threat QB made his biggest play down the stretch on the ground, powering in the go-ahead one-yard touchdown with 47 seconds left in the fourth quarter after being ruled out just short of the goal line on the preceding play. Denver's defense picked off Matthew Stafford on the game's final play to seal the victory and improve to 2-1. Nix has come up short of 200 passing yards twice in three games heading into a Week 4 road game against the 49ers, and he hasn't been running much since returning from ankle surgery, with just 15 rushing yards this season.

injuries.name: Jonah Coleman
injuries.headline: Coleman (ankle) is being placed on injured reserve Saturday, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
injuries.notes: Coleman has been diagnosed with a high-ankle sprain and was unable to practice all week. He'll now go on IR and will be required to miss at least four games, meaning the earliest he can return is Week 7 against the Cardinals on Sunday, Oct. 25. With Coleman sidelined, Tyler Badie could see an uptick in offensive snaps as the third option in the Broncos' backfield behind J.K. Dobbins and RJ Harvey.

injuries.name: Troy Franklin
injuries.headline: Franklin caught one of two targets for 27 yards in Sunday's 20-13 win over the Jaguars.
injuries.notes: With Marvin Mims (foot) inactive, Franklin played 13 of 62 offensive snaps as the clear No. 4 receiver behind Courtland Sutton, Pat Bryant and Jaylen Waddle. Franklin's 27-yard grab was his lone catch of the season through two weeks. He'll need an injury to obtain any fantasy relevance in redraft formats.

injuries.name: Nate Adkins
injuries.headline: Adkins caught all three of his targets for 32 yards and a touchdown while rushing once for six yards in Sunday's 20-13 win over the Jaguars.
injuries.notes: Adkins played 23 of the Broncos' 62 offensive snaps while also contributing six snaps to the special-teams unit. The No. 3 tight end was particularly reliable in his complementary role, catching everything thrown his way and scoring a fourth-quarter touchdown to tie the game at 13 points.

injuries.name: Tyler Badie
injuries.headline: Badie rushed one time for one yard in Denver's 20-13 win over the Jaguars on Sunday. He added two catches for 28 yards on three targets.
injuries.notes: With RJ Harvey (hamstring) inactive against Jacksonville and J.K. Dobbins suffering a hamstring injury of his own in the game, Badie saw 16 offensive snaps behind rookie Jonah Coleman. Badie also returned three kickoffs for 84 yards on special teams.

injuries.name: Zach Allen
injuries.headline: Allen recorded five tackles (three solo) including 2.0 sacks during Monday's 31-10 loss at Kansas City.
injuries.notes: Allen got off to a great start to the year in Week 1, recording multiple sacks in a game for his first time since 2024. The disruption he creates on the interior won't always show up in the box score, but he'll remain a big part of the defensive puzzle for Denver going into a Week 2 matchup versus the Jaguars.

injuries.name: D.J. Reed
injuries.headline: Reed (ribs) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice.
injuries.notes: Reed presumably picked up the injury during the Lions' 31-24 win over the Jets in Week 3, when he played 62 of 66 defensive snaps (93.9 percent) and finished with eight tackles (five solo) and one pass defense. He'll have two more chances to increase his practice participation to full and avoid an injury designation for Sunday's road game against the Panthers.

injuries.name: DJ Wonnum
injuries.headline: questionable
injuries.notes: questionable

injuries.name: Derrick Barnes
injuries.headline: Barnes registered eight tackles (five solo) and a defensed pass Sunday in a 31-24 victory against the Jets.
injuries.notes: Barnes tied with D.J. Reed for the second-most tackles on Detroit behind Christian Izien (11). Barnes has been consistent to begin the campaign, recording between six and eight stops in each of his three games so far. He also has 2.0 sacks on the campaign, halfway to his career-high total over 17 regular-season contests last year.

injuries.name: Chuck Clark
injuries.headline: Clark finished Sunday's 31-24 win over the Jets with seven tackles, including 1.0 sacks, and a forced fumble.
injuries.notes: Clark continues to start at safety for Detroit with with Brian Branch (Achilles) and Kerby Joseph (knee) both on the PUP list. Clark logged just a 45 percent defensive snap share in Week 1, but he upped that to 86 percent in Week 2 before playing every one of the Lions' 61 defensive snaps in Week 3. The veteran defender came up with a huge play late in the contest, sacking Jets QB Geno Smith and causing him to fumble with less than a minute remaining and New York nearing the red zone while trailing by seven points. The sack was Clark's first since he played for the Jets in 2024.

injuries.name: Christian Izien
injuries.headline: Izien posted 11 tackles (nine solo) and one defensed pass Sunday in a 31-24 win over the Jets.
injuries.notes: Izien paced the Lions in stops while playing all but two of the team's defensive snaps. The 26-year-old appears to be fully recovered from the groin injury that caused him to sit out Detroit's season opener. Izien has taken on a starting safety role due to Brian Branch (Achilles) and Kerby Joseph (knee) both being on the PUP list.

injuries.name: Isaac TeSlaa
injuries.headline: TeSlaa caught all three of his targets for 66 yards in the Lions' 31-24 win over the Jets on Sunday.
injuries.notes: Detroit's third receiver, TeSlaa played 48 percent of the offensive snaps against New York but made the most of his opportunities and ended up leading the team in receiving yards. With Jameson Williams continuing to struggle to get going early in the season, TeSlaa could start earning a couple more looks from Jared Goff. It's still unlikely to be enough to put TeSlaa in the redraft fantasy mix unless one of Williams or Amon-Ra St. Brown misses time with an injury.

injuries.name: Ben Bartch
injuries.headline: questionable
injuries.notes: questionable

injuries.name: Cade Mays
injuries.headline: Mays (wrist) is targeting a Week 7 return from injured reserve, Dave Birkett of the Detroit Free Press reports.
injuries.notes: Mays was placed on IR on Aug. 30. The center fractured his wrist in the preseason but is set to return to the active roster soon. If Mays can get back in action after the Lions' Week 6 bye, he should be able to reclaim the starting center role from Juice Scruggs to boost the team's interior offensive line.

injuries.name: Jake Bates
injuries.headline: Bates made a 30-yard field goal and all four of his extra-point tries in Sunday's 31-24 win over the Jets.
injuries.notes: The third-year pro is now 12-for-12 on extra-point attempts and 3-for-3 on field-goal tries in 2026. Bates is also the beneficiary of an offense that has scored 31 points in all three games so far.

injuries.name: Sam LaPorta
injuries.headline: LaPorta caught three of four targets for 44 yards in Sunday's 31-24 win over the Jets.
injuries.notes: The fourth-year tight end had his quietest game of the season, as five different Lions saw at least three targets from Jared Goff on the afternoon. LaPorta has been a complementary piece of an offense dominated by Jahmyr Gibbs and Amon-Ra St. Brown in the early going, producing a 14-144-1 line on 19 targets through three contests. LaPorta will look to step up his numbers in Week 4 on the road against the Panthers.

injuries.name: Jameson Williams
injuries.headline: Williams caught all four of his targets for 49 yards in Sunday's 31-24 win over the Jets.
injuries.notes: The fifth-year wideout has watched Jahmyr Gibbs and Amon-Ra St. Brown dominate the Lions' offense to begin the season, as that duo has combined for 11 total touchdowns -- including four in Sunday's win -- while Williams is still looking to make his first trip to the end zone in 2026. Williams will take a 10-137-0 line on 17 targets into a Week 4 tilt on the road against the Panthers.

injuries.name: Jared Goff
injuries.headline: Goff completed 25 of 32 passes for 269 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 31-24 win over the Jets. He added six rushing yards on four carries.
injuries.notes: The veteran QB found Amon-Ra St. Brown for a four-yard score in the second quarter and Jahmyr Gibbs for an 11-yard TD inside the final two minutes of the fourth for the game-winning points. Goff has tossed multiple touchdowns in three straight games to begin the year, completing 70.6 percent of his passes (77-for-109) for 802 yards and a stellar 8:0 TD:INT. He'll look to keep rolling in a Week 4 road clash against the Panthers.

injuries.name: Amon-Ra St. Brown
injuries.headline: St. Brown caught four of eight targets for 19 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 31-24 win over the Jets.
injuries.notes: The star wideout tied Jahmyr Gibbs to lead the Lions in targets, but St. Brown did little with his volume aside from a four-yard TD strike from Jared Goff in the second quarter. It was still St. Brown's fifth score of the season in three games, to go along with 23 catches for 228 yards on 35 targets. He'll likely get plenty of looks from Goff again in Week 4 on the road against the Panthers.

injuries.name: Jahmyr Gibbs
injuries.headline: Gibbs carried the ball 20 times for 99 yards and two touchdowns while catching seven of eight targets for 65 yards and a third TD in Sunday's 31-24 win over the Jets.
injuries.notes: That's now six trips to the end zone in three games to begin the season for Gibbs, who ran it in from 17 yards and one yard before hauling in a game-winning 11-yard toss from Jared Goff inside the final two minutes of the fourth quarter. Gibbs has added 463 yards from scrimmage to his ledger as well, more than earning his spot at the top of preseason draft boards. He'll look to keep rolling in a Week 4 road clash against the Panthers.

injuries.name: Thomas Harper
injuries.headline: The Lions placed Harper (ankle) on injured reserve Saturday.
injuries.notes: Harper has not been able to practice since sustaining an ankle injury during the Lions' Week 2 loss to the Bills. The safety departing for IR leaves the Lions' secondary dangerously low on defensive backs, now without Harper, Avonte Maddox (foot), Brian Branch (Achilles) and Kerby Joseph (knee). The Lions have elevated Jalen Mills from the practice squad to start at strong safety in Sunday's game against the Jets.

injuries.name: Tate Ratledge
injuries.headline: Ratledge (elbow) does not have any injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Jets, Tim Twentyman of the Lions' official site reports.
injuries.notes: Ratledge was limited in back-to-back practices to start Week 3 prep before upgrading to a full participant in Friday's session. With Christian Mahogany and Blake Miller also set to suit up, four-fifths of the starting Lions offensive line will be available to support backup center Juice Scruggs in Sunday's contest.

injuries.name: Blake Miller
injuries.headline: Miller (knee) does not have any injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Jets, Tim Twentyman of the Lions' official site reports.
injuries.notes: Miller was a limited participant in the first two practices of Week 3 prep before upgrading to full participation in Friday's session. The rookie first-rounder is set to suit up for his second NFL game after a brief week-long hiatus spent dealing with a knee injury.

injuries.name: Christian Mahogany
injuries.headline: Mahogany (hip) does not have any injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Jets, Tim Twentyman of the Lions' official site reports.
injuries.notes: Mahogany opened Week 3 prep with back-to-back limited practices before upgrading to a full participant in Friday's session. The starting left guard is set to suit up for Sunday's contest after missing the Lions' Week 2 loss to the Bills.

injuries.name: Avonte Maddox
injuries.headline: The Lions placed Maddox (foot) on injured reserve Tuesday.
injuries.notes: Maddox will miss the rest of the 2026 season due to a left foot injury he sustained in the Lions' Week 2 loss to the Bills. He'll shift his focus toward being fully healthy for the 2027 campaign, though he'll enter the offseason as an unrestricted free agent. With Maddox, Brian Branch (Achilles) and Kerby Joseph (knee) all sidelined, Thomas Harper and Chuck Clark will serve as Detroit's starting safeties for the time being.

injuries.name: Kevin Zeitler
injuries.headline: The Packers signed Zeitler to a one-year contract Wednesday, Rob Demovsky of ESPN.com reports.
injuries.notes: The contract is worth $4.05 million, with a maximum value of $5 million. It's another move the Packers are making to revamp their offensive line, as the team ranks last in the league in rushing yards per game (48.7). It's possible that Zeitler supplants Jacob Monk (quadriceps) for the starting job at right guard for Sunday's game against the Buccaneers.

injuries.name: Lukas Van Ness
injuries.headline: Van Ness (shoulder) was limited in Wednesday's practice.
injuries.notes: Van Ness presumably injured his shoulder during the Packers' 35-14 loss to the Falcons in Week 3, when he logged four tackles (one solo). He'll have two more opportunities to increase his practice participation and avoid an injury designation for Sunday's road tilt against Tampa Bay.

injuries.name: Edgerrin Cooper
injuries.headline: Cooper (concussion/shoulder) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice.
injuries.notes: Cooper sustained a concussion during the Packers' Week 3 loss to the Falcons, and he also appears to have picked up a shoulder injury. Even if he practices in full over the coming days, he would need to pass an evaluation by an independent neurologist in order to clear the league's concussion protocol ahead of Sunday's road game against the Buccaneers.

injuries.name: Karl Brooks
injuries.headline: questionable
injuries.notes: questionable

injuries.name: Skyy Moore
injuries.headline: Coach Matt LaFleur said Wednesday that Moore will be the next man up at wide receiver after it was announced Jayden Reed (neck) will undergo season-ending surgery, Ryan Wood of USA Today reports.
injuries.notes: With Reed out last Thursday night against the Falcons, Moore played 34 of 66 offensive snaps and ran 27 routes on Jordan Love's 55 dropbacks. Moore caught three of seven targets for 31 yards. He's expected to fight for scraps behind all three of Matthew Golden, Christian Watson and Tucker Kraft in the pecking order for targets.

injuries.name: Jayden Reed
injuries.headline: The Packers are expected to place Reed (neck) on injured reserve Wednesday, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
injuries.notes: Reed remains without a clear timeline for a return after sustaining a neck injury that resulted in a brief stay in the hospital in the Packers' Week 2 win over the Jets, but his impending move to IR ensures that he'll remain out for at least Green Bay's next four games. With Reed out indefinitely, second-year player Matthew Golden should be further insulated as the Packers' No. 2 receiver, while the likes of Skyy Moore, Bo Melton and J. Michael Sturdivant should see more involvement in three- and four-wide sets.

injuries.name: Aaron Banks
injuries.headline: questionable
injuries.notes: questionable

injuries.name: Warren Brinson
injuries.headline: questionable
injuries.notes: questionable

injuries.name: Anthony Campbell
injuries.headline: questionable
injuries.notes: questionable

injuries.name: Zach Bako-Bewele
injuries.headline: The Packers placed Bako-Bewele (knee) on injured reserve Monday, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
injuries.notes: Bako-Bewele sustained a complete tear of his right patellar tendon in the Packers' Week 2 overtime win over the Jets. The right tackle is out for the season and has thus been placed on injured reserve. Laken Tomlinson is the new reserve offensive lineman for the team, and Anthony Belton is expected to be the starting right tackle for the remainder of the 2026 season.

injuries.name: Micah Parsons
injuries.headline: Packers head coach Matt LaFleur said Monday that Parsons (knee) hasn't experienced any setbacks but won't be cleared to practice this week, Rob Demovsky of ESPN.com reports.
injuries.notes: Because he was placed on the PUP list July 28, Parsons has been eligible to resume practicing since Week 2, but the Packers aren't yet ready to open his 21-day evaluation window. Parsons had previously told Ryan Wood of USA Today that the Packers' Oct. 18 game against the Cowboys was a "very realistic" target for him to make his 2026 debut, but in order for that to happen, the star edge rusher would likely have to start practicing by next week.

injuries.name: Evan Williams
injuries.headline: Williams recorded 10 tackles (four solo) during Thursday's 35-14 loss to Atlanta.
injuries.notes: Williams reached double-digit tackles for a second consecutive week, with the third-year safety co-leading the Packers in stops in Thursday's loss. He's up to 27 tackles (17 solo) and two pass defenses through three regular-season games and leads Green Bay in stops, with linebacker Zaire Franklin and Edgerrin Cooper tied for the second-most total tackles on the Packers (21 each).

injuries.name: Xavier McKinney
injuries.headline: McKinney recorded five tackles (four solo) and one interception during the Packers' 35-14 loss to the Falcons on Thursday.
injuries.notes: It looked like the Packers' defense was going to make Thursday night a miserable 2026 debut for Michael Penix after the Falcons' QB was picked off by McKinney on the fourth play of Atlanta's first drive of the game, although Green Bay's offense was unable to capitalize on the takeaway. It was only two seasons ago that McKinney led the NFL with eight interceptions, though he's logged three picks across 19 regular-season games since the beginning of the 2025 campaign. He's opened the 2026 campaign with 12 tackles (nine solo) and one interception, and he's behind pace for the third 100th-tackle season of his seven-year NFL career.

injuries.name: Zaire Franklin
injuries.headline: Franklin tallied 10 tackles (three solo) during the Packers' 35-14 loss to the Falcons on Thursday.
injuries.notes: Franklin played every single defensive snap for the third week in a row and finished Thursday's game tied with Evan Williams for most tackles on the Packers. It was the first time this season that Franklin logged double-digit stops after doing so five times across 17 regular-season games in 2025. The veteran linebacker is up to 21 tackles (seven solo) and is on pace to crack the 100-tackle mark for a fifth consecutive year.

injuries.name: Jonnu Smith
injuries.headline: Smith caught two passes on three targets for 16 yards during Thursday's 35-14 loss to Atlanta.
injuries.notes: Smith was able to contribute to the Packers' passing attack Thursday after failing to log a target in Week 2 against the Jets .His 22 snaps on offense were second-most among Green Bay tight ends behind Tucker Kraft (50) and ahead of both Mark Redman (eight) and Josh Whyle (one). Smith will take a 4-66-0 receiving line (on six targets) into the Packers' Week 4 road tilt against the Buccaneers on Sunday, Oct. 4.

injuries.name: J. Michael Sturdivant
injuries.headline: Sturdivant tallied three catches on as many targets for 22 yards during the Packers' 35-14 loss to the Falcons on Thursday.
injuries.notes: Sturdivant's nine-yard catch late in the third quarter was the first of his NFL career. He went on to haul in two more passes of three and 10 yards in the fourth quarter and finished Thursday's contest having played 21 of the Packers' 66 snaps on offense (31.8 percent). Most of that playing time came when Green Bay was facing a large deficit, but Sturdivant figures to see at least some involvement in the offense given the uncertainty around the status of Jayden Reed (neck) for the rest of the 2026 season.

injuries.name: Bo Melton
injuries.headline: Melton logged 21 of 66 offensive snaps during Thursday's 35-14 loss to the Falcons but did not catch his only target. He also recorded two tackles and turned two kickoff returns into 46 yards.
injuries.notes: Melton played a total of 42 snaps Thursday, split evenly between special teams and offense, and his offensive snap count was fourth-most among Packers wide receivers. Despite the spike in playing time, Melton shouldn't factor into the team's offensive game plan unless a larger role opens up for the 2022 seventh-rounder due to the absence of one or multiple wide receivers.

injuries.name: Chris Brooks
injuries.headline: Brooks caught his only target for four yards and added a tackle on special teams during the Packers' 35-14 loss to the Falcons on Thursday.
injuries.notes: Brooks totalled 40 yards on 11 carries through the first two games of the regular season. However, he wasn't involved in the rushing game Thursday, though Kaleb Johnson and MarShawn Lloyd combined for only 17 yards on eight carries. Part of the Packers' struggles in the running game has to do with injuries to the offensive line, though it's hard to trust Brooks, Johnson or Lloyd for consistent production, even if Josh Jacobs (personal) continues to remain on the Commissioner's Exempt List. The Packers hit the road for a Week 4 tilt against the Buccaneers on Sunday, Oct. 4.

injuries.name: Kaleb Johnson
injuries.headline: Johnson tallied four carries for six yards and gathered in one of three targets for 10 yards during Thursday's 35-14 loss to the Falcons.
injuries.notes: The Packers backfield mustered just eight rushes (MarShawn Lloyd had the other four) on a night in which the team was increasingly in catch-up mode, spurring 53 pass attempts from QB Jordan Love. After Johnson was dealt to Green Bay from Pittsburgh on Aug. 30, he didn't receive a snap on offense in Week 1, but his offensive snap share increased from 27 percent in Week 2 to 36 percent in Week 3, while Lloyd's share has gone in the opposite direction, and Chris Brooks' has remained relatively stable. Because the team's RBs have mustered just 146 rushing yards (3.0 YPC) through three games, none of the trio are particularly intriguing for fantasy purposes at the moment, especially behind a makeshift O-line, but Johnson's elevated sway could mean that a stash eventually yields positive results.

injuries.name: Laken Tomlinson
injuries.headline: The Packers signed Tomlinson off the Cowboys' practice squad Saturday, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
injuries.notes: Tomlinson spent the offseason with the Cowboys' practice squad after being waived by the Texans in December. The offensive guard will now add depth to an injury-stricken Packers offensive line.

injuries.name: Jacob Monk
injuries.headline: Monk picked up an undisclosed injury toward the tail end of the Packers' 35-14 loss to the Falcons on Thursday, Rob Demovsky of ESPN.com reports.
injuries.notes: Monk was attended to by medical staff during the two-minute warning of the fourth quarter. It's unclear what type of injury he's working through, though the Packers should have an update on the third-year offensive lineman once he undergoes more tests.

injuries.name: MarShawn Lloyd
injuries.headline: Lloyd rushed four times for 11 yards and brought in two of three targets for seven yards in the Packers' 35-14 loss to the Falcons on Thursday.
injuries.notes: The inefficiency reflected in his final line underscores the type of season it's been so far for Lloyd, who's tried in vain to serve as a serviceable replacement for Josh Jacobs (personal) while he remains on the Commissioner's Exempt List. Lloyd's rushing opportunities were limited Thursday largely due to game script, but the 2024 third-round pick is averaging just 3.0 yards per carry through three games and has complemented it with an unremarkable 4-13-0 line through the air. Lloyd, Chris Brooks and Kaleb Johnson will continue to share the Packers' backfield workload in a Week 4 road matchup against the Buccaneers on Sunday, Oct. 4.

injuries.name: Tucker Kraft
injuries.headline: Kraft secured four of eight targets for 26 yards in the Packers' 35-14 loss to the Falcons on Thursday. He also recovered a fumble.
injuries.notes: Kraft finished third in targets and catches on the night for the Packers, but in uncharacteristic fashion, the field-stretching tight end was limited to a short-area role. He made an impressively rapid recovery from last year's torn ACL, which he suffered Week 9 of the 2025 campaign, to open the season in his customary No. 1 tight end role. However, he's mustered a modest a 9-106-0 line on 17 targets through three games heading into a Week 4 road matchup against the Buccaneers on Sunday, Oct. 4.

injuries.name: Trey Smack
injuries.headline: Smack went 0-for-1 on field-goal tries and 2-for-2 on extra-point attempts in Thursday's 35-14 loss to the Falcons.
injuries.notes: The kicker's 47-yard attempt in the second quarter was blocked. It was Smack's first miss on a field-goal try this season, and it probably wasn't his fault. The rookie has, however, missed an extra point as well.

injuries.name: Jordan Love
injuries.headline: Love completed 28 of 53 passes for 312 yards with two touchdowns and one interception and rushed once for no gain in the Packers' 35-14 loss to the Falcons on Thursday. He also committed a fumble recovered by Green Bay.
injuries.notes: While Love's final line was certainly a fantasy-friendly one, it was largely the byproduct of Green Bay being playing catch-up in the fourth quarter and the Falcons showing a willingness to give up some yardage while in prevent mode. Love spread the ball around to nine different targets on the night, and he connected with Christian Watson (four yards) and Matthew Golden (15 yards ) -- who were his two most prolific options by far -- for his pair of touchdown passes. Love's one interception closed out the Packers' final drive with the game already out of reach, but the embattled veteran signal-caller does head into a Week 4 road matchup against the Buccaneers on Sunday, Oct. 4 averaging 281.3 passing yards per game while sporting a 6:2 TD:INT.

injuries.name: Nico Collins
injuries.headline: Collins (hamstring) is taking part in Thursday's padded practice, DJ Bien-Aime of ESPN.com reports.
injuries.notes: After missing the Texans' last two games due a Grade 1 hamstring strain, Collins returned to practice Wednesday as a limited participant. The Texans will release their second Week 4 injury report later Thursday, but Collins appears poised to at least maintain limited participation. If he can make it through the practice week no worse for the wear, the star wideout looks to be trending toward a return to the lineup this Sunday versus the Cowboys.

injuries.name: Reed Blankenship
injuries.headline: Blankenship posted nine tackles (five solo) and two pass defenses (including one interception) during the Texans' 19-17 loss to the Colts in Week 3.
injuries.notes: Blankenship recorded his first interception of the season early in the third quarter, when he jumped in front of a floating pass from Daniel Jones intended for Josh Downs deep in Houston's territory. It was Blankenship's second interception since the start of the 2025 campaign after recording a career-high four picks across 15 regular-season games with the Eagles in 2024. His presence in the secondary will be crucial in Week 4 when the Texans welcome in the Cowboys, whose offense ranks in the top 10 in the league in points per game (29.3).

injuries.name: Mario Edwards Jr.
injuries.headline: The Texans placed Edwards on injured reserve Wednesday.
injuries.notes: Edwards suffered a torn ACL in Sunday's 19-17 loss to the Colts and will miss the rest of the 2026 season. The defensive tackle has been moved to injured reserve and will no longer take up a spot on the Texans' 53-man roster.

injuries.name: Chris Braswell
injuries.headline: The Texans signed Braswell from the practice squad to the active roster Wednesday.
injuries.notes: Braswell played 17 regular-season games with the Buccaneers in 2025, logging 30 tackles (21 solo), including 1.0 sacks, over 281 defensive snaps and 204 special-teams snaps.  The defensive end will now provide additional depth to a Texans line that may be without Will Anderson (ankle) and Jadeveon Clowney (knee) in Sunday's matchup against the Cowboys.

injuries.name: Will Anderson Jr.
injuries.headline: Anderson (ankle) was limited in Wednesday's practice.
injuries.notes: Anderson may have injured his ankle during the Texans' Week 3 loss to the Colts, when he logged seven tackles (five solo), including 2.5 sacks, one forced fumble and one fumble recovery. He's been a key piece to the Texans' defense since entering the league in 2023 as a first-round pick, and if he cannot play against the Cowboys on Sunday, then Jadeveon Clowney (knee) and Dominique Robinson would both be in line for more snaps at defensive end opposite Danielle Hunter. Anderson will have two more opportunities to log a full practice and avoid an injury designation for Week 4.

injuries.name: Azeez Al-Shaair
injuries.headline: Coach DeMeco Ryans said Wednesday that Al-Shaair is "week-to-week" with the groin injury he suffered during Sunday's game at Indianapolis, Jonathan M. Alexander of the Houston Chronicle reports.
injuries.notes: Al-Shaair was able to return to action in Week 3 after checking out of the game with the groin injury, but his outlook for Week 4 is now up in the air. He'll probably have to practice in full Thursday or Friday to avoid carrying an injury designation into the weekend.

injuries.name: Kayshon Boutte
injuries.headline: Boutte hauled in both of his targets for 21 yards during the Texans' 19-17 loss to the Colts on Sunday.
injuries.notes: For a second consecutive week, Boutte operated in an elevated role on offense due to the absence of Nico Collins (hamstring). Boutte's 37 offensive snaps actually led all Texans wide receivers, but he didn't see a target from C.J. Stroud until late in the fourth quarter, setting up a Woody Marks one-yard rushing touchdown. Per Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston, head coach DeMeco Ryans expressed optimism Monday that Collins would be back for Week 4 against the Cowboys, which would return Boutte to a secondary role.

injuries.name: Dare Ogunbowale
injuries.headline: The Texans signed Ogunbowale off the Raiders' practice squad Tuesday.
injuries.notes: Ogunbowale signed with the Raiders' practice squad after being trimmed from the team's roster during final cuts. The running back now returns to Houston, where he participated in 129 offensive snaps and 281 special-teams snaps over 17 regular-season games in 2025.

injuries.name: Woody Marks
injuries.headline: Marks turned five carries into 15 yards and a touchdown and hauled in his lone target for six yards during the Texans' 19-17 loss to the Colts on Sunday. He also returned two kickoffs for 52 yards.
injuries.notes: Marks and David Montgomery both averaged only 3.0 yards per carry during Sunday's loss, though the former found the end zone for the first time this season on a one-yard rushing touchdown late in the fourth quarter. Marks' 20 snaps on offense was behind Montgomery's 34, though neither running back has found much success in the rushing attack in each of the Texans' last two games. Houston will look to avoid an 0-4 start to the season in Week 4 against Dallas.

injuries.name: Ka'imi Fairbairn
injuries.headline: Fairbairn connected on a 24-yard field goal and both of his extra-point tries in Sunday's 19-17 loss to the Colts.
injuries.notes: The kicker made the most of his opportunities Sunday. He just didn't have very many, which has been a theme this season, as the Texans have given him just six PATs through three contests.

injuries.name: David Montgomery
injuries.headline: Montgomery rushed 11 times for 33 yards while catching both of his targets for 15 yards in Sunday's 19-17 loss to the Colts.
injuries.notes: Montgomery was stuffed for no gain on a fourth-and-1 in Colts territory in the first quarter, and he watched Woody Marks convert a one-yard rushing touchdown in the fourth quarter. Marks has 29 touches to Montgomery's 44 through three games, and it's concerning that Montgomery isn't monopolizing short-yardage opportunities after scoring three short TDs in the season opener. Neither running back has found much running room behind Houston's underwhelming offensive line, and Montgomery is averaging just 2.8 yards per carry heading into a Week 4 home game against the Cowboys.

injuries.name: C.J. Stroud
injuries.headline: Stroud completed 16 of 27 passes for 167 yards and a touchdown while rushing twice for 10 yards in Sunday's 19-17 loss to the Colts.
injuries.notes: Houston's offense struggled for a second consecutive week in the absence of top wide receiver Nico Collins (hamstring). Stroud threw a one-yard touchdown pass to Foster Moreau in the second quarter, but the Texans dropped to 0-3 for the second consecutive season. Houston bounced back to finish 12-5 in the 2025 regular season, but climbing out of an early hole again won't be easy, especially with the offensive line struggling to create running lanes or protect Stroud, who has been sacked 10 times through three games. Stroud will try to get off the schneid in an all-Texas Week 4 home game against the Cowboys.

injuries.name: Dalton Schultz
injuries.headline: Schultz is in line to see an increase in targets for the second consecutive game in Sunday's Week 3 matchup against the Colts due to Nico Collins (hamstring) being ruled inactive for the contest.
injuries.notes: The veteran tight end recorded a career-high 140 receiving yards on 12 receptions (14 targets) in the Week 2 loss to the Bengals, a game that marked Collins' first absence of the season. The fact the Texans were in catch-up mode and the Bengals defense tends to funnel production to tight ends were both factors in Schultz's atypical numbers, but Collins' second consecutive absence does create the opportunity for another busy afternoon as Houston aims to secure its first win. Additionally, the Colts have been fairly generous to tight ends over the first two games of the season, surrendering a 75.0 percent catch rate and 11.1 yards per reception and tying for the third-most receptions (15) given up to the position among teams that have played two games thus far.

injuries.name: Xavier Hutchinson
injuries.headline: Hutchinson is in line to serve as the Texans' No. 1 receiver for the second consecutive game in Sunday's Week 3 matchup against the Colts due to Nico Collins (hamstring) being ruled inactive for the contest.
injuries.notes: Hutchinson was in the same slotting for the Week 2 loss to the Bengals, a game in which he saw nine targets on 51 routes run but converted only three into catches. He ostensibly has a more palatable matchup Sunday, as the Colts have surrendered an elevated 72.7 percent catch rate and 17.9 yards per reception to wide receivers, along with three touchdowns, over the first two games.

injuries.name: Jake Hummel
injuries.headline: The Texans placed Hummel (groin) on injured reserve Saturday, Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston reports.
injuries.notes: Hummel has not practiced since sustaining a groin injury during the Texans' Week 1 loss to the Bills. The linebacker will now miss at least four games on IR before becoming eligible to return to the team's active roster. While Hummel is absent, Jake Hansen should continue to start alongside Azeez Al-Shaair and Aiden Fisher at linebacker.

injuries.name: DeForest Buckner
injuries.headline: Buckner registered seven tackles (two solo), including 1.5 sacks, during the Colts' 19-17 win over the Texans in Week 3.
injuries.notes: Buckner was responsible for two of the Colts' three sacks on C.J. Stroud in Sunday's win. The veteran defensive lineman got to Stroud early in the first quarter for a four-yard sack before Buckner combined with Adetomiwa Adebawore for a two-yard takedown of the Texans QB late in the second quarter. Buckner has logged at least 0.5 sacks in each of the first three games of the regular season and is up to 3.0 sacks on the year, which leads the Colts and is tied for eighth in the NFL.

injuries.name: Mo Alie-Cox
injuries.headline: Alie-Cox (illness) did not participate at practice Wednesday.
injuries.notes: The nature of Alie-Cox's ailment is unknown, so it's not clear whether his availability for Week 4 is in any jeopardy. If he can return to practice Thursday or Friday, he'll put himself in a good position to suit up Sunday against the Commanders in London.

injuries.name: Ashton Dulin
injuries.headline: Dulin (ankle) is not practicing Wednesday, James Boyd of The Athletic reports.
injuries.notes: Dulin has missed the past two games, and his practice week ahead of Week 4 is off on the wrong foot. With Alec Pierce (heel/IR) also out last Sunday against the Texans, the Colts used a three-wide set of Laquon Treadwell, Josh Downs and Keenan Allen.

injuries.name: Alec Pierce
injuries.headline: Colts head coach Shane Steichen reiterated Monday that Pierce didn't undergo surgery on his left heel and is continuing to rehab the injury, James Boyd of The Athletic reports.
injuries.notes: Ian Rapoport of NFL Network had previously relayed last week that Pierce would avoid another procedure after aggravating his surgically repaired heel in a Sept. 20 loss to the Chiefs, but that report was called into question after the wideout was spotted Sunday moving around the Colts locker room with the aid of a scooter while he had a cast on his left foot. Apparently, Pierce is using the cast for extra protection and using the scooter to keep weight off the injured foot, which he hopes will accelerate the healing process. Pierce is without a timeline to return to game action, but he'll have to miss at least three more contests after landing on injured reserve over the weekend.

injuries.name: Josh Downs
injuries.headline: Downs caught five of 11 targets for 77 yards during Sunday's 19-17 win over Houston.
injuries.notes: Downs garnered the most targets on the team, narrowly edging out tight end Tyler Warren (10), while his 77 receiving yards led the way for Indianapolis. With Alec Pierce (heel) sidelined for the foreseeable future, Downs appears to have taken command as the team's No. 1 option at wide receiver. Over three games to open the regular season, the wideout has reeled in 14 of 24 targets for 186 yards, and he'll look to secure his first touchdown of the season in Week 4 against the Commanders.

injuries.name: Keenan Allen
injuries.headline: Allen caught six of nine targets for 63 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 19-17 win over the Texans.
injuries.notes: Allen was able to take advantage of the absence of Alec Pierce (heel) in Week 3, matching his season-high six receptions while notching his first touchdown of the year in the second quarter on a six-yard pass from Daniel Jones. With Pierce set to miss extended time, Allen will have a chance to carve out a significant role for himself as a reliable option for Indianapolis.

injuries.name: Spencer Shrader
injuries.headline: Shrader made all four of his field-goal attempts while connecting on his lone extra-point try during the Colts' 19-17 win over the Texans on Sunday.
injuries.notes: It looked like Shrader was going to observe Sunday's contest from the sidelines after he sustained a groin injury during pregame warmups. However, Shrader was cleared to attempt a field goal in the first quarter, and two of his four made field goals came from 50-plus yards, including a 53-yarder with 19 seconds left in the fourth quarter to give the Colts their first win of the season. Shrader has made all eight of his field-goal attempts (including three from 50-plus yards) and six of seven extra-point tries through the first three games of the regular season.

injuries.name: Tyler Warren
injuries.headline: Warren caught nine of 10 targets for 55 yards and added a two-yard run in Sunday's 19-17 win over the Texans.
injuries.notes: Warren failed to score a touchdown for the first time this season but set a new career high in catches while seeing plenty of involvement as a pass catcher in the absence of wide receiver Alec Pierce (heel), who was placed on IR after exiting early in the Week 2 loss to Kansas City. The second-year tight end is poised to maintain a prominent role when the Colts travel to London to face the Commanders in Week 4.

injuries.name: Daniel Jones
injuries.headline: Jones completed 24 of 36 passes for 235 yards, one touchdown and one interception in Sunday's 19-17 win over the Texans. He also rushed three times for five yards and fumbled three times, losing two.
injuries.notes: Jones led the Colts to their first win of the season despite the absence of wide receiver Alec Pierce (heel), who was placed on IR earlier in the week. Tyler Warren (nine), Keenan Allen (six) and Josh Downs (five) accounted for 20 of Jones' 24 completions, including a six-yard touchdown pass to Allen in the second quarter. Ball security has been an issue for Jones, who has three interceptions and two lost fumbles through three games, but the Colts finally have something to feel good about, having notched their first win since Week 10 of last season ahead of a Week 4 trip across the pond to face the Commanders in London.

injuries.name: Jonathan Taylor
injuries.headline: Taylor rushed 23 times for 68 yards while catching two of three targets for four yards in Sunday's 19-17 win over the Texans.
injuries.notes: Taylor racked up 25 touches as the Colts notched their first win of the season, but he failed to find much running room against Houston's stout front. He finished with a season-low 72 scrimmage yards and failed to score after opening the season with a pair of two-touchdown performances. The workhorse running back is averaging 25 touches per game heading into the Colts' Week 4 trip to London to take on the Commanders at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, and Taylor's poised for another busy outing in the overseas clash between 1-2 teams.

injuries.name: Laiatu Latu
injuries.headline: Latu (chest) has returned to Sunday's game against the Texans, Kevin Bowen of 107.5 The Fan Indianapolis reports.
injuries.notes: Latu left for the locker room in the first half due to a chest injury, but he was back on the field for the Colts in the third quarter. Latu has yet to record a tackle.

injuries.name: Charvarius Ward
injuries.headline: Ward (groin) is active for Sunday's game against the Texans.
injuries.notes: Ward tweaked his groin during the Colts' overtime loss to the Chiefs in Week 2. He drew the questionable tag for Sunday's AFC South tilt following a DNP-LP-FP practice log, and the veteran cornerback has been given the green light to play after going through pregame warmups. Cam Taylor-Britt will operate in a depth role behind Ward and Sauce Gardner for Week 3.

injuries.name: Anthony Gould
injuries.headline: The Colts signed Gould from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday.
injuries.notes: Gould was elevated to the active roster for the Colts' Week 2 overtime loss to the Chiefs. The wide receiver played nine special-teams snaps in the loss, not touching the field for the offense. Now a member of the active roster, Gould will likely continue in his role as a special-teamer due to the absence of Ashton Dulin (ankle).

injuries.name: Laquon Treadwell
injuries.headline: Treadwell caught all three of his targets for 61 yards and made one tackle on kick coverage in Sunday's 33-30 overtime loss to the Chiefs.
injuries.notes: Treadwell played 48 of the Colts' 65 offensive snaps due to the injuries to Alec Pierce (heel, in-game injury) and Ashton Dulin (ankle). The wide receiver also logged 17 special-teams snaps, stepping up for the team in multiple phases even though it ultimately fell in a close game.

injuries.name: Micheal Clemons
injuries.headline: Clemons (toe) was placed on injured reserve by the Colts on Tuesday.
injuries.notes: Clemons sustained a toe injury in the team's 33-30 overtime loss against Kansas City on Sunday night, and he will now be forced to miss at least four contests while recovering. His absence won't have a major impact on the team's defensive approach.

injuries.name: Seth McGowan
injuries.headline: McGowan rushed twice for zero yards and had two kickoff returns for 58 yards in Sunday's 33-30 overtime loss to the Chiefs.
injuries.notes: McGowan saw just four offensive snaps in the contest, touchding the ball on half of them. The seventh-round rookie did not make a strong impression against the Chiefs' defensive line, but he proved useful on special teams with a 29-yard average on kickoff returns.

injuries.name: Anthony Richardson Sr.
injuries.headline: Richardson (groin) was a full participant at practice Thursday.
injuries.notes: Richardson didn't practice Wednesday due to a groin injury but resumed practicing without limitations Thursday, suggesting the backup QB isn't in danger of missing Sunday night's game at Kansas City. Daniel Jones struggled in the Week 1 loss to the Ravens but remains locked in as the starter for the Colts.

injuries.name: Cam Taylor-Britt
injuries.headline: Taylor-Britt's one-game suspension for violating the league's personal conduct policy was lifted Monday, Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston reports.
injuries.notes: Taylor-Britt was forced to sit out Indianapolis' Week 1 loss to the Ravens, but he's now on track to be available for Week 2 at Kansas City. He figures to play in a rotational role in the Colts' secondary in 2026.

injuries.name: LeQuint Allen Jr.
injuries.headline: Allen (hip) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice.
injuries.notes: Allen logged limited participation throughout the Jaguars' Week 3 prep practices and was ultimately cleared of any injury designation ahead of the team's Week 3 win over the Patriots. The No. 3 running back could be set to replicate the same practice pattern in Week 4 prep and once again be cleared ahead of Sunday's game against the Bengals.

injuries.name: Jakobi Meyers
injuries.headline: Meyers (thumb) was limited in Wednesday's practice.
injuries.notes: Meyers dealt with the thumb issue last week but ultimately didn't carry an injury designation into last Sunday's blowout win over the Patriots, where the veteran wideout hung a 7-64-1 receiving line on eight targets. Playing as a clear starter ahead of Brian Thomas, Meyers has 10 catches for 132 yards and two touchdowns on 11 targets through three games this season.

injuries.name: Josh Cameron
injuries.headline: Cameron secured one of two targets for a 12-yard touchdown in Sunday's 35-6 win over the Patriots.
injuries.notes: Cameron got the scoring started early in the second quarter, catching the first of Trevor Lawrence's three touchdown passes. The rookie ended up finishing with 23 offensive snaps against New England, the same amount as Brian Thomas but behind Parker Washington and Jakobi Meyers, who both played 50 snaps on offense. Cameron could be pushing Thomas for the No. 3 receiver role in Jacksonville.

injuries.name: Travis Hunter
injuries.headline: Hunter played five offensive snaps in Sunday's 35-6 win over the Patriots.
injuries.notes: He failed to see a target in the passing game for the second straight week and is clearly not in the team's plans on that side of the ball with everyone healthy at wideout. Hunter would likely need one or even two injuries ahead of him on the depth chart to see significant snaps on offense. On defense against New England, Hunter logged four tackles (three solo) and one pass breakup, including his first career regular-season interception.

injuries.name: Brenton Strange
injuries.headline: Strange caught three of five targets for 32 yards during the Jaguars' 35-6 win over the Patriots on Sunday.
injuries.notes: Most of Strange's production came on a 23-yard catch midway through the second quarter, which put the Jaguars just outside the red zone and helped lead to a 10-yard touchdown pass from Trevor Lawrence to Jakobi Meyers five plays later. Strange finished Sunday's game tied for the second-most targets and catches and third in receiving yards behind Meyers (64) and Parker Washington (40). Strange is off to a somewhat slow start to the 2026 season, though he's competing against Meyers, Washington and Brian Thomas for targets in the passing game. Strange will take a 7-72-1 line (on 10 targets) into a Week 4 road clash against the Bengals.

injuries.name: Chris Rodriguez Jr.
injuries.headline: Rodriguez turned eight carries into 37 yards and a touchdown during the Jaguars' 35-6 win over the Patriots on Sunday.
