injuries.name: Daniel Carlson
injuries.headline: Carlson made three of his four PATs and attempted no field goals in the Saints' 35-27 loss to the Raiders on Sunday.
injuries.notes: Carlson's missed PAT on the Saints' second drive of the contest was blocked by Thomas Booker. The missed point was relevant, impacting head coach Kellen Moore's decisions throughout the rest of a contest that was ultimately decided by eight points. Carlson moves to 7-of-8 on PATs and remains 4-of-5 on field-goal attempts through three regular-season games.

injuries.name: Travis Etienne Jr.
injuries.headline: Saints head coach Kellen Moore said that Etienne will have some "time lost" due to the hamstring injury he sustained in Sunday's 35-27 loss to the Raiders, Mike Triplett of NewOrleans.Football reports.
injuries.notes: Moore noted that a specific timeline for Etienne's return hasn't been established, making it uncertain whether or not the running back will be able to avoid a stint on injured reserve. At the very least, Etienne will be sidelined for the Saints' Week 4 game against the Falcons next Monday, which likely paves the way for Alvin Kamara to take on an expanded profile in the backfield after working in a complementary role the previous two weeks. Reserve backs Kendre Miller and CJ Donaldson also should be in store for more opportunities for however long Etienne is out.
injuries.vacated_opportunity_note: Primary beneficiary of vacated early-down carries & red-zone volume if starter is sidelined.

injuries.name: Noah Fant
injuries.headline: Fant caught all four of his targets for 33 yards and two touchdowns during Sunday's 35-27 loss to Las Vegas.
injuries.notes: Fant made the most of his opportunities, connecting with quarterback Tyler Shough for a three-yard touchdown in the second quarter and a 16-yard score in the third quarter. The tight end is the No. 2 option behind Juwan Johnson at his position, but Fant has still caught eight of 12 targets for 66 yards and three scores over the first three games this year.

injuries.name: Juwan Johnson
injuries.headline: Johnson caught all eight of his targets for 53 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 35-27 loss to the Raiders.
injuries.notes: The veteran tight end continues to have an impressive start to the season, hauling in TD strikes of one and two yards from Tyler Shough. but Johnson had a tough end to his day as he fumbled to end the Saints' final possession while they were trying to mount a comeback late in the fourth quarter. Johnson has put together a 15-173-3 line on 19 targets through three games, and he'll look to atone for his miscue in a Week 4 home tilt against the Falcons.

injuries.name: Alvin Kamara
injuries.headline: Kamara carried the ball nine times for 36 yards and caught his only target for five yards in Sunday's 35-27 loss to the Raiders.
injuries.notes: The veteran RB once again took a back seat to Travis Etienne to begin the game, but that changed after the former Jaguar aggravated a hamstring strain and left the game in the third quarter. Over the Saints' last five possessions, Kamara split the workload in the backfield with Kendre Miller, getting six touches to Miller's five. The severity of Etienne's injury isn't yet clear, but if he misses significant time, Kamara and Miller would likely continue working in tandem, with rookie CJ Donaldson also potentially mixing in as a short-yardage option.

injuries.name: Tyler Shough
injuries.headline: Shough completed 29 of 42 passes for 255 yards and four touchdowns with one interception in Sunday's 35-27 loss to the Raiders. He added 36 rushing yards on his lone carry but also lost two fumbles.
injuries.notes: The second-year QB was dynamic once again, tossing two TDs each to tight ends Juwan Johnson and Noah Fant, but protection issues in the absence of left tackle Kelvin Banks (ankle) ending up proving costly as all four of the Saints' fourth-quarter possessions ended in turnovers, causing them to squander a 27-22 lead. Shough has thrown eight touchdowns through three games but has also given the ball away six times (three INTs and three lost fumbles), and he'll try to clean up those issues in Week 4 at home against the Falcons.

injuries.name: Chris Olave
injuries.headline: Olave caught nine of 13 targets for 107 yards in Sunday's 35-27 loss to the Raiders.
injuries.notes: The fifth-year wideout led the Saints in catches, targets and receiving yards, but all four of Tyler Shough's TD passes went to tight ends instead of Olave. Olave has hauled in more than 100 yards in two of three games to begin the season, amassing a 27-375-1 line on 36 targets, and he'll look to keep rolling in Week 4 at home against the Falcons.

injuries.name: Anfernee Jennings
injuries.headline: Jennings has a knee injury and is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Raiders.
injuries.notes: The linebacker recorded three tackles (two solo) and a pass breakup before exiting. Jennings played more on special teams than defense in New Orleans' first two games.

injuries.name: Carl Granderson
injuries.headline: Granderson (ankle) has returned to Sunday's contest against the Raiders, Ross Jackson of WWL Louisiana reports.
injuries.notes: Granderson was briefly sidelined with an ankle injury that he suffered in the third quarter, but he has now returned to action. The 29-year-old is back in his starting role as a weak-side linebacker for New Orleans.

injuries.name: Pete Werner
injuries.headline: Werner (neck) is questionable to return to Sunday's contest against the Raiders, Matthew Paras of The New Orleans Times-Picayune reports.
injuries.notes: Werner suffered a stinger in the first half, and his status for the rest of the game is now in question. In his absence, Isaiah Stalbird and Danny Stutsman are two candidates to see an increase in workload at inside linebacker.

injuries.name: Zach Wilson
injuries.headline: Wilson (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the emergency third quarterback against the Raiders on Sunday.
injuries.notes: For a third consecutive week, Wilson will be the Saints' emergency QB3, meaning he cannot play Sunday unless both Tyler Shough and Spencer Rattler leave the game due to injury, illness or ejection.

injuries.name: Kelvin Banks Jr.
injuries.headline: Banks (ankle) underwent surgery this week, Katherine Terrell of ESPN.com reports.
injuries.notes: While head coach Kellen Moore indicated that the procedure went well, Banks will remain on injured reserve for the foreseeable future. As a result, Mason Murphy should continue to be more involved.

injuries.name: Kendre Miller
injuries.headline: Miller (illness) doesn't carry an injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Raiders.
injuries.notes: Miller was under the weather Thursday, keeping him off the practice field. However, he was a full participant Friday. Miller was a healthy scratch for the 24-17 win over Baltimore in Week 2, meaning he is in danger of suffering the same fate versus Las Vegas, though his services may be needed on special teams with WR Barion Brown (hamstring) ruled out. With that in mind, if Miller is inactive, that would likely mean more work for Alvin Kamara and CJ Donaldson behind Travis Etienne.

injuries.name: Jonas Sanker
injuries.headline: Sanker (knee) was a full participant in Thursday's practice, Mike Triplett of NewOrleans.Football reports.
injuries.notes: Sanker had limited practice participation Wednesday seemingly as a precautionary measure, and his return to a full session Thursday puts the second-year defensive back on track to play Sunday against Las Vegas. Sanker has 13 tackles (10 solo) through two regular-season games.

injuries.name: Chase Young
injuries.headline: Young (calf) was a full participant in Thursday's practice, Mike Triplett of NewOrleans.Football reports.
injuries.notes: Young opened Week 3 prep as a limited participant in Wednesday's practice due to a calf injury, but his full session Thursday puts the seventh-year pass rusher on track to play against the Raiders on Sunday. Young has two tackles (one solo), including 1.5 sacks, and one pass defense through the first two games of the regular season.

injuries.name: Isaiah Stalbird
injuries.headline: Stalbird (shoulder) was a full participant at the Saints' practice Wednesday.
injuries.notes: Stalbird was unavailable for the team's 24-17 win over the Ravens in Week 2 due to a shoulder injury, but he now appears to be back to full health. The 26-year-old will be back in his role as a top depth option behind Kaden Elliss and Pete Werner at inside linebacker Sunday versus the Raiders.

injuries.name: Oscar Delp
injuries.headline: Delp gathered in his only target for eight yards during Sunday's 24-17 victory over the Ravens.
injuries.notes: Delp didn't suit up for the 31-30 overtime loss to Detroit in Week 1 due to a hamstring issue, though he was on the field for Sunday's 24-17 upset win over Baltimore. However, despite the rookie's availability in Week 2, he appeared in just nine of the Saints' 68 offensive snaps, catching his only target for eight yards, while logging six snaps on special teams. Although Delp could see more action moving ahead, it doesn't appear as if he will be more involved than Noah Fant and Juwan Johnson anytime soon.

injuries.name: Tremaine Edmunds
injuries.headline: Edmunds logged 10 tackles (six solo) and one pass defensed in the Giants' 12-7 win over the Titans on Sunday.
injuries.notes: Edmunds played all 60 of the Giants' defensive snaps in the low-scoring win. The inside linebacker's 10 tackles would typically be enough to lead a team, but Arvell Reese totaled 13 tackles en route to the Giants allowing just seven points in the contest. Edmunds had a strong bounce-back game after being failing to record a single solo tackle in the Giants' Week 3 loss to the Rams.

injuries.name: Dru Phillips
injuries.headline: Phillips made 11 tackles (eight solo) in the Giants' 12-7 win over the Titans.
injuries.notes: Phillips played 49 defensive snaps in the contest, good for 82 percent of the Giants' total defensive plays. The third-year cornerback had only amassed three tackles over the first two games before Sunday's breakout, making the production difficult to rely on for fantasy purposes for the time being.

injuries.name: Arvell Reese
injuries.headline: Reese logged 13 tackles (10 solo) and one pass defensed in the Giants' 12-7 win over the Titans.
injuries.notes: Reese led both teams in tackles, putting together an impressive 10 solo stops in what was a defensive contest that featured 12 total punts and two total turnovers. The second-year linebacker also played all 60 of the Giants' defensive snaps in the contest, consistently assisting the team in shutting down the Titans' offense.

injuries.name: Tyrone Tracy Jr.
injuries.headline: Tracy (knee) did not practice Wednesday, Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports.
injuries.notes: Head coach John Harbaugh told reporters after Wednesday's session that Tracy is considered day-to-day and believes the knee injury isn't a serious matter. Tracy has mostly played on special teams this season, but if he's not cleared to play against the Cardinals on Sunday, then Devin Singletary -- who was a healthy scratch for Week 3 against the Titans -- would serve as the Giants' RB3 behind Cam Skattebo and Najee Harris.
injuries.vacated_opportunity_note: Primary beneficiary of vacated early-down carries & red-zone volume if starter is sidelined.

injuries.name: Jaxson Dart
injuries.headline: Dart recently underwent surgery to repair the meniscus and MCL in his left knee, Dan Duggan of The Athletic reports.
injuries.notes: Dart's ACL and PCL were apparently spared, but the quarterback remains done for the 2026 regular season after he was injured in the first quarter of Week 2 against the Rams. It's unclear if Dart could make a postseason return if the Giants are able to make it that far. Jameis Winston and newly acquired J.J. McCarthy will handle quarterback duties moving forward this season.

injuries.name: Andrew Thomas
injuries.headline: questionable
injuries.notes: questionable

injuries.name: Darnell Mooney
injuries.headline: Mooney caught two passes on three targets for 20 yards and logged a nine-yard carry during the Giants' 12-7 win over the Titans on Sunday.
injuries.notes: Mooney has logged two catches in each of the first three games of the season, and his 95 receiving yards are third-most on the Giants behind tight end Isaiah Likely (124) and Malik Nabers (96). The Giants will stay home in Week 4 against the Cardinals, whose defense has given up the second-most fantasy points to wide receivers this season.

injuries.name: Malachi Fields
injuries.headline: Fields caught both of his targets for 19 yards during the Giants' 12-7 win over the Titans on Sunday.
injuries.notes: Fields' 44 snaps on offense were actually second-most among Giants wide receivers behind Malik Nabers (50), though the former finished fourth on the team in targets behind Nabers (six), tight end Isaiah Likely (five) and running back Cam Skattebo (four). Fields has logged two catches in each of the first three games of the regular season, but the rookie third-rounder and the rest of the Giants pass catchers will take on the Cardinals in Week 4, with Arizona's defense ranking second-to-last in fantasy points allowed to opposing wide receivers.

injuries.name: Najee Harris
injuries.headline: Harris turned nine carries into 52 yards during the Giants' 12-7 win over the Titans on Sunday.
injuries.notes: Harris finished as a close second to Cam Skattebo (60) in rushing yards Sunday, but the former needed 11 less carries and averaged 5.8 yards per rush in the Giants' Week 3 win. Harris saw his usage on offense increase compared to Week 2 in what was his debut with the Giants, and it looks like he's settled in as the team's RB2 behind Skattebo and ahead of both Tyrone Tracy and Devin Singletary. Up next is a Week 4 road tilt against the Cardinals.

injuries.name: Charlie Jones
injuries.headline: The Giants signed Jones to the active roster from their practice squad Tuesday, Dan Salomone of the team's official site reports.
injuries.notes: Jones will slot in as the team's fifth-string receiver following the release of Odell Beckham earlier in the day. Jones is also expected to serve as the backup punt returner behind Braxton Berrios.

injuries.name: Brian Burns
injuries.headline: The Giants placed Burns (knee) on injured reserve Tuesday, Dan Salomone of the team's official site reports.
injuries.notes: Burns' move to injured reserve comes just one day after the team announced that he would miss the remainder of the season due to a torn ACL suffered during Sunday's win over the Titans. The 2019 first-round pick recorded eight tackles (four solo) across his three outings before getting hurt, and in his absence, Kayvon Thibodeaux should take over as the primary edge rusher opposite Abdul Carter.

injuries.name: Braxton Berrios
injuries.headline: The Giants signed Berrios off their practice squad Tuesday, Dan Salomone of the team's official site reports.
injuries.notes: After failing to win a spot on the Giants' roster coming out of preseason, Berrios re-signed with the organization as a member of the practice squad. The Giants then elevated him from the practice squad ahead of each of their first three games, with Berrios going without a target over 22 snaps on offense but holding a critical role on special teams as the team's kickoff and punt returner. With the Giants releasing Odell Beckham on Tuesday, Berrios will now be awarded a permanent spot on the 53-man roster.

injuries.name: Tyler Nubin
injuries.headline: questionable
injuries.notes: questionable

injuries.name: Deonte Banks
injuries.headline: questionable
injuries.notes: questionable

injuries.name: Isaiah Likely
injuries.headline: Likely caught two of five targets for 13 yards during the Giants' 12-7 win over the Titans on Sunday.
injuries.notes: After logging 13 catches through the first two games of the regular season, Likely was held to only two receptions in Week 3, the first game with Jameis Winston as the starter instead of Jaxson Dart (knee, IR). Likely's five targets were second most on the Giants behind Malik Nabers (six), but the scoring floors of all Giants pass catchers figure to be lower with Winston under center. That said, New York could turn the keys over to the recently acquired J.J. McCarthy if Winston continues to underwhelm. The Giants will stay home for Week 4 against the Cardinals, whose defense gave up a 6-82-2 receiving line to tight end George Kittle in a 36-30 loss to the 49ers in Week 3.

injuries.name: Jameis Winston
injuries.headline: Head coach John Harbaugh reaffirmed that Winston is the Giants' starting quarterback after the team acquired J.J. McCarthy from the Vikings on Monday, Evan Barnes of Newsday reports.
injuries.notes: While stepping in for the injured Jaxson Dart (knee) in Week 3, Winston threw for just 118 yards on 22 pass attempts in adverse weather conditions during the Giants' 12-7 win over the Titans. Despite his pedestrian numbers, Winston played turnover-free football, and that performance looks as though it will give him some job security even after the Giants added McCarthy, a 2024 first-round draft pick, to their quarterback room. Even though Dart is likely out for the season, Winston will still likely need to limit mistakes and keep the Giants competitive in his future starts in order to ward off McCarthy from supplanting him on the depth chart. Next up for Winston and the Giants is a home date versus the 1-2 Cardinals this Sunday at MetLife Stadium.

injuries.name: J.J. McCarthy
injuries.headline: The Giants acquired McCarthy from the Vikings on Monday in exchange for a 2027 fifth-round pick, Tom Pelissero of Netflix reports.
injuries.notes: The No. 10 overall pick in the 2024 NFL Draft, McCarthy had fallen out of favor in Minnesota and had dropped behind both Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz on the depth chart. The 23-year-old will get a fresh opportunity in New York, where he should at least settle in as the No. 2 quarterback behind Jameis Winston while Jaxson Dart (knee) is likely out for the season. Though Winston led the Giants to a 12-7 win over the Titans in his first start this past Sunday, he's completed just 25 of 49 pass attempts for 229 yards (4.7 YPA) while playing nearly two full games. Another underwhelming performance or two from Winston could compel the Giants to give McCarthy a look in the starting role once he has time to get up to speed with the new playbook.

injuries.name: Dominic Zvada
injuries.headline: Zvada made all four of his field-goal attempts during the Giants' 12-7 win over the Titans on Sunday.
injuries.notes: Neither team could generate that much offense in tough conditions Sunday, but Zvada helped the Giants build and maintain their lead with four field goals, all of which came from within 40 yards. The rookie kicker has made all six of his field-goal attempts and each of his four extra-point tries through the first three games of the regular season.

injuries.name: Malik Nabers
injuries.headline: Nabers caught five of six targets for 26 yards in Sunday's 12-7 win over the Titans.
injuries.notes: The Giants' passing game struggled with Jameis Winston under center instead of Jaxson Dart (knee), and while Nabers led the team in catches and targets, he didn't make much of an impact -- his longest gain went for just 12 yards. That doesn't bode well for the rest of the third-year wideout's campaign with Dart not expected back until 2027, but Nabers and Winston will have plenty of time to develop more chemistry. Nabers will take a 12-96-0 line on 19 targets into a Week 4 home tilt against the Cardinals.

injuries.name: Cam Skattebo
injuries.headline: Skattebo carried the ball 20 times for 60 yards and caught three of four targets for 40 yards in Sunday's 12-7 win over the Titans.
injuries.notes: With Jameis Winston under center instead of Jaxson Dart (knee), the Giants leaned a little more heavily on their backfield and Skattebo saw a season high in touches while hitting for 100-plus scrimmage yards for the first time in 2026. The second-year back's longest play came on a 30-yard toss in the first quarter, as he made himself available downfield to bail out a scrambling Winston. Through three games, Skattebo is showing no ill effects from the ankle injury that ended his rookie campaign early, and he's collected 177 rushing yards and a TD on 50 carries while adding a 7-59-0 line on eight targets. He figures to see a big workload again in Week 4 at home against the Cardinals.

injuries.name: Ar'Darius Washington
injuries.headline: With Tyler Nubin (calf) inactive, Washington will start at safety against the Titans on Sunday, Jordan Raanan of ESPN.com reports.
injuries.notes: Nubin was not cleared by medical staff to play Sunday, so Washington and Jevon Holland will be the Giants' starting safeties for Week 3, with Jason Pinnock and Elijah Campbell providing depth at the position. Washington has two tackles (one solo) through two regular-season games, and the last time he was a regular starter on defense was during the second half of the 2024 campaign as a member of the Ravens.

injuries.name: Demario Davis
injuries.headline: Davis recorded 10 tackles (seven solo), including 1.0 sacks, during Sunday's 31-24 loss at Detroit.
injuries.notes: Davis again led Jets linebackers in snaps in Week 3, but it was his first time registering a double-digit tackle total since Week 12 of the 2025 season. With that said, he remains solidly on the IDP radar in most formats going into a Week 4 matchup against a run-first Chicago offense.

injuries.name: Dylan Parham
injuries.headline: Parham is considered week to week due to a knee injury, Zack Rosenblatt of The Athletic reports.
injuries.notes: Parham is expected to sit out Sunday's matchup versus the Bears after suffering a knee injury during the Week 3 loss to the Lions. In his absence, Jordan Meredith will likely start at left guard.

injuries.name: Jeremy Ruckert
injuries.headline: Ruckert (knee) was limited in Wednesday's practice.
injuries.notes: Ruckert may have picked up the injury during the Lions' 31-24 loss to the Lions in Week 3, when he hauled in all five of his targets for 39 yards and a touchdown, which was the second score of his five-year NFL career. Ruckert, Mason Taylor (thumb) and Kenyon Sadiq (back) are all dealing with injuries, leaving Jelani Woods and Andrew Beck as the only healthy tight ends to begin Week 4 prep. Ruckert will have two more opportunities to log a full practice and avoid an injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Bears.
injuries.vacated_opportunity_note: Assumes inline snaps and high-leverage red-zone target share.

injuries.name: Kene Nwangwu
injuries.headline: Nwangwu (back) was listed as a full participant in Wednesday's practice.
injuries.notes: Head coach Aaron Glenn indicated before Wednesday's session that Nwangwu would be limited in practice due to a back injury that has prevented the veteran running back from playing in each of the first three games of the regular season. It looks like Nwangwu's back injury is past him, and he is on track to make his 2026 regular-season debut Sunday against the Bears. With Breece Hall (quadriceps) considered week-to-week, Nwangwu could serve as the Jets' RB3 behind Braelon Allen and Isaiah Davis for Week 4.

injuries.name: Kenyon Sadiq
injuries.headline: Sadiq was limited at Wednesday's practice due to a back injury.
injuries.notes: Meanwhile, fellow TE Jeremy Ruckert (knee) also was limited, while Mason Taylor (thumb) didn't practice. In Taylor's absence this past Sunday at Detroit, Sadiq, a rookie first-round pick, broke out with seven catches (on eight targets) for 105 yards and one touchdown. Another hefty workload could be on tap for Sadiq in Week 5 at Chicago if Taylor remains sidelined and Ruckert also is less than 100 percent. First, though, the statuses of the three players will continue to be watched to get a sense of the overall situation.
injuries.vacated_opportunity_note: Assumes inline snaps and high-leverage red-zone target share.

injuries.name: Kingsley Enagbare
injuries.headline: questionable
injuries.notes: questionable

injuries.name: Minkah Fitzpatrick
injuries.headline: Coach Aaron Glenn said Fitzpatrick (groin) will be limited in Wednesday's practice, Antwan V. Staley of the New York Daily News reports.
injuries.notes: After missing back-to-back games in Weeks 2 and 3, Fitzpatrick has a decent shot at returning for Sunday's game against the Bears. Dane Belton and Andre Cisco have been manning the safety spots for the Jets with Fitzpatrick sidelined.

injuries.name: Adonai Mitchell
injuries.headline: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said that Mitchell (finger) won't practice Wednesday and is considered week-to-week, Zack Rosenblatt of The Athletic reports.
injuries.notes: Mitchell sat out the Jets' 31-24 loss to the Lions in Week 3 due to the finger injury, and his absence to begin Week 4 prep in addition to Glenn classifying him as week-to-week rather than day-to-day suggests that the receiver is trending toward another absence this Sunday versus the Bears. If Mitchell ends up sitting out a second straight game, Isaiah Williams would be in store for another elevated snap count as the Jets' No. 2 wideout behind Garrett Wilson.
injuries.vacated_opportunity_note: Expands to high-volume target progression and 2-WR/3-WR set route participation.

injuries.name: Breece Hall
injuries.headline: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said that Hall (thigh) won't practice Wednesday and confirmed the running back is being viewed as week-to-week, Zack Rosenblatt of The Athletic reports.
injuries.notes: Though Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reported Monday that an MRI on the quad injury Hall sustained in Sunday's loss to the Lions wasn't as significant as the Jets had feared, the running back appears likely to miss at least one game. Unless Hall is able to fit in some practice activity Thursday or Friday, the Jets will likely officially rule him out ahead of Sunday's contest in Chicago. Hall's expected absence would clear the way for Braelon Allen to serve as the Jets' lead option on the ground, while Isaiah Davis would likely be in store for added work in a change-of-pace role.
injuries.vacated_opportunity_note: Primary beneficiary of vacated early-down carries & red-zone volume if starter is sidelined.

injuries.name: Mason Taylor
injuries.headline: Taylor (thumb) will not practice Wednesday and remains week-to-week, Zack Rosenblatt of The Athletic reports.
injuries.notes: Taylor appears set to miss a second straight game Sunday against the Bears. With Taylor out last Sunday against the Lions, first-round rookie Kenyon Sadiq played a season-high 57.6 percent of the Jets' offensive snaps and posted a 7-105-1 receiving line on eight targets. With Adonai Mitchell (finger) also week-to-week for Gang Green, Sadiq has a path to once again play a prominent pass-catching role versus Chicago.
injuries.vacated_opportunity_note: Assumes inline snaps and high-leverage red-zone target share.

injuries.name: Isaiah Williams
injuries.headline: Williams caught one of his two targets for 21 yards and returned four kickoffs for 95 yards over 63 total snaps in the Jets' 31-24 loss to the Lions on Sunday.
injuries.notes: Williams played 90 percent of the Jets' offensive snaps in the contest alongside an additional eight special-teams snaps as a returner. The wide receiver has seen more playing time lately due to injuries to Adonai Mitchell (finger) and Omar Cooper (ankle). If Mitchell misses another game, Williams should see similar playing time as the No. 2 option in the Week 4 matchup with the Bears.

injuries.name: Jason Sanders
injuries.headline: The Jets signed Sanders off their practice squad Tuesday, Eric Allen of the team's official site reports.
injuries.notes: Though New York cut him at the conclusion of the preseason, Sanders re-signed with the organization as a member of the practice squad and was elevated for each of the first three games of the season. He went 5-for-6 on field-goal tries and drilled all five of his point-after attempts during that stretch, with his performance earning him a spot on the 53-man roster. Sanders should have more security after New York waived Blake Grupe in a corresponding move.

injuries.name: Kiko Mauigoa
injuries.headline: questionable
injuries.notes: questionable

injuries.name: Isaiah Davis
injuries.headline: Davis played 16 special-teams snaps during the Jets' 31-24 loss to the Lions on Sunday.
injuries.notes: Davis didn't see any work on offense in Week 3, but he could be called upon to handle a complementary role in the backfield next Sunday in Chicago. After exiting the loss to the Lions in the fourth quarter with a thigh injury, starter Breece Hall is considered week-to-week and looks likely to miss at least one game. Braelon Allen should be in line to lead the New York backfield in Hall's absence, while Davis may serve as a change-of-pace option.

injuries.name: Sterling Shepard
injuries.headline: Shepard reverted to the Jets' practice squad Monday, per the NFL's transaction log.
injuries.notes: In his first action of the season, Shepard played 30 of 66 offensive snaps in Sunday's loss to the Lions, turning his only target into a three-yard reception. With Adonai Mitchell (finger) battling an injury, Shepard could again be elevated ahead of next Sunday's game against the Bears. He has no fantasy appeal.

injuries.name: Braelon Allen
injuries.headline: Allen and Isaiah Davis will man the Jets backfield for as long as Breece Hall (thigh) is potentially sidelined, Rich Cimini of ESPN.com reports.
injuries.notes: Hall exited in the fourth quarter of Sunday's loss at Detroit due to a thigh injury, and afterward he relayed that he "felt something" while running, per Brian Costello of the New York Post. Ian Rapoport and Adam Schefter of ESPN then reported Monday that Hall is considered week-to-week. While Hall hasn't outright been ruled out for Week 4 or beyond, Allen currently ranks second on the team in carries with 19, which have gone for 61 yards, while Davis hasn't logged an offensive snap through three contests to begin the season. As a result, Allen is the better bet to take advantage of an absent Hall, if that comes to pass.

injuries.name: Geno Smith
injuries.headline: Smith completed 31 of 37 passes for 321 yards and three touchdowns in Sunday's 31-24 loss to the Lions. He added 12 rushing yards on two carries and threw a two-point conversion.
injuries.notes: The veteran QB was almost flawless as the Jets nearly pulled off the upset, with his only turnover being a fumble on his fifth sack of the day late in the fourth quarter, ending his final possession. Smith spread the ball around, completing passes to eight different targets and connecting with Garrett Wilson, Jeremy Ruckert and rookie first-round pick Kenyon Sadiq for his scores. Smith has been extremely efficient to begin the season, posting a 75.5 percent completion rate (77-for-102) with a 4:0 TD:INT and 7.7 YPA. He'll look to stay sharp in a Week 4 road trip to Chicago.

injuries.name: Garrett Wilson
injuries.headline: Wilson caught 10 of 13 targets for 107 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 31-24 loss to Detroit.
injuries.notes: The star wideout -- who was evaluated for a head injury and cleared to return -- paced Jets pass catchers in all three receiving categories, and his 23-yard TD from Geno Smith in the fourth quarter tied the game at 24-24, only for the Lions to respond inside the final two minutes. It's Wilson's first 100-yard performance since Week 14 of the 2024 season, as injuries disrupted his 2025 campaign. Wilson also has found the end zone in back-to-back games, and he'll take a 21-243-2 line on 27 targets into a Week 4 road trip to Chicago.

injuries.name: Qwan'tez Stiggers
injuries.headline: Stiggers (hand) returned to Sunday's game versus the Lions, Brian Costello of the New York Post reports.
injuries.notes: Stiggers exited the contest after suffering a hand injury early in the first quarter. However, it appears the injury wasn't anything serious, though his return mostly impacts the special-teams unit while adding depth to the secondary.

injuries.name: Joseph Ossai
injuries.headline: Ossai (foot) is active for Sunday's game against the Lions.
injuries.notes: Ossai was trending in the right direction for Week 3 after logging a full practice Friday, and the veteran pass rusher has been given the green light to play Sunday after going through pregame warmups. It will be Ossai's 2026 regular-season debut, and he's expected to serve in a rotational role at defensive end behind starters Will McDonald and Kingsley Enagbare.

injuries.name: Jamaal Pritchett
injuries.headline: The Jets signed Pritchett from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday, Zack Rosenblatt of The Athletic reports.
injuries.notes: The Jets signed Pritchett to the practice squad Sept. 2 after waiving the wide receiver on cutdown day. The second-year player out of South Alabama has yet to play in an NFL contest. If Adonai Mitchell (finger) cannot suit up for Sunday's game against the Lions, Pritchett is set to be the No. 4 option for the Jets in his debut.

injuries.name: Arian Smith
injuries.headline: Smith (knee) underwent surgery Wednesday to repair a torn ACL and will miss the rest of the season, Antwan V. Staley of the New York Daily News reports.
injuries.notes: Smith suffered a knee injury during the 20-17 overtime loss to Green Bay in Week 2. He will finish the 2026 campaign without a catch (one target), adding four carries for 13 yards. With Smith, Omar Cooper (ankle) and Tim Patrick (groin) out of the equation, Isaiah Williams could be in line for more opportunities behind Adonai Mitchell and Garrett Wilson. The Jets also signed Malik McClain off the practice squad Tuesday, which will help fill some of the void left by the injuries within the receiving corps.

injuries.name: David Onyemata
injuries.headline: Onyemata (groin) underwent core-muscle surgery Wednesday, Antwan V. Staley of the New York Daily News reports.
injuries.notes: Onyemata was injured during the 20-17 overtime loss to Green Bay in Week 2. He was placed on the injured reserve list Tuesday, and while that means he will miss at least four games, he is anticipated to be out longer, though head coach Aaron Glenn expects him back before the end of the season. While Onyemata is out of commission, Darrell Jackson, Jowon Briggs, T'Vondre Sweat and Harrison Phillips will presumably see more snaps in each game moving ahead.

injuries.name: Chance Campbell
injuries.headline: out
injuries.notes: out

injuries.name: Jihaad Campbell
injuries.headline: Campbell (knee) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice.
injuries.notes: Campbell likely suffered his knee injury during the Eagles' Week 3 loss to the Bears. The linebacker practicing in a limited capacity despite the new injury is a good sign. Campbell should be able to avoid any injury designation for Sunday's Week 4 matchup with the Rams by upgrading to a full participant in practice by Friday.

injuries.name: Zack Baun
injuries.headline: Baun (concussion) did not participate in Wednesday's practice.
injuries.notes: Baun suffered a concussion in the Eagles' Week 3 loss to the Bears. The linebacker has entered the league's five-step concussion protocol and will need to be cleared by an independent neurologist to upgrade his practice participation and suit up for Sunday's game.

injuries.name: Hollywood Brown
injuries.headline: Brown (ankle) did not participate in Wednesday's practice.
injuries.notes: Brown has yet to practice since sustaining his ankle injury during Week 3 prep. The wide receiver will likely need to upgrade to at least limited practice participation by Friday to have a shot at playing in the Eagles' contest against the Rams on Sunday.
injuries.vacated_opportunity_note: Expands to high-volume target progression and 2-WR/3-WR set route participation.

injuries.name: Will Shipley
injuries.headline: Shipley (foot) did not participate in Wednesday's practice.
injuries.notes: Shipley ended Week 3 prep with back-to-back limited practices and had no injury designation heading into the Eagles' 27-7 loss to the Bears on Monday Night Football. Shipley's downgrade to a non-participant in Wednesday's session could be precautionary or may be a sign the running back aggravated the issue during Monday's game.

injuries.name: Moro Ojomo
injuries.headline: questionable
injuries.notes: questionable

injuries.name: Dallas Goedert
injuries.headline: Goedert (knee) didn't take part in Wednesday's walkthrough.
injuries.notes: Goedert already has missed one game due to an MCL sprain in his right knee and likely will continue to trend toward absences in future weeks until he returns to the practice field in some capacity. In Monday's loss at Chicago, Johnny Mundt started in place of Goedert and logged 26 of 50 offensive snaps, which was followed by Zach Ertz's 19 and E.J. Jenkins' 13. A similar breakdown of TE reps is likely between the trio until Goedert is back in the lineup.
injuries.vacated_opportunity_note: Assumes inline snaps and high-leverage red-zone target share.

injuries.name: DeVonta Smith
injuries.headline: Smith missed Wednesday's walkthrough due to a hamstring injury.
injuries.notes: Smith also kicked off last week with a DNP on the Eagles' first practice report due to a hamstring issue, only to progress to full and no designation ahead of Monday's road matchup with the Bears. In the end, though, his status bears watching in the coming days to ensure he's also good to go for Sunday's contest against the Rams.
injuries.vacated_opportunity_note: Expands to high-volume target progression and 2-WR/3-WR set route participation.

injuries.name: Zach Ertz
injuries.headline: Ertz reverted to the Eagles' practice squad Tuesday, per the NFL's transaction log.
injuries.notes: Ertz brought in one of two targets for nine yards during Monday's 27-7 loss at Chicago. It was a mostly uneventful reunion with his old team, but given that he was just signed a week ago, it's relatively impressive he led Philadelphia's tight ends in targets. With Dallas Goedert (knee) lacking a clear return date and rookie second-rounder Eli Stowers (hamstring) still on IR, Ertz has a good chance of being added to the gameday roster again for a Week 4 matchup versus the Rams.

injuries.name: Kenny Moore II
injuries.headline: The Eagles signed Moore from the practice squad to the active roster Tuesday.
injuries.notes: The Colts released Moore in early May, and the defensive back signed with the Eagles' practice squad Sept. 22. The expectation was always that Moore would eventually be promoted to the 53-man roster and given a one-year, $3 million contract. Moore is set to serve as the primary depth option in the Eagles' secondary for the remainder of the 2026 season.

injuries.name: Dontayvion Wicks
injuries.headline: Wicks recorded two receptions for 32 yards on five targets in Monday's 27-7 loss to the Bears.
injuries.notes: Though he didn't find paydirt, Wicks played a critical role on the Eagles' lone scoring drive late in the second quarter, leading off the possession with a 13-yard catch and run. He was otherwise held in check while the game was still competitive, with his other reception coming in the fourth quarter when the Bears had built a 20-point lead. Through his first three games with Philadelphia, Wicks has produced a 9-179-1 receiving line on 15 targets.

injuries.name: Makai Lemon
injuries.headline: Lemon recorded three receptions for 29 yards on four targets in Monday's 27-7 loss to the Bears.
injuries.notes: After taking the field for north of 60 percent of the snaps in both of the Eagles' first two contests, Lemon wasn't a major beneficiary of the absence of tight end Dallas Goedert (knee). Even though the Eagles leaned more heavily on three-wide formations, Lemon saw only a slight uptick in playing time Monday, logging 35 of 50 snaps (70 percent). The rookie first-round pick appears to be little more than a tertiary option in the passing game at this stage of his career, as he's thus far been held to seven catches for 38 yards on nine targets through his first three NFL games.

injuries.name: Fred Johnson
injuries.headline: questionable
injuries.notes: questionable

injuries.name: Jake Elliott
injuries.headline: Elliott converted his sole PAT and attempted no field goals in the Eagles' 27-7 loss to the Bears on Monday night.
injuries.notes: Elliott had an uneventful day, kicking through his one extra point on a second-quarter touchdown. The kicker remains 2-for-2 on field-goal attempts and moves to 7-for-7 on extra-point tries through three regular-season games.

injuries.name: Tank Bigsby
injuries.headline: Bigsby caught his only target for five yards Monday in a Week 3 loss to the Bears. He also lost a fumble.
injuries.notes: Bigsby logged 13 carries and scored a touchdown in Week 2 against Tennessee after Saquon Barkley suffered a stinger, but he went back to a minor role Monday. That was partly due to Barkley looking healthy and turning 15 totes into 82 yards, though Bigsby's lost fumble following his lone reception near the end of the first quarter also may have had a role in his lack of subsequent touches. Whatever the case may be, Bigsby doesn't seem likely to have a significant week-to-week role on offense whenever Barkley is healthy.

injuries.name: Jalen Hurts
injuries.headline: Hurts completed 16 of 25 passes for 153 yards with no touchdowns and one interception while rushing four times for 25 yards and a touchdown in the Eagles' 27-7 loss to the Bears on Monday night.
injuries.notes: Hurts scuffled through the air as much as his final line suggests, averaging a modest 6.1 yards per attempt while taking a pair of sacks. The star signal-caller also absorbed a big hit on the sideline at the end of a two-yard scramble midway through the second quarter, and he missed four plays while undergoing a concussion check he subsequently passed. Hurts led the Eagles to their only points upon checking back in for the following possession, one he capped off with a one-yard touchdown run as time expired in the first half. That would prove to be the highlight of an otherwise forgettable night, and Hurts is averaging an unremarkable 206.7 passing yards per game alongside a 5:3 TD:INT ahead of a Week 4 home showdown against the Rams on Sunday.

injuries.name: Saquon Barkley
injuries.headline: Barkley rushed 15 times for 82 yards and secured one of two targets for minus-2 yards in the Eagles' 27-7 loss to the Bears on Monday night.
injuries.notes: Barkley was a rare bright spot for an otherwise moribund Eagles offense, showing no ill effects from the stinger that cost him substantial time in a Week 2 win over the Titans. The star running back got his night started on the right foot with a 12-yard run on Philadelphia's opening possession and a nine-yarder on the second drive that was wiped out by a holding penalty. Barkley would go on to add another four rushes of seven or more yards, including a game-long 17-yard scamper. Barkley has yet to top 15 carries in any of the first three games of the season, but he's been highly efficient while averaging 5.1 yards per carry and posting four runs of 10-plus yards overall. Barkley and the Eagles have a tall order on their Week 4 ledger, however, as the Rams come to town Sunday.

injuries.name: Jonathan Greenard
injuries.headline: Greenard (pectoral) is active for Monday night's matchup with Chicago.
injuries.notes: Greenard will make his Eagles debut after missing the team's first two contests of the regular season while recovering from a pectoral injury. The 29-year-old registered 3.0 sacks over 12 regular-season contests with Minnesota in 2025 before being traded to Philadelphia in April, and he'll look to get off to a strong start against the Bears to open his 2026 campaign.

injuries.name: Andrew Mukuba
injuries.headline: Mukuba (knee) was a full participant in Friday's practice.
injuries.notes: Mukuba was a full participant in Friday's practice after being limited in Thursday's session. The safety appears to be over the knee injury that plagued him throughout Week 2. Mukuba will likely head into Monday night's game against the Bears healthy and without any injury designation.

injuries.name: Jalen Carter
injuries.headline: Carter (wrist) was a full participant in Friday's practice.
injuries.notes: Carter logged a limited practice session Thursday before upgrading to full participation Friday. The defensive tackle appears to be over the wrist injury that he played through in the Eagles' Week 2 win over the Titans. There is a strong chance Carter heads into Monday night's matchup with the Bears fully healthy and clear of any injury designation.

injuries.name: Darius Cooper
injuries.headline: Cooper caught two of three targets for 26 yards and a touchdown in the Eagles' 24-20 win over the Titans on Sunday.
injuries.notes: With Dallas Goedert (knee) going down early in the game, Cooper played 31 offensive snaps as the No. 4 receiver after logging just eight in Week 1 against the Commanders. Cooper responded to the increased playing time by breaking free in the back of the end zone with nine seconds left in the fourth quarter to catch the game-winning three-yard touchdown from Jalen Hurts. Cooper doesn't carry much value in redraft fantasy leagues and would need an injury or two ahead of him at the position for that to change.

injuries.name: Johnny Mundt
injuries.headline: Mundt caught two of three targets for eight yards in Sunday's 24-20 win against the Titans.
injuries.notes: Mundt started along with fellow tight end Dallas Goedert (knee), and he logged 49 of Philadelphia's 76 offensive snaps. The significant playing time was partly due to Goedert exiting in the first half after spraining his MCL. Goedert is now slated to miss multiple weeks due to the injury, but that won't necessarily mean that Mundt will be an attractive fantasy waiver-wire pickup. The Eagles signed veteran Zach Ertz to a contract Tuesday, and he'll likely slide in as the team's top tight end during Goedert's absence, though it's unclear how long Ertz will need to get up to speed.

injuries.name: Brandin Echols
injuries.headline: Echols (concussion) no longer has an injury designation for Thursday's game against the Browns.
injuries.notes: A limited practice participant through Week 4 prep, Echols had been listed as questionable heading into Thursday. However, Alan Saunders of SteelersNow.com relayed Wednesday that the cornerback had cleared the five-step concussion protocol, and the Steelers have now signed off on Echols playing on a short week. Through Pittsburgh's first three games, Echols has accrued two tackles while handling a limited role on defense and serving as a key player on special teams.

injuries.name: Yahya Black
injuries.headline: The Steelers added Black to their injury report and list him as questionable for Thursday's game against the Browns due to a personal matter.
injuries.notes: Black's status for Thursday's game will be clarified when the Steelers release their inactive list 90 minutes prior to the 8:15 p.m. ET kickoff. The 24-year-old has filled a rotational role along the Steelers' defensive line this season, logging no more than 40 percent of the snaps in any of the team's three contests while accruing four tackles.

injuries.name: Jalen Ramsey
injuries.headline: Ramsey (wrist) is questionable for Thursday night's game against the Browns, Brooke Pryor of ESPN.com reports.
injuries.notes: Ramsey was limited in practice all week after suffering the injury last Sunday against the Bengals. Rayshawn Jenkins would become an every-down safety with Daylen Everette and Brandin Echols (concussion) seeing increased reps in the secondary if Ramsey is unable to play.

injuries.name: Rico Dowdle
injuries.headline: The Steelers ruled Dowdle (toe) out for Thursday's game in Cleveland, Brooke Pryor of ESPN.com reports.
injuries.notes: Dowdle will miss a second straight game after he was unable to practice in any fashion on a short week. With Dowdle out of the mix again, Jaylen Warren looks primed to handle a workhorse role out of the Pittsburgh backfield, after he logged 56 of 62 snaps and handled 20 touches (17 carries, three receptions) for 176 yards in a 30-27 win over the Bengals last week.
injuries.vacated_opportunity_note: Primary beneficiary of vacated early-down carries & red-zone volume if starter is sidelined.

injuries.name: T.J. Watt
injuries.headline: Watt made one tackle in the Steelers' 30-27 win over the Bengals on Sunday.
injuries.notes: Despite playing 43 defensive snaps in the contest, Watt did not log more than a single tackle assist in the Steelers' win. The pass rusher had a quiet night, contributing to Joe Burrow's 282 passing yards and three passing touchdowns in the shootout.

injuries.name: Patrick Queen
injuries.headline: Queen logged 13 tackles (four solo) and one pass defensed in the Steelers' 30-27 win over the Bengals on Sunday.
injuries.notes: Queen once again played all of the Steelers' defensive snaps, logging 56 snaps against the Bengals. The linebacker led both teams in tackles and is now up to 23 total tackles (six solo) and two passes defensed, including one interception, across the first three games.

injuries.name: Darnell Washington
injuries.headline: Washington caught three of four targets for 67 yards during the Steelers' 30-27 win over the Bengals on Sunday.
injuries.notes: Washington's three catches were as many as he had accumulated through the first two games of the season. He was responsible for the Steelers' longest play late in the fourth quarter, when he took a short pass from Aaron Rodgers and broke multiple tackles for a 47-yard gain, leading to what was ultimately the game-winning field goal by Chris Boswell. Washington was on the field for 47 of the Steelers' 62 offensive snaps (75.8 percent), noticeably ahead of Pat Freiermuth (37). Washington will take a 6-92-0 receiving line on eight targets into Thursday's game against the Browns, whose defense ranks in the bottom-10 in yards allowed to tight ends this season.

injuries.name: Ben Skowronek
injuries.headline: Skowronek hauled in his lone target for a 23-yard touchdown during Sunday's 30-27 win over the Bengals.
injuries.notes: Skowronek ranked fifth among Steelers receivers by playing 11 of the team's 62 offensive snaps, but the 29-year-old was able to connect with quarterback Aaron Rodgers on a pass to the end zone during his limited time on the field. Despite coming up with a big play in the Week 3 win, Skowronek remains likely to see most of his field time on special teams moving forward.

injuries.name: Pat Freiermuth
injuries.headline: Freiermuth recorded two receptions for 30 yards on four targets and carried once for one yard in Sunday's 30-27 win over the Bengals.
injuries.notes: Freiermuth took the field for 37 of the Steelers' 62 offensive snaps, with his 60 percent share placing him slightly behind fellow tight end Darnell Washington (47 snaps, 76 percent). The Steelers should continue to make ample use of two-tight-end sets to keep Freiermuth involved in their game plans, but since he doesn't project to see heavy target volume week to week, he'll remain a largely touchdown-dependent fantasy option.

injuries.name: Michael Pittman Jr.
injuries.headline: Pittman caught two passes on five targets for 16 yards in Sunday's 30-27 win over the Bengals.
injuries.notes: Pittman was cleared to return from a one-game absence due to a foot injury. Despite the low offensive output, he played 45 of 62 offensive snaps (72.3 percent), which was second-most among Steelers wide receivers behind DK Metcalf (56). Pittman also was tied for the second-most targets, though six Pittsburgh pass catchers were targeted at least four times by Aaron Rodgers. Pittman has a 5-74-0 receiving line (eight targets) across two regular-season contests heading into Thursday's game against the Browns, whose secondary could be without starters Grant Delpit (shoulder) and Tyson Campbell (knee).

injuries.name: Roman Wilson
injuries.headline: Wilson caught three of six targets for 60 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 30-27 win over the Bengals.
injuries.notes: Wilson came out of the gates hot Sunday, securing a 38-yard touchdown from quarterback Aaron Rodgers on the team's opening drive of the game. The wide receiver led the team in targets in Week 3, and he has now registered exactly six targets in each of the team's first three contests this season. Wilson has reeled in 11 of 18 targets for 114 yards and a touchdown so far this year.

injuries.name: Chris Boswell
injuries.headline: Boswell made all three of his field-goal attempts and each of his three extra-point tries during the Steelers' 30-27 win over the Bengals on Sunday.
injuries.notes: Boswell missed one kick in each of the first two games of the regular season, but he was perfect during Sunday's win. He connected on field goals from 44, 36 and 33 yards, the last of which occurred just before the two-minute warning of the fourth quarter and gave Pittsburgh the lead for good. It appears the Steelers' offense may have figured something out in Week 3, and that continued success would raise Boswell's scoring floor over the coming weeks.

injuries.name: Aaron Rodgers
injuries.headline: Rodgers completed 19 of 34 passes for 292 yards with three touchdowns and one interception while adding three rushes for 10 yards in the Steelers' 30-27 win over the Bengals on Sunday.
injuries.notes: After averaging just 5.2 yards per attempt while completing a sparse 59.5 percent of his passes over the first two games of the season, Rodgers begin clicking in Mike McCarthy's offense Sunday. The future Hall of Famer averaged 8.6 yards per attempt and had five completions of 22 yards or more while connecting with nine different pass catchers overall. Rodgers distributed the ball on his three touchdown passes as well, hitting Roman Wilson, Ben Skowronek and DK Metcalf from 38, 23 and six yards out, respectively. Rodgers' passing yardage total was a season high despite his completion total being his lowest through three games, and he'll look to carry the momentum into a Week 4 road matchup against an aggressive Browns defense on Thursday night.

injuries.name: DK Metcalf
injuries.headline: Metcalf brought in three of five targets for 31 yards and a touchdown in the Steelers' 30-27 win over the Bengals on Sunday.
injuries.notes: Metcalf once again put together a very modest receiving line, but the veteran wideout managed to deliver his first touchdown of the season on a six-yard grab late in the third quarter. His high-water mark through three games is the four-catch, 40-yard tally he managed in Week 1 against the Falcons, but with Aaron Rodgers and the passing attack as a whole looking much more cohesive Sunday, there's some hope for an uptick in production during a Week 4 road matchup against the Browns on Thursday night.

injuries.name: Jaylen Warren
injuries.headline: Warren rushed 17 times for 127 yards and secured three of four targets for 49 yards in the Steelers' 30-27 win over the Bengals on Sunday.
injuries.notes: Warren had the Steelers backfield to himself Sunday due to the absence of Rico Dowdle (toe), and the former took full advantage. Filling his usual versatile role, Warren came within striking distance of his single-game career high of 143 rushing yards, and he would have easily blown by that figure had an 87-yard run just before the midway point of the fourth quarter not been nullified by a DK Metcalf holding penalty. If Dowdle is unable to beat the short turnaround for a Week 4 road matchup against the Browns on Thursday night, Warren will be in store for another hefty workload in the divisional clash.

injuries.name: Jamel Dean
injuries.headline: Dean (ankle) is active for Sunday's game against Cincinnati.
injuries.notes: Dean was working through an ankle issue during Week 3 prep and drew the questionable tag after logging back-to-back limited practices Thursday and Friday. He's been cleared by medical staff to play Sunday and will start opposite Asante Samuel at outside cornerback. Dean has eight tackles (five solo) through the first two games of the regular season.

injuries.name: Brock Hoffman
injuries.headline: Hoffman will start at right guard against the Bengals on Sunday, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
injuries.notes: Hoffman operated in a depth role through the first two regular-season games, but he'll work with the first-team offense Sunday as the Steelers overhaul the right side of the offensive line, with Max Iheanachor starting at right tackle. Spencer Anderson and Dylan Cook will be the depth options behind Hoffman and Iheanachor for Week 3.

injuries.name: Max Iheanachor
injuries.headline: Iheanachor will start at right tackle against the Bengals on Sunday, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
injuries.notes: Iheanachor played a total of four offensive snaps through the first two games of the regular season while serving as a depth option, but the rookie first-rounder will be a starter Sunday for the first time in his short NFL career. The Steelers are overhauling their entire right side of the offensive line, with Brock Hoffman getting the nod at right guard next to Iheanachor.

injuries.name: Gennings Dunker
injuries.headline: The Steelers placed Dunker (knee) on injured reserve Saturday, Tom Pelissero of Netflix reports.
injuries.notes: Dunker suffered an MCL sprain during Week 3 prep and will need to miss 4-to-6 weeks with the issue. Now on IR, Dunker will need to wait four games before becoming eligible to return to the Steelers' active roster.

injuries.name: Travis Homer
injuries.headline: The Steelers signed Homer from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday, Teresa Varley of the team's official site reports.
injuries.notes: Homer was elevated for the Steelers' Week 2 loss to the Patriots, playing two offensive snaps and 10 special-teams snaps in the game while logging two rushes for 16 yards. The running back could be the primary option for the Steelers in the Week 3 contest against the Bengals. Jaylen Warren (shoulder) is listed as questionable and Rico Dowdle (toe) has been ruled out, meaning at worst Homer will be the No. 2 or No. 3 option Sunday.

injuries.name: Gracen Halton
injuries.headline: Halton (ankle) was not listed on Wednesday's practice report, Vic Tafur of The Athletic reports.
injuries.notes: Halton did not return to the 49ers' Week 3 win over the Cardinals due to an ankle injury. However, his absence from Wednesday's injury report indicates that his ankle is fine, and the rookie fourth-rounder should be available for Sunday's home game against the Broncos. Halton has eight tackles (five solo) and one pass defense through the first three games of the regular season.

injuries.name: Dre Greenlaw
injuries.headline: Greenlaw (quadriceps) didn't practice Wednesday, Vic Tafur of The Athletic reports.
injuries.notes: Greenlaw injured his quad during the fourth quarter of the 49ers' 36-30 win over the Cardinals in Week 3, when he logged eight tackles (three solo). The veteran linebacker will need to return to practice in at least a limited capacity over the coming days to have a realistic chance of playing against the Broncos on Sunday. If Greenlaw is unable to play, then Garret Wallow would likely start alongside Fred Warner and Jaden Dugger at linebacker.

injuries.name: KhaDarel Hodge
injuries.headline: Hodge (knee) did not practice Wednesday, Vic Tafur of The Athletic reports.
injuries.notes: Hodge may have tweaked his knee during the 49ers' 36-30 win over the Cardinals in Week 3, when he played 54 offensive snaps without seeing a target from Brock Purdy. Hodge will have two more opportunities to log a full practice and avoid an injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Broncos.
injuries.vacated_opportunity_note: Expands to high-volume target progression and 2-WR/3-WR set route participation.

injuries.name: Mykel Williams
injuries.headline: The 49ers opened Williams' (knee) 21-day practice window Wednesday to return from the reserve/PUP list, Matt Maiocco of NBC Sports Bay Area reports.
injuries.notes: Williams spent his first practice back with the 49ers as a limited participant. The team has until Oct. 21. to add the linebacker to the 53-man roster, or he will remain on the reserve/PUP list for the remainder of the 2026 season. Williams is still recovering from a torn ACL he suffered in November 2025, but he'll be eligible to suit up as early as Week 5.

injuries.name: Keion White
injuries.headline: questionable
injuries.notes: questionable

injuries.name: Mike Evans
injuries.headline: Coach Kyle Shanahan said Evans (ribs) won't practice Wednesday, Cam Inman of The San Jose Mercury News reports.
injuries.notes: Evans was laboring after taking a big hit from Cardinals safety Budda Baker in the second quarter of this past Sunday's win against Arizona, eventually being ruled out due to a rib injury. Afterward, Evans was diagnosed with a strained rib, but Shanahan also relayed to Vic Tafur of The Athletic on Wednesday that the wide receiver "may" practice later this week. Logging some on-field work Thursday and/or Friday seemingly will give Evans a chance to play Week 4 against the Broncos, but his upcoming availability remains up in the air.
injuries.vacated_opportunity_note: Expands to high-volume target progression and 2-WR/3-WR set route participation.

injuries.name: Renardo Green
injuries.headline: Green recorded 13 tackles (seven solo) and one pass breakup in Sunday's 36-30 win over the Cardinals.
injuries.notes: With the Cardinals running 87 offensive plays, it led to inflated tackle numbers across the board for San Francisco defenders, and it was Green's second career game with double-digit tackles. Through three games this season, Green has 18 tackles (10 solo) and two pass breakups, including one interception.

injuries.name: Fred Warner
injuries.headline: Warner recorded 17 tackles (eight solo) in Sunday's win over Arizona.
injuries.notes: The Cardinals ran a whopping 87 offensive plays Sunday, and Warner was on the field for all of them, leading to the inflated tackles number. The 17 tackles were the most Warner has ever recorded in a single game during his nine-year career. Through three games this season, Warner has 33 tackles (14 solo), including 0.5 sacks, two forced fumbles and one pass breakup.

injuries.name: Kaelon Black
injuries.headline: Black turned four carries into 17 yards and failed to haul in his lone target during the 49ers' 36-30 win over the Cardinals on Sunday.
injuries.notes: Black accumulated 95 scrimmage yards on 22 touches through the first two games of the season while working behind Christian McCaffrey, but the rookie observed most of Sunday's game from the sidelines, seeing the field for only eight of the 49ers' 54 offensive snaps (14.8 percent). Keeping McCaffrey healthy is a top priority, but Black's workload is likely to remain erratic and dependent on game script. The 49ers will remain home in Week 4 to host the Broncos this Sunday.

injuries.name: Romello Height
injuries.headline: questionable
injuries.notes: questionable

injuries.name: Jacob Cowing
injuries.headline: Cowing failed to corral either of his two targets while playing 17 of the 49ers' 54 snaps on offense in Sunday's 36-30 win over the Cardinals.
injuries.notes: Even though Demarcus Robinson (ankle) was moved to injured reserve following Week 2 and Mike Evans (rib) was unable to finish Sunday's contest, Cowing didn't benefit from much of a spike in playing time. In fact, after logging 24 of the 49ers' 52 offensive snaps (46.2 percent) in Week 2, Cowing saw his snap share drop to 31.5 percent. The biggest beneficiary of Robinson's absence and Evans' early exit was KhaDarel Hodge, who finished second to only Deebo Samuel (39) among 49ers receivers with 30 snaps.

injuries.name: Jordan Watkins
injuries.headline: Watkins recorded two receptions for 60 yards on two targets in Sunday's 36-30 win over the Cardinals.
injuries.notes: Making his 2026 debut after he was a healthy inactive for the 49ers' first two contests, Watkins took the field for 15 of the team's 54 offensive snaps and was able to make a mark with 34- and 26-yard grabs. He still finished fifth among 49ers receivers in playing time, but he could see an uptick in opportunities if the rib strain Mike Evans suffered Sunday prevents him from playing Week 4 against the Broncos.

injuries.name: James Thompson Jr.
injuries.headline: Thompson (ankle) won't play in San Francisco's Week 4 matchup versus the Broncos, Jennifer Lee Chan of NBC Sports Bay Area reports.
injuries.notes: Thompson is in line to miss a second consecutive game due to the high-ankle sprain he suffered during the Week 2 win over the Dolphins. While there's currently no timetable for his return, his next chance to play will be the Week 6 matchup against Seattle.

injuries.name: Nick Bosa
injuries.headline: Coach Kyle Shanahan said Monday that Bosa (calf) won't play this coming Sunday against the Broncos, Cam Inman of The San Jose Mercury News reports.
injuries.notes: After Bosa strained his calf at practice last Thursday, Shanahan told Matt Barrows of The Athletic that the pass rusher would miss "a few weeks," so a second consecutive absence in Week 4 comes as no surprise. The 49ers started Ogbo Okoronkwo and Keion White at defensive end during Sunday's win versus the Cardinals and likely will continue to lean on the duo until Bosa is able to return to action.

injuries.name: Eddy Pineiro
injuries.headline: Pineiro connected on a 57-yard field-goal try and went three-of-five on extra-point attempts in Sunday's 36-30 win over the Cardinals.
injuries.notes: Pineiro had not missed an extra point in 2026 coming into Sunday. He has nonetheless made 11 through three contests, so he's getting regular scoring opportunities in the 49ers' high-powered offense.

injuries.name: Deebo Samuel Sr.
injuries.headline: Samuel turned two carries into 14 yards and scored an 80-yard touchdown during Sunday's 36-30 win over Arizona.
injuries.notes: Samuel started off his day with a bang, receiving a lateral from fellow wideout Mike Evans during a hook-and-ladder play by San Francisco in the first quarter, taking off down the sideline for an 80-yard score. Samuel failed to catch a pass and didn't garner a target for the first time in three games this year, but he still found a way to make the most of limited opportunities. Evans suffered a rib/oblique injury in the second quarter of the victory, and if he's sidelined moving forward, Samuel will stand to operate as the team's No. 1 option at wide receiver.

injuries.name: George Kittle
injuries.headline: Kittle brought in six of seven targets for 82 yards and two touchdowns in the 49ers' 36-30 win over the Cardinals on Sunday.
injuries.notes: Kittle led the 49ers in receptions, receiving yards and targets on the afternoon, marking what may have been his return to both full health and a full workload following last January's Achilles tear. The veteran tight end struck from 10 and 20 yards out for his pair of fourth-quarter scoring grabs, his first multi-TD tally since Week 11 of last season. Kittle now has hit or exceeded the 80-yard mark in consecutive games, and he should remain heavily involved in a Week 4 home matchup against a Broncos defense that tends to funnel passing toward the middle of the field due to its outstanding cornerback play.

injuries.name: Brock Purdy
injuries.headline: Purdy completed 15 of 27 passes for 297 yards with four touchdowns and no interceptions and rushed twice for 34 yards in the 49ers' 36-30 win over the Cardinals on Sunday.
injuries.notes: Purdy's completion percentage was below his usual standards, but the fifth-year signal-caller more than made up for it with some effective downfield passing and his quartet of scoring tosses. His yardage total also got a boost from an 80-yard hook-and-lateral play in the first quarter between Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel that the latter took all the way to the house from San Francisco's 20-yard line, which served as the quarterback's first touchdown pass of the day. Purdy would go on to connect with Evans (23 yards) and George Kittle (10 and 20 yards) for his other three scoring tosses, with the final one of those coming two plays after a holding penalty on the talented tight end nullified a winding 45-yard touchdown run by the athletic quarterback. Purdy now boasts a 9:1 TD:INT and 789 passing yards over his first three games heading into a tough Week 4 home showdown against the Broncos next Sunday.

injuries.name: Christian McCaffrey
injuries.headline: McCaffrey rushed 15 times for 75 yards and a touchdown while bringing in four of five targets for 41 yards in the 49ers' 36-30 win over the Cardinals on Sunday.
injuries.notes: McCaffrey's carry total was modest by his standards, but he still outpaced backup Kaelon Black by 11 rushes and four targets while also recording a one-yard touchdown run early in the third quarter. McCaffrey was highly efficient with his rushing opportunities, and he finished second in receptions and third in targets for the 49ers on the afternoon. San Francisco's pass-catching corps suffered further attrition this weekend -- Mike Evans exited the game with a rib/oblique injury, while Demarcus Robinson (ankle) was placed on injured reserve Saturday -- so McCaffrey could continue to see his receiving work creep up in a Week 4 home showdown against the Broncos next Sunday.

injuries.name: Trent Williams
injuries.headline: Williams (neck) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Cardinals, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
injuries.notes: Williams was carted off the field and into the locker room during the third quarter, so he figures to be closer toward the doubtful side of returning to Sunday's contest. Vederian Lowe figures to take over at left tackle in Williams' absence.

injuries.name: Jack Jones
injuries.headline: Jones (foot) is active for Sunday's game against the Cardinals, Brooke Evans of the 49ers' official site reports.
injuries.notes: Jones sustained a foot injury in the 49ers' Week 2 win over the Dolphins, but the fifth-year pro has been cleared to play in Sunday's NFC West showdown. He's logged three pass defenses and zero tackles through the first two games of the regular season while serving in a rotational role in the secondary.

injuries.name: Zach Charbonnet
injuries.headline: Charbonnet (knee) was designated to return to practice Thursday.
injuries.notes: Thursday's move opens the 21-day window for Charbonnet to resume practicing, during which he can be added to the active roster. Charbonnet is ineligible to play against the Chargers on Sunday after being placed on the reserve/PUP list to begin the season, but he could suit up as soon as Week 5 against the 49ers if added to the roster. Jadarian Price (chest), Emanuel Wilson and George Holani (ribs) have held the fort at running back while Charbonnet works his way back from a torn ACL sustained last postseason.

injuries.name: Ty Okada
injuries.headline: Okada (hamstring) didn't participate in Seattle's practice Wednesday, John Boyle of the team's official site reports.
injuries.notes: Okada has yet to practice since the regular season got underway as he continues to nurse a hamstring injury. The 26-year-old is in danger of missing a fourth consecutive game, and AJ Finley would likely notch another start at safety if Okada is unable to play in Sunday's matchup against the Chargers.

injuries.name: Julian Love
injuries.headline: Love (calf) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice, John Boyle of the team's official site reports.
injuries.notes: Love managed to return to practice, albeit in a limited capacity, after sitting out the Week 3 loss to the Commanders due to a calf injury. If the 2019 fourth-round pick manages to practice either Thursday or Friday as well, he should have a good chance of suiting up for Sunday's matchup versus the Chargers.

injuries.name: Grey Zabel
injuries.headline: questionable
injuries.notes: questionable

injuries.name: Jarran Reed
injuries.headline: questionable
injuries.notes: questionable

injuries.name: George Holani
injuries.headline: Holani (ribs) was a limited participant at the Seahawks' practice Wednesday, John Boyle of the team's official site reports.
injuries.notes: Holani rushed three times for 10 yards while catching all five of his targets for 48 yards during the team's 33-31 loss to the Commanders in Week 3. He appears to have picked up injury to his ribs along the way, and the running back was unable to log a full session Wednesday as a result. Fellow running back Jadarian Price (chest) was also a limited participant to open the week, leaving Emanuel Wilson as the team's only fully healthy option in the backfield ahead of Thursday's practice.

injuries.name: Jadarian Price
injuries.headline: Price was limited in practice Wednesday due to a chest injury, Bob Condotta of The Seattle Times reports.
injuries.notes: Price logged career lows in snap share (28 percent) and touches (six) during this past Sunday's loss at Washington, accounting for just 22 yards from scrimmage. Perhaps the current health concern is partly to blame, but fellow RB Emanuel Wilson earned nine touches (all rushes) in Week 3, while George Holani (rib, LP on Wednesday) handled eight touches. Considering Holani now is banged up as well, Wilson may be the safest best among the trio to produce on game days.
